I'm a huge rust fan. I started in the wee early stages of Alpha when the game had quite a heavy load of bugs.  If you're someone who is giving the store page a quick look and you have no clue whether or not to buy this game, I'll give you a few reason why NOT to buy this game.  And i'm not picking at the game here, legacy was quite enjoyable, but if you're coming here thinking that you're going to buy a game to enjoy, then turn away quickly. If you're someone who is willing to wait for the Alpha stages to work these bugs out just so you can play the game, then by all means get the game and sit behind a loading screen and wait because you'll be doing a lot of it. In a list below, i'll be trying to make a quick and easy way to explain to you why this game simply just doesn't work.
1. This game is not compatible with Windows 10. If you are of the lucky few that get this game and are able to play it on Windows 10 without any issues, bless the gods around you 'cause everyone else is failing at the moment.
2. Memory leaks.  Even if you somehow figure out a way by going on the forums and getting through the long loading screens, you'll most likely crash and figure out that you cannot play the game without turning your setting to the lowest settings possible. Get used to slick textures and pixelated materials.
3. Rust doesn't like win32 users.  For all of those who use 32bit Windows, I feel for you. Even though you should probably upgrade your rig, you shouldn't have to for a game like this. I've played much more developed games than Rust and still had some FPS to spare even in the most crowded of areas.
4. The game is still in Alpha. You just have to remind yourself that even though there are a bagillion bugs, this game is still in Alpha. How? I don't know this game has been out on the market for like forever. But they still are developing the game so even if you do complain about how horrible it is to load or play the game, give it some credit, the devs are doing the best of their abilities.
I gave this review a 'thumbs down' only because I don't want people to get their hopes up and not being able to play the game. Go read the forums, there are countless amounts of people refunding their copies because they simply cannot play it.  Yes, they could of done some better research, but if you're someone excited about playing games, you just gotta have it.

Undertale is incredibly unique amongst the slews of shooters and RPGs that have become so prevalent these days. It doesn't have breathtaking graphics or incredible gameplay, but it doesn't need it. It doesn't even necessarily have the strongest story. But it has an incredible cast of characters, an intricate way of handling the player's morality and choices, and above all else, it makes you think about what you're doing and feel for the characters around you. Wacky hijinks and clever wit aside, Undertale has a way of making the player feel like both a wonderful and horrible person, sometimes simultaneously. (Sure, everyone knows that killing things isn't the right way to go in Undertale, and you can remove wonderful from the previous descriptor if you run around mass-murdering, but this isn't the place to discuss the specifics of that particular path, chilling as it is.) It really brings you to task for the things that you normally do in games - not the character you play, but you, the player controlling the character. Suffice to say that not everything in Undertale is wiped away and forgotten by reloading a past save. I can't say very much without spoilers, but there's a reason its fans are so passionate about and defensive of its characters - just how attached they can become after a few hours of sprites and text, bringing them to life without fancy graphics or long infodumps detailing their backstories. Undertale pulls through on wit, introspection, and ability to move the player, and its experience is in no way lessened by its lack of more prevalent modern gaming elements.
(Okay, and the soundtrack. It has an awesome soundtrack.)
The amount of detail put into the writing is amazing - for example, the game has accounted for pretty much every weird, contrived thing the character can do with the world, and characters will react accordingly. There are also plenty of hidden secrets, right down to datamining, for those who are into those sorts of mysteries.
My only complaint with Undertale is that it has no replay value. Or negative replay value. Because it actively makes me feel like a♥♥♥♥♥♥if I try to replay the game. Like I said, it's effective.

This game is an emotional rollercoaster (in a good way). This game made me feel almost every emotion that I could feel. It also carried some of those emotions into real life. This game gave me determination (pun intended) to look for the good in the world and to work hard so that some day I could eventually make a difference. Alright back to the actual game aspect of the game. It's a turn based RPG with 2 options of dealing with enemies, either sparing them or killing them. Sparing is when you do all sorts of actions like talking or petting your enemies until you can spare them. While if you decide to kill them, you have to a little time minigame (it's hard to describe). What about the characters? They are fantastic. Even though then their voices qualify as a bunch of beepish sounds, you can still feel the emotion of the characters via their dialog. What about the music? It's the best I heard in a while only being rivaled by the Hotline Miami series. All of the music tells you the emotions of the situation at hand and all of it is placed at where it needs to be. What about the graphics? The graphics are in an retro 8-bit style with many vibrant colors. While some may be turned of the game because of the asthetics, overall to most gamers the visuals will be appealing. What about the story? Well the story is probably the best aspect of the game. It's seemingly querky yet serious without having things get all messy. When I say it's querky I mean that they are lot of jokes and puns in the game that always got a laugh out of me. There are many comedic bits aimed for both adults and other more innocent people. Also warning this game can get really tragic and really heart-warming. All right so thats the gist of the game, great gameplay, great music, and great visuals, an excellent story. This is an obvious reccommendation from me and personally this is one of if not the best game I have ever played. Also what do you call a lone skeleton... Bonely (Ha Ha).

I just don't get it. I didn't grow up with Earthbound, and I got my fill of player-choice-consequences with the original Deus Ex, so the retro vibe didn't thrill me, and the idea of sparing your enemies felt way behind the times.
The writing was often lovely, the soundtrack was solid, and I can totally see how one could get sucked into the rabbit hole of repeat playthroughs and mucking about with save files. I've spent hundreds of hours doing the same on Dark Souls because the lore was so deep and hard to access.
But the Underground isn't Lordran. I just didn't want to explore it again. For every charming monster there was a half-baked meta-joke or a nonsequiter that pulled me out. The world varied so wildly between saccharine, self-aware, genuinely funny, and tragic that I couldn't latch on to any one part of it. So many filler areas, so many empty hallways and one-off characters. The final boss was excruciatingly hard, and too many of the sequences wore out their welcome almost instantly (the Papyrus/traps/puzzle section just DRAGGED. ON. FOREVER.) And while I understand Alphys's appeal to a broad swath of anime fans, all I could think during Hotland was 'PLEASE JUST SHUT THE ♥♥♥♥ UP. WHERE'S YOUR GODDAMN SELF-RESPECT?'
I will say that Temmie Village is a stroke of pure, demented genius. Goddamn I loved that place.
But overall, no. I didn't enjoy playing this game. I understand why many do, but I can't bring myself to recommend it.

To be honest, I do not believe Undertale to be nearly as good as many people seem to think.
The story seems to believe itself more complex or unique than it actually is, the gameplay outside of boss fights are annoyingly easy, the inventory screen only a formality, the game most of the time tells you how you should feel, the writting outside for the core characters is weak, and despite being labeled an RPG it misses many core things that actually make an RPG - supposedly as a result of Toby Foxes' underlying criticism and deconstruction of the medium of videogames and genres, but nonetheless leaving the game shallower by excluding core mechanics just to hit you with yet another contrived plot device and meta.
Undertale isn't really unique. It borrows and outright lifts a lot of its ideas and designs from other places, coating them in an obsession with Doge memes, image-board culture, and intentionally bad puns. What Undertale does, games such as Yume Nikki and Cave story did years before it, if not arguably better in many ways.
Similarly, it boggles my god damn mind  the ways in which people hail the game as the second coming of video game Jesus.
I enjoyed my time with it enough to do all three possible endings, and I believe I got my moneys worth despite not believing it to be "TEN OUT OF TEN, THE CITIZEN KANE OF VIDEOGAMES" , if only because of the fun characters, occasionally fantastic bullet hell mechanics tailored to each individual boss fight, a game world that remembers your actions, and memorable soundtrack.
Undertale isn't an amazing game, but it is a good one.

Graphics: 9/10 [Toby, Temmie, and the rest of the crew made fantastic creatures, NPC's, and landscapes. The scenery is especially gorgeous in some scenes. If you like pixel art, this is for you.]
Music: 11/10 [The soundtrack is phenomenal. Do yourself a favor and buy it too.]
Dialogue and Story: 10/10 [This game made me laugh and cry along with the plights of this fictional world. I felt things for these well designed characters like they were dear friends I've known all of my life and I don't think I'll be forgetting this any time soon.]
Gameplay: 10/10 [Seems to take a lot from Japanese bullet hell games, which are pretty cool. Also the mechanics make the game what it is.]
Undertale. When I first heard about it, I didn't buy all of the hype. I figured people were going mad over it because it was something different and you can play by NOT killing things and etc. But was I wrong. People like this game because of the memorable characters, the witty dialogue, the beautiful level designs, the heart-wrenching story, the phenomenal soundtrack, and the fact that you can play by NOT killing things. Even after watching a Youtuber play through the game, I still got it myself and accomplished the same ending. It's a totally different feeling. Even if you've seen this game played, I recommend you pick it up for yourself. It feels so much more personal when it's you controlling it, with the fate of the fictional world in your hands.
Should you buy this game? Yes. 100% yes.
Bottom Line: Undertale is one of my favorite RPG's to exist. It isn't the most visually appealing, it's gameplay isn't ground breaking, but it's story, loveable characters, and special mechanics make it to where this game will always have a place in my heart. 10/10

Borderlands 2 took everything they did right from Borderlands and made it even better. From game options to gameplay, everything has been tweaked to satisfy a greater audience and they did it without dumbing down much of what made Borderlands so great.
With the three DLC's that have been released so far, you will have a lot more variation in scenery and gameplay if you get bored of the main story line. Pirate Butts is a medium length story but the end missions will usually pay off with some amazing loot. Some people complain about reskinned enemies but there's plenty of new things that keep it visually interesting. The new weapons are definitely unique, some of them are considered "cursed" which can give them amazing bonuses but they will have a drawback that can be just as devestating to you as the bonuses are to the enemies.
The Torgue DLC is filled with the great comedy that made Borderlands so memorable and the final raid boss is amazingly fun to fight unlike Gee in Pirate Butts. Seraph items have actually become useful in this one: For grenades, the O-Negative, Crossfire and the Meteor Shower are simply amazing and replace some of the legendary gear for sheer mass destruction. The Hoplite is the seraph equivalent of the Fabled Tortoise with less of a speed impact, so technically it's even better and should be used over the FT. Oh yeah, EXPLOSIONS!
Sir Hammerlock's Big Game Hunt is a rather short DLC but it takes you to a very different part of Pandora. Instead of wastelanads you visit an underground oasis for rare and unusual (for Pandora) animals. While the main plot isn't too long, there's plenty of side missions to keep yourself busy with. The seraph dealer has found some amazing weaponry this time like the new Interfacer which is now the absolute strongest shotgun in the game and The Hawkeye sniper rifle. The Hawkeye may be weak for body shots, it has one of the highest crit bonuses for any sniper and has great accuracy. The vast manjority of enemies are new and there's a returning enemy from Borderlands which may or may not make some people rage. Along with the missions you will get a new vehicle, new heads and new skins to customize your character and a terribly designed raid boss with unavaoidable shock novas.
Borderlands 2 is worth picking up if you're a fan of the original game and it's often silly humor. Just be warmed, you may lose track of time very easily so don't play this before work. :P

Rust is a sophisticated survival game based around human nature. In this game, you will experience the many varities of life, including: Aggressive, vulgar twelve year olds; aggressive, vulgar teenagers, as well as the occasional empathetic individual who may or may not just want to kill you.
Join together with your human kin and challenge the grand maze known as life. Kill each other out of fear and spite; steal the common man's belongings and make him suffer - because in the end, he'll probably kill you anyway.
"Enter, 'Crafting.'"
In Rust, you are a remarkable craftsman and engineer, able to construct automated defense turrets, code locks, armored walls, and even assault rilfes from the most basic of resources; not to mention the fact that you can do so in a mere day.
But before you can do that, you must extract magical fragments of blue paper from mysterious metal barrels, said to be left behind by the gods. These blue fragments grant fantastical knowledge, essential to your survival.
"The wildlife and You."
The various animals that inhabit Rust hold a formidable power to bend space to their will.
Should you anger a predator, you may find that it can scale intimidating heights in a matter of seconds.
This is a power that all animals possess which is said to be granted by the gods themselves; but worry not, for they aren't the only ones with godly power, as you - the player - can bend TIME and MATTER to your will.
As previously spoken of, the player is able to construct a multitude of creations; in addition to that, however, you can carry impossible amounts of weight; yes, an entire BUILDING'S amount of weight in ADDITION to the volume that it would take up.
"What does this all mean?"
I believe it is quite simple, what this all means: I believe us humans are in fact demigods.
I believe that the gods who made our world, granted us a portion of their strength and knowledge so that we may carry ourselves through life, and become gods as well. As a demigod myself, I have seen others transcend their presumed limits and build godly cities of metal. I believe the gods test us with their power and see what we can achieve.
That would be why they send birds of flame and death towards us: to test us. It would also explain why they give us gifts from above.
So, in conclusion, Rust is test of our power and humanity, so that we may one day become gods.

I don’t want to spoil the game, so I’ll leave significant details out, but this deceptively simple looking game surprised me with its complexity and depth. The thought that went into each character, into each possibility, each action, is staggering. Not to mention the soundtrack is one of the best I have heard in recent years.
Though by no means as rabid a fan as many online seem to be, I love this game. I had a real emotional response to the characters. I wanted to see my favorites happy, and didn’t want them hurt. I wanted more, and that drove me to try and see if there was more to be had. Depending on your choices and actions in the game, the results will change. Monsters will react differently, items will be avaialble or not exist, and your ending will depend on how you handled each encounter.
Make friends or don't. Negotiate or fight. Explore or b-line for the ending, Undertale lets you play your own way and doesn't force you to experience it like everyone else. There was a recent patch that dealt with glitches (which I never encountered), but also opened up more possibilities for those who need to fill in the lore gaps without messing with the game code.
I played Undertale twice, and as much as I want to experience the game again, I can’t replay it without undoing all the things I had accomplished. I’d have to reset all the characters, undo any good I had done in the realm of monsters, where I, a fallen human, must pass through in search of a way out.
Undertale is so good I may never play it again. It may not make sense until you try it yourself, but there it is. How many games can say that?

I don’t want to spoil the game, so I’ll leave significant details out, but this deceptively simple looking game surprised me with its complexity and depth. The thought that went into each character, into each possibility, each action, is staggering. Not to mention the soundtrack is one of the best I have heard in recent years.
Though by no means as rabid a fan as many online seem to be, I love this game. I had a real emotional response to the characters. I wanted to see my favorites happy, and didn’t want them hurt. I wanted more, and that drove me to try and see if there was more to be had. Depending on your choices and actions in the game, the results will change. Monsters will react differently, items will be avaialble or not exist, and your ending will depend on how you handled each encounter.
Make friends or don't. Negotiate or fight. Explore or b-line for the ending, Undertale lets you play your own way and doesn't force you to experience it like everyone else. There was a recent patch that dealt with glitches (which I never encountered), but also opened up more possibilities for those who need to fill in the lore gaps without messing with the game code.
I played Undertale twice, and as much as I want to experience the game again, I can’t replay it without undoing all the things I had accomplished. I’d have to reset all the characters, undo any good I had done in the realm of monsters, where I, a fallen human, must pass through in search of a way out.
Undertale is so good I may never play it again. It may not make sense until you try it yourself, but there it is. How many games can say that?

I can't even begin to say how much I enjoy this game!
The  general story is pretty much pieced together in the end, but there is still a lot going on and so many secrets I have yet to discover or find. I do love the story/writing, it makes me curious and I love being curious! I was also feeling sadness, frustration(but that was just me being bad at the game), and even fear.  it was just an over stimulation of the emotions.
The gameplay was different, maybe I just never run into a dodging-type game like this, but I thought it was different from the usual rpg where every attack is based on luck and numbers. This one is more based on skill, memory, patience, and literal determination. I'm not kidding, this is the first time I actually felt ready get back in there and try again just from a game over screen (although I've had moments where I took a break just to cool down).
The art style is simply sublime. I was in awe just from all the detail and character design. Oh my goodness don't get me started on character design, I'm big on character designs, so I could go on for a while about how cool/cute/interesting they look! *sigh* yes... even Jerry.
So I say at least give this game a try before you put it down for looking "retro" or "old". Honestly it does look retro but the story and text are very refreshing. giving it a new, crisp feel!
If you've tried it and still don't like it, thats cool. I won't judge you, we all don't like the same things. Thats what makes us different from one another.

I don’t want to spoil the game, so I’ll leave significant details out, but this deceptively simple looking game surprised me with its complexity and depth. The thought that went into each character, into each possibility, each action, is staggering. Not to mention the soundtrack is one of the best I have heard in recent years.
Though by no means as rabid a fan as many online seem to be, I love this game. I had a real emotional response to the characters. I wanted to see my favorites happy, and didn’t want them hurt. I wanted more, and that drove me to try and see if there was more to be had. Depending on your choices and actions in the game, the results will change. Monsters will react differently, items will be avaialble or not exist, and your ending will depend on how you handled each encounter.
Make friends or don't. Negotiate or fight. Explore or b-line for the ending, Undertale lets you play your own way and doesn't force you to experience it like everyone else. There was a recent patch that dealt with glitches (which I never encountered), but also opened up more possibilities for those who need to fill in the lore gaps without messing with the game code.
I played Undertale twice, and as much as I want to experience the game again, I can’t replay it without undoing all the things I had accomplished. I’d have to reset all the characters, undo any good I had done in the realm of monsters, where I, a fallen human, must pass through in search of a way out.
Undertale is so good I may never play it again. It may not make sense until you try it yourself, but there it is. How many games can say that?

- Secondly It has a extremely high amount of pvp, it should have some servers where pvp is limited (so it could expand its playerbase by diversifying its target audience.

Borderlands 2 is a very well done loot finding Fps, however if that  isn't your thing I don't recommend it.
The visuals are very top notch and the animations are solid. The voice acting is top notch and the music adds a good amount of atmosphere.  The gameplay feels more refined than the first by that I mean they added a mini map, more customization, etc. The shooting works well for what it is, but I think they could make it more satisfying. Honestly what makes borderlands a rewarding game is finding a new weapon or leveling up more. The feeling you get when come across a new gun and using is such a great feeling in a game.
Now in terms of what I dislike with the game, well the biggest one is the humor. It's really forced and it's just a bunch of internet memes, since that's what the writer considers "humor".  Now I do appreciate that the game attempted to put in a narrative, and while the humor falls flat the actual writing is good mostly and the characters are well done. In terms of other issues well sometimes borderlands can feel a bit samey in places.
That being said the positives out weigh the bad, though it's not everyone it's a solid title.

I can't even begin to say how much I enjoy this game!
The  general story is pretty much pieced together in the end, but there is still a lot going on and so many secrets I have yet to discover or find. I do love the story/writing, it makes me curious and I love being curious! I was also feeling sadness, frustration(but that was just me being bad at the game), and even fear.  it was just an over stimulation of the emotions.
The gameplay was different, maybe I just never run into a dodging-type game like this, but I thought it was different from the usual rpg where every attack is based on luck and numbers. This one is more based on skill, memory, patience, and literal determination. I'm not kidding, this is the first time I actually felt ready get back in there and try again just from a game over screen (although I've had moments where I took a break just to cool down).
The art style is simply sublime. I was in awe just from all the detail and character design. Oh my goodness don't get me started on character design, I'm big on character designs, so I could go on for a while about how cool/cute/interesting they look! *sigh* yes... even Jerry.
So I say at least give this game a try before you put it down for looking "retro" or "old". Honestly it does look retro but the story and text are very refreshing. giving it a new, crisp feel!
If you've tried it and still don't like it, thats cool. I won't judge you, we all don't like the same things. Thats what makes us different from one another.

-About 3 main endings, each one with different fights and dialogue.

If any of that interests you, try the demo from the main website. Don't trust the hype, because this game isn't for everyone.

Envitonments were glitchy with clipping errors, etc. When you did get a multiplayer game going it was rife with looters, trolls and hacked gear.
Well...Borderlands 2 fixed all that. Almost every complaint I had about BL1 was addressed in BL2 and then some. Steam friends are easy to find and join. Co-op is awesome with a great new matchmaking system, including quickmatch. Great new cast of characters, endlessly entertaining NPC dialog (love Scooter, Ellie, Tiny Tina, and of course Handsome Jack) and the ever expanding landscape that is Borderlands [1&2] continues to amaze. Weapons are fun to collect and even more fun to use. Homing grenades, elemental weapons, shields that absorb bullets and add them to your inventory, new vehicles, new skills, and on and on. The depth and breadth of this game is only superceded by the polish that Gearbox has lavished on this epic quest.
There are some small niggles but Gearbox continually provide updates and balance to the game. They have released 3 of their 4 season pass DLCs on schedule and have not disappointed. This year, I'm spending a lot more time in the Borderlands.
Highly recommend the season pass. Worth every dollar.

Borderlands 2 improves upon the first game but misses the mark in several big areas.
For those adverse to this essay the summery is as follows: The guns/shields are bad and need to be seriously reworked and balanced. Badass rank is like a second job to get anywhere. Grenades are amazingly fun. Charecter building and customization is also fun. Late game is a chore to play & is MMO level grindy to get various unique guns. Ammo system sucks should be partially removed. DLC is dodgy & might make playing without it impossible as 51+ level guns will drop for level 50 characters.
The badass point system only works if you have ground out multiple characters to rank 50 and bothered to do some of the whackier bits. Even then the inability to build to your playstyle and shoehorned into get X stat to 5% now get all others to 5% before it can be buffed again. Weapons have some serious itemization inssues which is a huge problem.
Many guns feel inferior or have wonky behvaiors. E-tech rifles deform reflex sight scopes making them headache inducing. Dahl weapons only burst in ironsight and unless unique always a 3 round burst. Making sniper rifles waste ammo and Etech guns waste 2 shots 90 degrees from center. Hyperion reverse recoil is fun but shake the screen the first few shots in a way that gives me a headache and no amount of headbob in a game makes me sick. Jacobs and Torque and to a lesser extent maliwan the only really solid manufactuers whose gimmicks make them fun to use. The other feel almost handicapped. Especially Dahl, could they not get 2x 3x 4x 5x bursts randomly, or burst from the hip? A 2x Dahl sniper would be fun where the inaccuare ammo wasting 3x ones are garbage time. I loved burst rifles and pistols in BL1 & was sad to see them done like this.
The previous games ammo regen builds are missing forcing a constant game of feeding fast firing lower damage and/or accuracy weapons over never bothering with higher damage slow ones. If one thing is totally wrong with Borderlands its ammo. Just make rockets and grenades take ammo. Leave the fire rate vs accuracy vs damage juggling be free of a poorly done mmo goldsink and let us never stop shooting. Honestly the raid fights feel like they were meant for that.
Grenades however are amazing and a vast imrpovment over the last game I really cannot overstate how fun grenade mod combos can be. A stuff like a homing grenade that sticks to a target that pulls everything into a singularity before covering it in acid, fantastic stuff.
Level 50 content is difficult to the point of 3-4 shots knocking a legendary equipped character down. The enemies however turn into BL1 style badass bullet sinks even if not badass. Some of the actual badass enemies can survive upwards of 30 seconds of point blank overpowered attacks such as dual infinite ammo pistols on a pistol build gunzerker that fires at somewhere over 1200rpm. Everything is now a HP bullet sink & unfun to fight in many areas forcing you into extreme play styles.
The raid boss fights are not my cup of tea and the serpraph crystal guns look very unfun and akin to Magic the Gatherings junk Rares. Most are the perfect form of the flawed guns in the game. Inaccurace, slow projectile speeds and Extreme gimmick like an assault rifle that arcs like a garden hose.
Character builds are really fun and bring out a lot of combos without feeling cookie cutter or otherwise stale. Lots of fun can be had mixing and matching from various tree and trying out how the guns (even with the problems I mentioned) work with them.
The DLC grind aspect kind of irks me but the first 2 were really fun. The Hammerlock one was hugely dissapointing. Totally phoned in and the Fallout 3 green overlay is actually sickening. Enemies are even bigger hitpoint sinks and it felt hollow. There is going to be a second season as well. I suspect it will end up like BL1 where they up the level cap of the weapons even if you do not have the DLC. Causing your level 50 non DLC characters to find level 51+ weapons you cannot use till you buy the DLC to up the cap.
Adendum: After the first wave of DLC this game is dead and has no soul. The fanbase is vitrolic and defensive. We hit level 51 playing the DLC and are still using the same guns we got when we beat hard mode. Nothing good drops. Everything is garbage and all is lost.
Well worth playing if you like open world and lot's of missions.

This game is intended to have three main endings. I have no qualms with either of the two that are considered the "good" endings. However, the route to achieving the third ending is awful, and the reason why i wouldn't ever recommend this game to another person, especially one who wants to get the most out of a game they purchase. The things i would normally list as positives for the game, which are things like a fantastic soundtrack, solid writing, good humor, and a charming cast, are entirely absent from nearly a third of the game.
In a poor attempt to make you feel bad about yourself and your actions, the game deliberately makes itself less fun to play in order to achieve the "bad" ending. First, all of the wonderful music tracks from the rest of the game is replaced with deliberately off beat and slow music. Would you enjoy watching your favorite movie if the entire score was replaced with dull, uninspired music? Of course not, and the same line of thought applies here, the music doesn't fit and hardly leaves an impression when playing the game this way. (As support for this, none of the overworld tracks from the "bad ending" playthrough are on the official soundtrack, because they simply aren't enjoyable to listen to.)
Second, the game's main story sequences are all altered and cut short when the game takes control out of the hands of the player in order to interrupt things. The cast is given far less screen time, and most of what remains is spent with out of character dialogue in an attempt to tell the player what they are doing is morally wrong. There is no actual plot progression in this story. All of the characters from the other two routes are shoe-horned in. This includes the bosses, of which all but one is reduced to a few lines of dialogue spent rehashing the idea that "the player is evil." Ultimately the player doesn't feel evil as a result of this, but rather they're just bored when nothing exciting happens.
To achieve this ending you are required to exhaust every area of random encounters. Most people would list "grinding" (or the repeated killing of enemy units in one area in order to power up your character(s).) as one of their least favorite things about Role-Playing games. In most games, this is optional and the player can still beat the game and see all of the content without having to spend potential hours fishing for encounters. Undertale instead decides to force the player to grind in EVERY area, and if you choose not to, you cannot achieve this ending. Now normally, enemy encounters in undertale are entertaining and well designed. Unfortunately in this route the player is forced to spend every encounter using only the most boring method, the standard attack. The player is kept from seeing all of the unique interactions with every enemy type that make this game so charming in the other routes.
Lastly, many players will praise this route through the game due to the boss fights you'll encounter along the way. Contrary to the other routes, this path includes only two actual boss fights, with the rest being replaced by stereotypical dialogue repeating the trope that "humans are the real monsters" and that you are evil. The two boss fights that remain are unique, but they are flawed, and certainly not worth taking this path for. ***Spoiler warning*** i am going to discuss these two fights in great detail now, if you wish to avoid spoilers skip to my closing paragraph.
The first of the two fights is against the character Undyne. In the other two paths Undyne is an overly zealous royal guard oozing with character. However, in this run her entire character is changed to instead be portrayed as a serious heroine who has no time for messing around. This is an interesting change, but it makes her less enjoyable as a character by turning her into a simple trope. The fight against Undyne in the other two paths includes an amazing music track titled "Spear of Justice" it is upbeat, intense, and incites the player to feel excited and determined to win. The music in this fight however, is somber and slow. It is impossible to feel anything close to happy while the music is playing, and it contrasts with what is supposed to be an intense battle.
While it is an intense battle, it is intense for the wrong reasons. The original fight against Undyne introduced a new game mechanic and encouraged the player to learn its nuances and patterns, while incrementally increasing the difficulty. This fight however is designed around tricking the player. The ONLY way a player can achieve success the first time trying this fight is through luck. Each of the patterns is designed to mess you up by doing the opposite of what is expected, or switching the rules. This fight also has multiple attacks that are entirely random, meaning that no matter how well the patterns are memorized, there will always be unforeseen variances. Once the fight is completed Undyne warns the player of preparations being made to stop them from progressing, This would be a nice prelude of things to come, however almost none of the things she points out are ever witnessed by the player, further emphasizing how little plot or content there is in this route.
The second boss that people praise this game for is the final fight in this route, the fight against Sans. This fight is deemed by many to be the most challenging in the game. While this statement is true, it is not as enjoyable as many would make it seem. The music track for this fight is actually well done, unlike the one for the previous fight, and actually conveys a good bit of emotion and sets the stage for an epic fight. Sans takes a page from his brothers handbook and his attacks are almost all based around platforming. These segments are well done and actually rely on player skill. However, there are aspects to this fight that are blatantly unfair and meant to simply annoy the player. Attacks begin to appear while the player is choosing their actions and can even harm them while they search for a healing item.
The entire time you battle sans he spouts out lazy exposition to the player. Prior to this fight Sans has had no deeper significance in the story, other than being a silent protector or guardian for the player in the other routes, and being almost absent from this one entirely.  This fight goes far beyond that and suddenly personifies him as all-knowing, and all-powerful. This could have led to an interesting story, or been a fitting piece to a larger whole, but the game up until this point has not tried to tell a story of any significance. After this fight, the game moves on for only a short while before ending with a very deus ex machina reveal, that you the player have been the unwitting host of another character bent on destroying reality.
Story elements like these should've been developed properly, and had a lead-in with a logical story progression. Instead the game chooses to shoehorn in all of the relevant plot elements in a very short window. The message of this story is very transparent, and i have no issue with what it's attempting to do. It is designed to be a unique take on an RPG where the player's excessive violence has consequences on the world they are in, and make the player question their actions. The way this message is presented in-game however is quite poor. At every possible moment, rather than developing a plot or providing much-needed exposition for the player, the game decides to force this message down the player's throat. It repeats the idea that the player is a monster over and over again, with very little subtext.

Borderlands is one of the best game-series ever made in my opinion. You can play it for 200 hours and there will still be something you didn't find yet.
Gameplay:
First things first - You get further in the game by doing quests BUT every quest is kinda unique and I don't feel like doing the same thing all over again. (Except you are playing the game again and again. In this case you really do the same thing over and over again... but it's still fun!)
The best thing about this game is it's great sense of humor. It doesn't take it self very seriously even though you will recognize that there is a deeper story going on under all the jokes.
At some point it feels like an MMO mixed with a FPS and the detail and humorous story of an indi game. I don't see any way how this could go wrong! :D
Combat:
I've never had such a variety of weapons in a game before and with those different kinds of guns there comes a whole new feeling to all of the fights. You can start of by picking the obvious enemys with a sniper rifle and take the rest out with a shotgun that makes everything explode around you. And I'm not even talking about the legendary weapons yet. When it comes to combat everything is up to you. There is no "whaaat you want to use this weapon? sorry but you took that class so you can't use this!". Just take something that looks nice to you and tare the world apart!
Characters:
You will meet a lot of different characters through out the game and everyone is insane in a different way. You will even get background information about some people by doing quests or finding random stuff. The Characters are one of the biggest reasons why this game is so great!
Leveldesign:
The world could look a little boring when you look at it but it really isn't. There is so much going on and things are changing as you move forward in the story. You can find secrets and eastereggs all over the place but they are sometimes really hard to find. In general the world is split in different areas which you can explore so it's not fully openworld but it doesn't feel like you are forced to go a specific way. For me it solves the problem of wanting to explore the world and every little detail in it and fully losing track while doing that. You are free to look around but you still get to where you have to go.
Looting:
I think that's one of the biggest parts of this game. You will lose count of how many cases and lockers you've looted really soon but you will find new weapons and ammo in it so you should try to loot everything you see. The ammo runs out really quick on some weapons so keep an eye out for the green light which marks a lootable object.
Lategame:
You will finish the main story kinda quick (depending on how many sidequests you are doing and how much you are into exploring) and that will be around level 25-30. But it's not even close to being over at this point. You will just unlock the next stage of the game at this point which means that you start a "new" game but you keep all your levels and stuff, just the story resets and the enemies will now be on your level again. There are some quests which you can only do if you are level 50 or even higher so it's worth the extra time you are spending. And as i said earlier, you won't be bored since the combat is so much fun and you will develop even further, getting stronger weapons and all that nice stuff. And if you are level 50 in the end and everything is done, don't you worry mate, there is still a ton of DLCs and other playable characters to try out! Borderlands 2 may be released some years ago but it's not even close to beeing dead! There is still stuff released for it and it get's better the longer you play it.
Bad Stuff:
Of course there is something bad on every game, so these are my greatest problems in BL2.
- Sometimes when you kill an enemie and it drops loot or throw out something of your inventory the items will fall through the ground and be gone for ever. I lost quite a high amount of my legendary weapons this way. So always search a save spot for something like that or use the trade option.
- There are some quests which lead you right back into an area which you've already cleared and it's a bit painful to walk that way all over again especially since you have to do that twice for every character since you will have to replay everything to get a highlevel char.
- The pizza at Claptraps party is cold. (Insider xD)

Undertale. Where do I start? This game is AMAZING.
Let's start with the soundtrack.
The soundtrack in UNDERTALE is one of the best, most melodic soundtracks of any game Ive played. Each boss has his/her own theme. The soundtrack fits very well with certain parts of the game. Even if your facing a hard boss, You wont mind hearing the song over, and over again. The slight chiptune songs go very well with UNDERTALE's pixel look.
STORY:
The story in UNDERTALE is one of the most creative, well written, and touching stories Ive ever seen. While the intro to the game breifly explains the story to you, there is SO MUCH MORE Hidden parts of the story. The game leaves little clues to hidden peices of the story scattered throughout its 3 Endings. As you find out the TRUE story, The peices start to form together slowly, Leaving that little "Eurika!" Feeling inside of you.
CHARACTERS:
The characters in UNDERTALE are easily the most quirky, lovable, and cute characters in ANY game I've played. You get attached to the SO easily. The character design, both personality AND apperance, Are ON POINT.
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay in UNDERTALE is REALLY good.  From Its Unique
bullet-hell battle system that has NEVER been seen before in an RPG, To the greatly designed puzzles, This game will provide about 6 Full hours (That IS If you only choose to do ONE ending) of spot- on entertainment.
MISC.:
So I only have one thing here in the Misc. section, and that is the multiple times this game breaks the 4th wall. From closing itself, to changing the name of the window, This game breaks the 4th wall, and does it right.
So here you are. Should you buy this game? Yes.
EDIT: Well, the community has gotten pretty toxic sice I wrote this review. To anyone looking to buy this masterpeice: Do not let anybody tell you how to play the game. Try to keep spoilers at a bre minimum. A blind playthrough is the best playthrough.

This game is intended to have three main endings. I have no qualms with either of the two that are considered the "good" endings. However, the route to achieving the third ending is awful, and the reason why i wouldn't ever recommend this game to another person, especially one who wants to get the most out of a game they purchase. The things i would normally list as positives for the game, which are things like a fantastic soundtrack, solid writing, good humor, and a charming cast, are entirely absent from nearly a third of the game.
In a poor attempt to make you feel bad about yourself and your actions, the game deliberately makes itself less fun to play in order to achieve the "bad" ending. First, all of the wonderful music tracks from the rest of the game is replaced with deliberately off beat and slow music. Would you enjoy watching your favorite movie if the entire score was replaced with dull, uninspired music? Of course not, and the same line of thought applies here, the music doesn't fit and hardly leaves an impression when playing the game this way. (As support for this, none of the overworld tracks from the "bad ending" playthrough are on the official soundtrack, because they simply aren't enjoyable to listen to.)
Second, the game's main story sequences are all altered and cut short when the game takes control out of the hands of the player in order to interrupt things. The cast is given far less screen time, and most of what remains is spent with out of character dialogue in an attempt to tell the player what they are doing is morally wrong. There is no actual plot progression in this story. All of the characters from the other two routes are shoe-horned in. This includes the bosses, of which all but one is reduced to a few lines of dialogue spent rehashing the idea that "the player is evil." Ultimately the player doesn't feel evil as a result of this, but rather they're just bored when nothing exciting happens.
To achieve this ending you are required to exhaust every area of random encounters. Most people would list "grinding" (or the repeated killing of enemy units in one area in order to power up your character(s).) as one of their least favorite things about Role-Playing games. In most games, this is optional and the player can still beat the game and see all of the content without having to spend potential hours fishing for encounters. Undertale instead decides to force the player to grind in EVERY area, and if you choose not to, you cannot achieve this ending. Now normally, enemy encounters in undertale are entertaining and well designed. Unfortunately in this route the player is forced to spend every encounter using only the most boring method, the standard attack. The player is kept from seeing all of the unique interactions with every enemy type that make this game so charming in the other routes.
Lastly, many players will praise this route through the game due to the boss fights you'll encounter along the way. Contrary to the other routes, this path includes only two actual boss fights, with the rest being replaced by stereotypical dialogue repeating the trope that "humans are the real monsters" and that you are evil. The two boss fights that remain are unique, but they are flawed, and certainly not worth taking this path for. ***Spoiler warning*** i am going to discuss these two fights in great detail now, if you wish to avoid spoilers skip to my closing paragraph.
The first of the two fights is against the character Undyne. In the other two paths Undyne is an overly zealous royal guard oozing with character. However, in this run her entire character is changed to instead be portrayed as a serious heroine who has no time for messing around. This is an interesting change, but it makes her less enjoyable as a character by turning her into a simple trope. The fight against Undyne in the other two paths includes an amazing music track titled "Spear of Justice" it is upbeat, intense, and incites the player to feel excited and determined to win. The music in this fight however, is somber and slow. It is impossible to feel anything close to happy while the music is playing, and it contrasts with what is supposed to be an intense battle.
While it is an intense battle, it is intense for the wrong reasons. The original fight against Undyne introduced a new game mechanic and encouraged the player to learn its nuances and patterns, while incrementally increasing the difficulty. This fight however is designed around tricking the player. The ONLY way a player can achieve success the first time trying this fight is through luck. Each of the patterns is designed to mess you up by doing the opposite of what is expected, or switching the rules. This fight also has multiple attacks that are entirely random, meaning that no matter how well the patterns are memorized, there will always be unforeseen variances. Once the fight is completed Undyne warns the player of preparations being made to stop them from progressing, This would be a nice prelude of things to come, however almost none of the things she points out are ever witnessed by the player, further emphasizing how little plot or content there is in this route.
The second boss that people praise this game for is the final fight in this route, the fight against Sans. This fight is deemed by many to be the most challenging in the game. While this statement is true, it is not as enjoyable as many would make it seem. The music track for this fight is actually well done, unlike the one for the previous fight, and actually conveys a good bit of emotion and sets the stage for an epic fight. Sans takes a page from his brothers handbook and his attacks are almost all based around platforming. These segments are well done and actually rely on player skill. However, there are aspects to this fight that are blatantly unfair and meant to simply annoy the player. Attacks begin to appear while the player is choosing their actions and can even harm them while they search for a healing item.
The entire time you battle sans he spouts out lazy exposition to the player. Prior to this fight Sans has had no deeper significance in the story, other than being a silent protector or guardian for the player in the other routes, and being almost absent from this one entirely.  This fight goes far beyond that and suddenly personifies him as all-knowing, and all-powerful. This could have led to an interesting story, or been a fitting piece to a larger whole, but the game up until this point has not tried to tell a story of any significance. After this fight, the game moves on for only a short while before ending with a very deus ex machina reveal, that you the player have been the unwitting host of another character bent on destroying reality.
Story elements like these should've been developed properly, and had a lead-in with a logical story progression. Instead the game chooses to shoehorn in all of the relevant plot elements in a very short window. The message of this story is very transparent, and i have no issue with what it's attempting to do. It is designed to be a unique take on an RPG where the player's excessive violence has consequences on the world they are in, and make the player question their actions. The way this message is presented in-game however is quite poor. At every possible moment, rather than developing a plot or providing much-needed exposition for the player, the game decides to force this message down the player's throat. It repeats the idea that the player is a monster over and over again, with very little subtext.

Rust has huge potential but it needs to be found. A basic description of the game would be it is Mine/Survivial craft on steroids. Pretty graphics and resource mining/converting. It is also  a grinder in terms of repetative behaviours (mining, logging/smelting) which makes it doubley infuriatioing when one dies. There are many ways to die in the game and its pretty brutal. A couple of hits and you are down. Time and resources are lost for nothing.  You will initally die being food for random wandering wolves and bears. You will also be mercilessly hunted down by fellow humans after your loot or to eat you because they can. Each time you die, if you have not managed to construct a base with a bed you will wake up naked on the beach with a rock and will have to start again from scratch. The real terror ( in a real sense) comeas in human to human interactions. You are out gathering resources and hear footsteps (even worse, maybe a few footsteps) do you sit tight and not say a word or do you  try and engage? Sometimes people are in your base and you can hear them trying to break in and steal all you possess. Ive had good and bad experiences from chatting to people. In essence I woulod say you need friends in this game (maybe clan) it is a lonely grind playing alone. The maps are massive and the random nature of them is great. Ive not tried other mods yet but suspect there are many more good ideas that can be put into practice. All in all a good game that needs to steer away from grind.

Borderlands 2 improves upon the first game but misses the mark in several big areas.
For those adverse to this essay the summery is as follows: The guns/shields are bad and need to be seriously reworked and balanced. Badass rank is like a second job to get anywhere. Grenades are amazingly fun. Charecter building and customization is also fun. Late game is a chore to play & is MMO level grindy to get various unique guns. Ammo system sucks should be partially removed. DLC is dodgy & might make playing without it impossible as 51+ level guns will drop for level 50 characters.
The badass point system only works if you have ground out multiple characters to rank 50 and bothered to do some of the whackier bits. Even then the inability to build to your playstyle and shoehorned into get X stat to 5% now get all others to 5% before it can be buffed again. Weapons have some serious itemization inssues which is a huge problem.
Many guns feel inferior or have wonky behvaiors. E-tech rifles deform reflex sight scopes making them headache inducing. Dahl weapons only burst in ironsight and unless unique always a 3 round burst. Making sniper rifles waste ammo and Etech guns waste 2 shots 90 degrees from center. Hyperion reverse recoil is fun but shake the screen the first few shots in a way that gives me a headache and no amount of headbob in a game makes me sick. Jacobs and Torque and to a lesser extent maliwan the only really solid manufactuers whose gimmicks make them fun to use. The other feel almost handicapped. Especially Dahl, could they not get 2x 3x 4x 5x bursts randomly, or burst from the hip? A 2x Dahl sniper would be fun where the inaccuare ammo wasting 3x ones are garbage time. I loved burst rifles and pistols in BL1 & was sad to see them done like this.
The previous games ammo regen builds are missing forcing a constant game of feeding fast firing lower damage and/or accuracy weapons over never bothering with higher damage slow ones. If one thing is totally wrong with Borderlands its ammo. Just make rockets and grenades take ammo. Leave the fire rate vs accuracy vs damage juggling be free of a poorly done mmo goldsink and let us never stop shooting. Honestly the raid fights feel like they were meant for that.
Grenades however are amazing and a vast imrpovment over the last game I really cannot overstate how fun grenade mod combos can be. A stuff like a homing grenade that sticks to a target that pulls everything into a singularity before covering it in acid, fantastic stuff.
Level 50 content is difficult to the point of 3-4 shots knocking a legendary equipped character down. The enemies however turn into BL1 style badass bullet sinks even if not badass. Some of the actual badass enemies can survive upwards of 30 seconds of point blank overpowered attacks such as dual infinite ammo pistols on a pistol build gunzerker that fires at somewhere over 1200rpm. Everything is now a HP bullet sink & unfun to fight in many areas forcing you into extreme play styles.
The raid boss fights are not my cup of tea and the serpraph crystal guns look very unfun and akin to Magic the Gatherings junk Rares. Most are the perfect form of the flawed guns in the game. Inaccurace, slow projectile speeds and Extreme gimmick like an assault rifle that arcs like a garden hose.
Character builds are really fun and bring out a lot of combos without feeling cookie cutter or otherwise stale. Lots of fun can be had mixing and matching from various tree and trying out how the guns (even with the problems I mentioned) work with them.
The DLC grind aspect kind of irks me but the first 2 were really fun. The Hammerlock one was hugely dissapointing. Totally phoned in and the Fallout 3 green overlay is actually sickening. Enemies are even bigger hitpoint sinks and it felt hollow. There is going to be a second season as well. I suspect it will end up like BL1 where they up the level cap of the weapons even if you do not have the DLC. Causing your level 50 non DLC characters to find level 51+ weapons you cannot use till you buy the DLC to up the cap.
Adendum: After the first wave of DLC this game is dead and has no soul. The fanbase is vitrolic and defensive. We hit level 51 playing the DLC and are still using the same guns we got when we beat hard mode. Nothing good drops. Everything is garbage and all is lost.
Well worth playing if you like open world and lot's of missions.

It makes you question the ethics of playing a video game, if you didn't think that was possible, which I now realise, is possible. This briliantly made game has so much love and care put into it, you'd sware it was a Triple A release. But it isn't.
Now, if you want a good RPG, Undertale has got you covered. If you want an emotional rollercoaster of both good and bad feelings, Undertale has you covered. If you want some bullet-hell, Undertale still has you covered. And that is what is so great about it. The experience you have with Undertale is what YOU make it to be. Did you kill those charcters? Then the game will reflect that. Did you go save everyone in the game? Undertale will show you what happens. That's the beauty of it. Undertale will only give what you give to it. It mirrors you, the player, and shows you want from it.

In my opinion, Rust is an incredible game, there is a lot to do and explore from the first time you spawn in and wake up.
You can do many things on Rust from joining a clan and controlling your favourite server to making an un-raidable base in the middle of the ocean.
The graphics are enjoyable and can look realistic at times and run smoothly without high PC requirements.
The controls are comfortable, however, take some getting used to.
There is a large variety of activities to do but can get tedious at times and once you have done everything there tends not to be much more to do. Although I think there is not always much to do there are updates that are brought out every week which can keep the gameplay fresh and addictive.
I personally would recommend Rust as it is a fun experience, however, be prepared to get annoyed when being raided or killed for gear and resources to be stolen.

Overview:
Rust may seem just another average, run-of-the mill multiplayer survival early access title you see pop up on Steam every now and then, and for the most part, you'd be right. However, seeing the vast community that Rust has managed to put together, and seeing it on sale, I decided to give it a go, and boy, do I have a tale to tell! This game is both good, great, and horrible at the same time. Keep reading to understand why.
Worth Noting: I won't talk about really specific things as they are always subject to change. This will be a review of the overall experience you will get out of the game.
The Pros:
Great Maps - Each server has it's own procedural map (which you can see here) and it is pretty huge. Plenty of nice landscapes, biomes and landmarks to explore. With different spreading of resources and rare goods spots.
Powerful Crafting - Crafting is intuitive, takes time to do, and offers many items to choose from, and even more to risk your life gathering ingredients for. Brings the balance between a sandbox builder and shooter. Building your base is also a pleasant experience once you've gathered the resources.
The Social Aspect - If you don't have friends that play rust, you're pretty much doomed if you can't join a clan or small group. Rust is ruthless, with players jumping at each-others' necks for survival. You will be hunted, harassed, and you are expected to do the same, lest you risk being killed yourself. Teamwork and lack of trust in strangers are emphasized and crucially important here.
Intense fights! - When people get greedy, they tend to rely on others to do the hard work for them. Enter raiding bases, and defending your own. If you happen to be online when you are attacked, raids are blood-pumping, scary, but also tons of fun, no matter on which side of the wall you are. Guns, crossbows and explosives everywhere!
Strategy Based - Rust rewards brain over brawn. If you can make a good base design, place your home somewhere strategic, kill enemies from cover, or even deceive them, trap them etc. brings a whole world of rewards and will keep you alive for longer than flailing your assault rifle.
Bi-weekly Updates - Even though this game has been in Alpha for 2 years now, updates are rolling in about two times a week, and it's nice to see a steady development flow. Still, it may be unfinished for a long time, but definitely playable nonetheless.
Modded Servers - Want to freebuild? Want to get all resources and just focus on killing? There are a lot of community hosted servers with mods just for that!
The Cons:
Ruthless! - Every one will try to kill you on sight, no questions asked. Everyone will try to raid your base, even though you just started. You will end up entering the game only to find everything you had stolen and your based turned to ruins. I myself with a group of 3 other friends just lost 50 hours of playtime each to an overnight raid, which brings me to my next point:
Raiding is too easy! - Once you get your hands on a few C4 and / or rockets, raiding becomes too easy to perform and too hard to defend against. In order to have a well defended base, you will need to sacrifice actual inside room, if you want to actually be able to build it. Offline raiding (attacking once the players are offline) is also sadly available. You may have lookout towers and a lot of guns. But with no one to operate them, you will lose 100%.
Building Sucks! - I said it's fun, and it is, but in order to combat abuse, you are only allowed to remove structures you placed 10 minutes after you place them. If you notice a mistake, or if you want to expand the building and say, replace a wall with a door, then tough luck, buddy! You'll have to raid your own base. So, start small, think in advance, stack resources and only build once you know what you want!
Conclusion:
I recommend this game. It's fun, and it's frustrating, but it's fun because it is frustrating. Don't be afraid to lose, and try to have fun! This game is great with friends, and it has a very large community built around it!
Early Access Disclaimer:
As with all Early Access titles I review, I urge the reader to consider that this is an unfinished product and it can change for the best or for the worst during development. Unless you are happy about the current state of the game, or want to support the developers, then do not purchase this game. You run the risk of not liking it later / being abandoned, and you will have only yourself to blame.

If you are a fan of the first Borderlands game, discontinue reading this and buy now! If you are new to the series It is a blend of RPG and FPS at its finest with more guns than you can shake a stick at.
Graphics: It has a unique take in this department with the use of cell shading that gives everything a comic book feel. The world is more diverse than the first in the series.  It's also worth mentioning that this is one of the first games that I have noticed PhysX utilized.  That being said if you want extra special effects the game favors Nvidia cards over ATI.  If you have an ATI card the game will still run fine but if you want to beef up the PhysX setting you better have a BEASTLY CPU to pull it off without very noticeable FPS drops at higher PhysX settings.
Gameplay: A very fluid FPS with character progression thru leveling up and attaining skill points.  These skill points can be allocated to unlock many character specific abilities. Want to make a beast that can mash thru bosses SP style? Done. Or you can create a skill set that works well with a team. With up to 4 player co-op multiplayer (that also scales in difficulty as well as the quality of loot found) you will find that each character can play an important part in that team.  Your skill tree isn't carved in stone as you can reassign points at different stations in the game for a small sum of in-game money.
Replayability: (Screw you that IS A WORD when it comes to videogames!) Very high on this game.  Considering the fact that after you beat the game the first time it unlocks a more difficult mode, but with the higher difficulty comes more rewards.  My only gripe with this area at the moment is the fact that the level cap is set at 50 vanilla.  The level cap will be increased sometime in the future (at least thats what they did in the previous game, the devs have also promised a level cap but it seems they have more important things to do at the moment).  With four characters to play with out of the box, and one character that is DLC you will still have plenty of fun getting them to level 50.  I have 3 Characters that are sitting at lvl 50 and im waiting for that damn level cap since I have farmed out bosses etc to get most of the god tier drops for 50, and most of that will probably be rendered obsolete once they raise the lvl cap so that has killed some of the replayability for me at the moment.

Now, if you've played the first Borderlands and you liked it, you'll probably love this one. I got sick of the old one, this is a similar formula but with much wackier weapons (there is one that you reload by throwing it and it explodes, I mean, what the hell is with that? :D), different vehicles, new charismatic characters and especially LOTS of enemies, the spawn rate is sick and I like that. The only con is it can slowly become boring if you do it all solo, I prefer to play it with friends or random people if there are no friends. For those who don't know Borderlands, it's like this... You can imagine something like torchlight or diablo, skill trees, lots of loot, quests, level ups, big maps, dungeons, all those kind of stuff, BUT with a twist. You see, Borderlands is an FPS in some sort of god-forsaken planet inhabitated by psychopaths. But which counts more in the gameplay? The RPG aspect (stats, skills, rare equipment,...) or the FPS aspect (shoot, dodge, strafe, aim,...) ? The great thing is neither, I say it's roughly 50/50, you can go kill people of higher level, it will be hard, or if you aim too high, outright impossible (you do almost no damage while they oneshot you... with an automatic gun) but if you suck at the fps aspect your characater may be dying a lot with characters of his level. Oh, but do not worry, the difficulty is fine. The coop is greatly done, no DC, no lag, no nothing (at least for me), and the more guys you have in your party, the stronger the "creatures" of pandora become and the better loot they drop, sweet! Definitely recommend.

Do I reccomend the game? Yes it's worth the money, but don't be fooled by the die hard fans, the game has flaws and they're not few and far between. This is a warning for possible spoilers.
Pro's:
*Characters aren't just 1 dimensional tropes.
*The music is very good.
*The gameplay is fun and original.
*Very memorable.
Cons:
*The music may be good, but it's not varied. The creator, Toby Fox, has a habit of taking songs he's already created and remixing them to use them again, even songs from the game itself, he really uses and abuse the idea of a leitmotif.
*The game is pretty badly paced, you'll feel like you spend an eternity in the Ruins, a few minutes in snowdins, maybe 10 minutes in hotlands, 5 minutes in the Core, and 2 in the final area. The rest will be battles and walking around at an abysmally slow pace.
*The game is very short. It can be beaten in 6 hours easily minus the time it takes to beat Sans on a Genocide run.
*The game is REALLY easy. Like I said it can be beaten in 6 hours easily, the only difficulty you'll find is on a Genocide run with two bosses, Undyne the Undying and Sans (Which are the only two real bosses).
*The Genocide path is hidden unless you want to play the game like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ JRPG and grind for miles.
*The game doesn't really have a plot besides the characters backstories, and only Alphys and the Goats have quality backstories.
* A lot of the memorability and likability comes from "Teh feels" so if you're just an unfeeling cynic like me you'll feel a little bit sour since that's basically all it tries to do character wise.
*The meta aspect is really pushed home, up to a point where it tries to dissuade you from replaying the game. Additionally you can't get the best ending EVER if you've done a genocide run first without external file manipulation.
*The message the game is trying to give in that "Actions have consequences" is extremely on the nose, obvious and anvilicious.
*The game is very linear, now you'd expect such from an RPG of this type, but there are no side routes, few hidden things and very little sidequests or other things that would differentiate runs.
and finally
*The fan base ♥♥♥♥ing sucks. The game is a Tublrina cringe magnet. Do not look at the Subreddit. Do not Look at Tumblr and for the sake of your own sanity do not misspell it "Undertail" if you aren't prepared to bleach your eyes,
Now you might say "Well if there are so many cons then why is this a positive review?" Well there are a few reasons, one is that I think the game is worth the money, although it'd be better to get it on sale since it's ONLY JUST worth the money for the little time.
Seccondly I want to get attention to the downsides, as the negative reviews are drowned out by rabid fans (I payed the courtesy of upvoting all constructive criticism)
And three I actually like the game, despite it's downfalls (Evident by my avatar), but I do not think that it's perfect like everyone says it is. No matter how many times the fans cry this isn't game of the year material. But it is a memorable and fairly enjoyable experience.
If this game's price was a small loan of a million dollars, I'd still recomend it.

Games have the power to do things that any other medium cannot, and very little portion of games actually use this power to it's advantage. This "game" does just that!
I wouldn't say this is the best game ever (as in subjectively), because it has some bad flaws that people get picky about, but this game is unique, because it is one of those games that was able to blend gameplay and story together (not make great gameplay and a great story) to make something memorable.
?/10 Cannot rate this. It's an experience, it's not trying to be flawless, it is trying to make an experience and thats it.
Recommend it to everyone. I hope this gets on consoles, so that more people can experience this piece of art.

I wasn't too impressed when I got through Borderlands 1 for the first time many years ago and at one point I actually quite disliked the game but Borderlands 2 was a serious step up. It won me over entirely and I now love anything Borderlands related.
Borderlands 2 really did take everything up a notch. Everything is bigger, better and it actually opens up the first one in a way that I found to be quite clever. The story in 2 not only made the first one feel more worth it but progressed in a way that really brings the universe together. There are so many characters, all with their own histories. There is so much going on and so much to discover. You can play the main game and get the main story and all, but if you get into it there is a lot of detail to it with the side missions and DLCs. If you're a competitionist, this one will take you a while.
The main thing that attracts me to this game is that it's quite different to your usual FPS. It's kind of like an isometric RPG type game like Diablo but in first-person. Weapon customisation is huge and you can farm bosses for better and better gear. There are loads of challenges and even skins that you can loot or earn for those that like collecting things. With a fair choice of classes (even more choice if you get the DLC characters) each playthrough will feel a little different seeing as each one has a different ability and different skill trees. Completing challenges also earns you "bad♥♥♥♥♥ranks" which can be used to increase your base stats. Great part of that being they carry across to all of your characters. Beef up your first character a little with bad♥♥♥♥♥ranks, start a new character and that new character will get those stat boosts too.
I must of played this game through like 10 times already with friends who wanted to play it co-op and I absolutely love it. I adore the humour in these games, I think it's the main reason why i'm so content with playing it so much. The characters are interesting and I love learning new things about the universe. Handsome Jack ended up being one of the best video game villains ever.
It was great when they came out with the pre-sequel and Tell-Tale came out with the Tales from the Borderlands because I was excited to know more. They fill in the gaps and expand things even further. I can't wait for Borderlands 3.

I do feel a little bad about calling Borderlands 2 my GOTY. It's a fairly standard FPS spliced with some of Diablo's DNA, same as the original. The story's a bit better this time around, as is the voice-acting; the humor has suffered a little, but otherwise it's a clear improvement over its solid predecessor, both in its writing and its mechanics.
Still, 2012 brought us, among many others, Hotline Miami and Thirty Flights of Loving. Games that felt special, somehow. They were not as predictable, not as immediately familiar as Borderlands 2 or many of the other great games released this year were.
2012 was also the year of Twine games. Text games made by everyone, for everyone, about anything. Highly important stuff. The most important thing to happen to games in a long time. Much more so than another FPS, or ARPG, or top-down ♥♥♥♥-'em-up.
So why's Borderlands 2 my Game of the Year 2012, then?
Well, I had played almost 250 hours of it before the year was over, and I'm not even done with it now.
Sure, at times I found myself wishing it was smarter. Less crude, less mindless.
Most of the time, though, I only had one thought:
Deep down, this really is everything I want from a video game.
And it's even better with friends.
Go grab some buddies and catch a ride. You won't regret it.

On: Emotion in Video Games, or "Why Undertale made choices matter".
In Undertale, I was quickly introduced to a flower, which told me it was kill or be killed. I disregarded this message, because I had read so many comments about this game, making it sound like a kid’s game.
When my first real fight came, I made a conscious choice to attack, assuming that somehow, the fight would end well - I was already too attached to this character to see her perish so quickly. And I made a mistake. Flowey was right. I was upset with myself, and regretted my choice - an absolute rarity in any video game - and reset to an earlier time. I found a way to endure this fight, and moved forward, only to be confronted by Flowey. He reminded me of what I did, and it felt like a punch in the gut. I wanted so badly to hide my rash actions, but he knew, and I was ashamed. In less than an hour, Undertale made me feel wonder, joy, excitement, despair and regret - emotions video games rarely make me feel anymore. For this reason, I must recommend this game. The music adds such a genuine sense of legitimacy and heart to the game, the gameplay is solid, but how Undertale makes you feel is its defining trait.

I was a big fan of the first Borderlands. The crude humor drew me in, and the entertaining gameplay kept me playing for hours on end.
I'm not the biggest fan of shooters. In fact, Borderlands 2 is the only shooter I find myself wanting to play. Then again, I'm a big RPG fan, and Borderlands 2 meets that need despite having a different combat style from what I'm used to.
Borderlands 2 could be compared to Diablo in a way, at least in terms of the loot system. You fight monsters and do quests, and you get better gear. Most of the end game is spent farming the best weapons -- that is, if you don't ruin the game by cheating first. Just because a player comes into the game and drops amazing guns in front of you doesn't mean you should take them.
One of the biggest improvements I've seen in Borderlands 2 over the first game is the driving. Driving in the first game was always an unbearable nightmare. This time around, I feel the playing field is more levelled, and hopping into a car won't signal endless hours of torture.
The replayability on this game does exist, but in a limited manner. There's four main characters to choose from, and two you can purchase as DLC. Beyond making one of each class, the game doesn't offer much variation. You pick up a quest, you do a quest, you turn in a quest -- rinse, wash, repeat. The quests don't change.
Regardless, this is a game you might find yourself coming back to every now and then. And I appreciate that the developers are constantly pushing out new DLC to keep things fresh.
