The graphics in Undertale resemble that of older SNES RPGs, and is very much inspired by the Mother series. Most people will not be impressed by the graphics- the game is 2D, which is a turn off for more people than it should be. If you can appreciate the very stylized pixels presented in the game, the graphics are really, really solid. If you don't have a thing for games that will sacrifice superior graphics for a very stylized aesthetic, you won't be impressed.
Never have I ever been more into such a deceptively simple soundtrack. It's easy to enjoy soundtracks from
or
, which have huge orchestras ready to compose an entire two and a half hours of music, but in Undertale, it's
16-bit chiptune- and what wonderful chiptune it is. The best part though is that while it's not all old 16-bit style music, even when it's not, it seamlessly blends into the rest of the soundtrack. If you search YouTube for "Undertale cover", you're presented with over 500,000 results. That's how good the soundtrack is. They nailed it.
There is slight,
spoilers in the next section. Nothing crazy, nothing to avoid, nothing you wouldn't learn from watching the trailer, but you've been warned.
The game has three different MAJOR endings, but an incredible amount of small decisions that will effect the way the ending plays out in either of the three paths. The story is better in some paths (in my opinion), but overall, the story is incredibly impressive with amount of depth that is offered. I highly recommend you don't look up anything other the three different major paths, and how to take them, because if you know nothing about this game, it will be difficult to find them all, but I enjoyed all three endings immensely.
It's hard for me to like characters. Usually, this is because the character shares nothing in common with myself, or because the character seem so fake and planned that it's just
unbelievable. Neither of these was the case for the characters in
. Everyone has someone in the game that they will relate to, and a good amount of people will relate to all of them in some way. Overall, there was one or two characters that I didn't enjoy, because they were either overbearing or just didn't generate the feelings with me that I could tell the creator was trying to create, but this is a very rare occurrence and does not effect the game much at all.
For me, this is the low point of
, which is strange to me, because I loved the actual gameplay. The exploration is what was just a little too bland for my tastes. Walk here. Press Z. Walk there. Press Z. The actual battles, however, are incredibly interesting, and combined with tight controls you wouldn't expect in a game like
, This makes for one the most enjoyable experiences I've had in these older styled games. All the fights are incredibly memorable, and this is usually a good thing, but the second time I played through, I remembered everything from before, which took some of the guessing out, which is what made the first play though so enjoyable. Overall, it sounds like nitpicking, and that's because it is.
I went into
thinking that it was going to be over hyped, and it was. That didn't stop me from enjoying immensely though. The game is a breath of fresh air from what I'm used to playing and very welcome in this day, where every game seems to be the same thing over, and over, and over again. I don't think the game will ever get a sequel, and I hope it doesn't...but if it does, I'll buy it day one.

This has grown to be my all time favourite franchise.
I wasn't too impressed when I got through Borderlands 1 for the first time many years ago and at one point I actually quite disliked the game but Borderlands 2 was a serious step up. It won me over entirely and I now love anything Borderlands related.
Borderlands 2 really did take everything up a notch. Everything is bigger, better and it actually opens up the first one in a way that I found to be quite clever. The story in 2 not only made the first one feel more worth it but progressed in a way that really brings the universe together. There are so many characters, all with their own histories. There is so much going on and so much to discover. You can play the main game and get the main story and all, but if you get into it there is a lot of detail to it with the side missions and DLCs. If you're a competitionist, this one will take you a while.
The main thing that attracts me to this game is that it's quite different to your usual FPS. It's kind of like an isometric RPG type game like Diablo but in first-person. Weapon customisation is huge and you can farm bosses for better and better gear. There are loads of challenges and even skins that you can loot or earn for those that like collecting things. With a fair choice of classes (even more choice if you get the DLC characters) each playthrough will feel a little different seeing as each one has a different ability and different skill trees. Completing challenges also earns you "bad♥♥♥♥♥ranks" which can be used to increase your base stats. Great part of that being they carry across to all of your characters. Beef up your first character a little with bad♥♥♥♥♥ranks, start a new character and that new character will get those stat boosts too.
I must of played this game through like 10 times already with friends who wanted to play it co-op and I absolutely love it. I adore the humour in these games, I think it's the main reason why i'm so content with playing it so much. The characters are interesting and I love learning new things about the universe. Handsome Jack ended up being one of the best video game villains ever.
It was great when they came out with the pre-sequel and Tell-Tale came out with the Tales from the Borderlands because I was excited to know more. They fill in the gaps and expand things even further. I can't wait for Borderlands 3.
Even the little things make this game great. The enemy chat dialog for example, they can be the same enemy copy and pasted but given different voices who all say weird sh*t. It makes me laugh to myself and even after how much I've played it I somehow always notice something new. It really makes the game feel more alive when you're blasting through a crowd of enemies and a psycho blatantly quotes Breaking Bad or shouts a new curse word at you and you're like... well wow okay, did he f*cking just?
All in all this game is basically the best game ever.

I do feel a little bad about calling Borderlands 2 my GOTY. It's a fairly standard FPS spliced with some of Diablo's DNA, same as the original. The story's a bit better this time around, as is the voice-acting; the humor has suffered a little, but otherwise it's a clear improvement over its solid predecessor, both in its writing and its mechanics.
Still, 2012 brought us, among many others, Hotline Miami and Thirty Flights of Loving. Games that felt special, somehow. They were not as predictable, not as immediately familiar as Borderlands 2 or many of the other great games released this year were.
2012 was also the year of Twine games. Text games made by everyone, for everyone, about anything. Highly important stuff. The most important thing to happen to games in a long time. Much more so than another FPS, or ARPG, or top-down ♥♥♥♥-'em-up.
So why's Borderlands 2 my Game of the Year 2012, then?
Well, I had played almost 250 hours of it before the year was over, and I'm not even done with it now.
Sure, at times I found myself wishing it was smarter. Less crude, less mindless.
Most of the time, though, I only had one thought:
Deep down, this really is everything I want from a video game.
And it's even better with friends.
Go grab some buddies and catch a ride. You won't regret it.

I recommend this game to those who want to have some multiplayer FPS-RPG experience, though you can go on a adventure alone if you want.
Just remember that if you are more players playing the game ( max. 4ppl) the harder the mobs get, the better guns you get, and the funnier the Gaming get. ^^

This game is, in all honesty, one of the most enjoyable and heartwarming experiences I have had in a long time with video games. It was made by a single person, more or less, which begs the question: Why do Triple A titles fail to recreate this same level of genuine entertainment and soul put into Undertale? The answer is quite simple; its personal. Toby Fox said so himself on Twitter around the time of this review. Toby made the game not to be marketed and merchandised, but to be enjoyed as a video game. This is what makes these kinds of games, the Undertales, the Shovel Knights, the Nuclear Thrones, different from Triple A titles. It's a work of art that was designed to connect with the player, emphasize with the player, and make the player understand their choices. Triple A titles don't do this♥♥♥♥♥♥ We constantly see game after game, year after year, of the same♥♥♥♥♥♥that companies spew out for the cash and cash alone. That is what companies are designed to do, by the way; make money. Undertale wasn't made by a company who simply want to raise their own bottom line at the expense of the time and money of others. It was made by a guy, just like you and me, who wanted to genuinely express himself to not only the gaming community, but most likely himself too. Toby Fox is an artist, not a company.

Sadly, I found that the numeric keybinds for the item slots no longer function properly (although mousewheel seems to work), and the framerates are now abysmal.   This has gone from being a survival game to a faction-based raiding / destruction game.

I stand by my recommendation to NOT purchase this game.

I do feel a little bad about calling Borderlands 2 my GOTY. It's a fairly standard FPS spliced with some of Diablo's DNA, same as the original. The story's a bit better this time around, as is the voice-acting; the humor has suffered a little, but otherwise it's a clear improvement over its solid predecessor, both in its writing and its mechanics.
Still, 2012 brought us, among many others, Hotline Miami and Thirty Flights of Loving. Games that felt special, somehow. They were not as predictable, not as immediately familiar as Borderlands 2 or many of the other great games released this year were.
2012 was also the year of Twine games. Text games made by everyone, for everyone, about anything. Highly important stuff. The most important thing to happen to games in a long time. Much more so than another FPS, or ARPG, or top-down ♥♥♥♥-'em-up.
So why's Borderlands 2 my Game of the Year 2012, then?
Well, I had played almost 250 hours of it before the year was over, and I'm not even done with it now.
Sure, at times I found myself wishing it was smarter. Less crude, less mindless.
Most of the time, though, I only had one thought:
Deep down, this really is everything I want from a video game.
And it's even better with friends.
Go grab some buddies and catch a ride. You won't regret it.

And what I mean by that is it's pathfinding and AI, The old DayZ had quite blocky pathfinding, but in retrospect, So did ArmA.
2. The graphic settings and entire option menu has been cut/copy/pasted and not only that, But it was done in such a way it butchered the, almost-sometimes-good option menu from ArmA2, And changed it to something that was.. Prehistoric.. I mean.. the original Doom had better option menus. Ontop of this, When I first tried playing it, It set itself to like.. 400x640x16 or something.. incredibly stupid. I have two monitors, and everything on my left monitor was almost burried on the right one, A easy fix.. But this shouldn't happen in a modern game. Even early access, Not acceptable. Look at KSP and Project Zomboid, Kenji or any other early access game. Games in 2015 do *not* need to start in a "safe mode" for any reason. Whatsoever.
3. The inventory system is.. awkward, That might be a personal mark against me, But I'm not happy with the way it's been handled, It's very.. figity.. Sometimes you'll see stuff in your vicinity, That you cannot see whatsoever, And vice versa. That's just bad handling of loot in a game that again, We should not be seeing, I'll go easy on this one, It is early access, And I'm not asking for polish I should be seeing in a 59.99$ game, but that's just.. rediculous? Why did you add so many loot spots on a new chernarus and not /at least/ Bug test them? Maybe even a little? I'm fine with seeing objects sticking through walls.. but.. But things under the floor/invisible loot spawns? That's really not okay IMO to release a map/code loot to spawn under floors of cells.
4. Riding on the coat-tails of #3, What on earth did they do to the loot tables? Now, I know that there are servers labeled "High loot" But I want to play the original DayZ, Y'know, What we're paying for here. Not a slightly customized version, But it's litterally impossible to find any type of weapon, Which.. Isn't a problem since there aren't any zombies to use them on at all, But I mean.. Come.. oonn, In the 4 hours I played, I took very common routes after spawning, Solinchny towards NW, and through countless barns and hunting shacks.. I know it's suppose to be hard and I respect that but.. Damn.. You normally could at least find, I don't know, A pistol, before you hit the NW airfield, Where I'm assuming they've piled on every possible weapon spawn ever to compensate. Or one of the new Military bases.
I'm really disapointed in the state this game is in, even for alpha, When it went standalone, I expected better. Not far, far worse. It's such a cakewalk now and that's not okay. The public hive thing? I like that, But the whole mod-y feel of DayZ and how awesome it was seemed to die with a direct relation to money earned. Pretty hard.
And for people who might say I'm cracking on a alpha game, Damn right I am, This game was in alpha like 2 years ago as a mod, And it felt like a finished product, There was some broken things and some bugs, But it was a mod, Nobody was really making bank off this game, Now we've got the full game, the standalone game, and it's in worse condition than the mod was.. Why not just charge for the mod like it was? I'd much rather play that.

Alright, so I think it is about time I review this game.
At this moment of writing this review, I have 190hrs on record for this game. I have played it enough to know how it goes. This game has an amazing potential. That is something that gets tossed around alot in reviews, but I really mean it. From the Survival Genre, its amazing. It has the features that you would expect to see, and enjoy, and dislike. The interface takes a while to get used to, zombies can be pests, people will try to get in your way of succeeding in this game. But, let me start with what makes it a great survival game.
Firstly, the crafting is there, the hunting is there, the cooking is there, the player health, food, hydration, stamina, tempreture etc. are also there. You hop in a river, you get soaked and cold. You shake, then you struggle to aim. Its that sorta thing. It works well. If you decide to run into a town, knowing you will have to probably aim at some one, you shouldn't sprint before battle, as you increase your weapon sway because you are tired. It makes sense, and that in itself breeds new situations, and things to think about. Crafting also makes sense. Burlap bag+rope=improvised back pack. Materials that can burn+some wood and sticks= fire. Its nice. The hunting makes sense too. You have to sneak up, aim, shoot in the neck, get food from it, put it over a fire, and eat it. Shoot the animal too much, you get worse quality food. The list goes on, and it works. So from a 'Survival Game' aspect, its nice.
Now the community, the people that you encounter in DayZ.
I've noticed that is really depends on the country you are playing in, what servers, blah blah. But generally it has the same feel. I have encountered many people in DayZ. At times I was geared, they were not, vice versa. Sometimes it goes well, most of the time, it doesn't. People often 'Kill On Sight', and often for some motive, or none other than, 'I am bored.'
People get other people in interesting situations, such as kidnapping, force feeding food, etc.
Sometimes you encounter some one that is trying to help around. He gives you free food, clothes, saline bags and the such. Its nice, but these sort of people are not as common as, say, the common bandit, who may choose to politley rob you, or just shoot you on sight.
But none of this is really 100% because of the game. It is not the game that has the fault (as some might say) of annoying bandits that 'ruin' the experience of DayZ. It's the people behind that bandit character, the person clicking that left mouse button as soon as he sees anyone who could be a possible threat.
It is the people, not the game.
But I personally feel that these different people and situations are the defining 'feature' of DayZ. It is what makes the game unique, fustrating and fun. The game is developing slowly, but it is, believe it or not.
There was a point where you spawned, got geared, got bored, and so then went off to kill people. Now you can find a tent, set up camp, live off the land, start a farm, fish etc. You still get people that just go off to either protect the fresh spawns, or to kill everyone in their sight.
The game will become better. I know it will. Barricading houses, different vehicles, all of this will only improve the game.
BUT. Be warned. This game is VERY glitchy. VERY. Keep this is mind when you try to get into a car, but then your gun falls out of your hands, or when you realize suddenly that persistance was turned off, so now your tent is gone. Or when you run from a zombie into a nice building, close all the doors, but remember that there is about a 50/50 chance that the zombie could easily run through the walls, and begin to tear at your face.
(if you want to know about the devs, and what they do to stay in touch with us, please read another review. I decided to not include comments about that, as my review would simply be too long)

The positives: it's unique, if you somehow think puns and randomness is funny or endearing then you will probably enjoy this game, it's too simple to have any real technical issues so you can run it on virtually anything. The negatives: If you are an older gamer like me, the writing is not as good as the hype would lead you to believe. While the bullet-hell mini game combat is different, it coupled with other design flaws makes it very difficult to play the completely non-lethal route your first time through unless you read a guide and know what to expect next. I won't get into details, but there is no way to get more hp without using lethal means. I personally found most of the writing adolescent at best, but to each their own. And finally puzzles are introduced in the beginning making me feel like they were going to be a major part of the game, but ended up being used not even a handful of times.
In conclusion, I as a mid 30s gamer, I don't think I am the demographic for this game, I forced myself to get through it because of everyones hype and the ending was somewhat infuriating as I really don't want to devote another 5 hours into this game just to see another ending.

Being honest I didn't take much interest in Undertale when I first saw it, mainly because this style/genre doesn't interest me an awful lot, however after seeing some cleverly written dialogue within the game as well as all my friends raving about it, I decided that there was no harm in trying it.
I can safely say, that buying this game is the best $10 I've ever spent on anything in my entire life.
Somehow this game that I had no intention of really acknowledging has now become my personal favourite game of all time. The writing and dialogue, as well as the cast of characters which was what originally interested me are perfectly written with clever uses of comedy as well as subtle commentaries of how people and society behave and act, being elegentally woven into the games atmosphere rather than shoved down the players throat. As well as the comedy being extremely well done, the game knows when it wants to be very serious and focus on the central idea of the game, being the justifications of your actions, and believe me when your enemies have this much character to them, you better have good reason for doing what you 'must' do.
The story and writing is extremely strong however accompanied by the soundtrack just makes the experience and immersion infinetly better. Each piece is greatly unique and great to listen to, hell as I'm writing this review I am listening to the soundtrack right now.
What surprised me the most however was the fighting mechanic and the gameplay towards that. The options to attack or passively spare your enemies is a lovely touch and adds a layer of complexity to the fighting. The challenge of dodging the enemies attacks is deeply satisfying as well as not being too challenging to make the player angry, well at least in my playthroughs i didnt get mad
Overall this is a masterfully crafted piece of art, there arent many games where I would play twice in a row and enjoy the experience more the second time. Give this game a try, it'll fill you with determination.

What can be said about Undertale that hasn't already been said? Nothing, really. If you haven't been convinced to get the game already, this review probobally won't do much to change that. However, I'll still try my best to try and convince you why this game is something you should buy.
Despite what people may say, Undertale is not just "some meme game" or "that furry thing". It's also not "the SJW game", as some people like to call it for some reason. However, I will admit it's also not "Best Game Ever".
(Seriously GameFAQS, what the hell?)
What Undertale is however, is a great experience. The combat system is something that hasn't been done in many games before. And no, I'm not just referring to the ACT option that everyone knows by now, I'm referring to everything else in it. Whether it be the FIGHT option being more about timing than simply grinding to improve your stats, you actually are able to doge opponent's attacks based on your timing and skill, and the fun little secrets that can occur if you use certain items, it's definately a fun way to go about fighting enemies.
Also, the characters in the game are definately a reason to play. Without spoiling the story too much, the characters all have flaws and redeeming qualities, making them more than just one note stereotypes, which makes you actually care for them.
Of course, there's also the soundtrack. Oh my lord the soundtrack. I have heard that Toby Fox created songs for the game and then afterwards made the areas and situation where they would play, and this is definately evident. Each song in the soundtrack clearly has love and care put into it, and fits the area it plays in perfectly.Whether it be a song that makes you sad, happy, pumped up to fight an enemy, scared, this game uses music better than most games in recent memory. Several people I know who don't even play the game regularly listen to the soundtrack, because it's just THAT good.
Finally, it subverts the RPG genre and gaming in ways that really tie the game together. I won't say how, because I really can't in fear of spoilers, but that is all I'll put in terms of that aspect.
Undertale is truely an experience, one that I would reccomend to almost any gamer I know. It's not my favorite game of all time, but it's definately my GOTY for 2015.

Ahhh Borderlands 2, a better game overall than Borderlands but still has some issues. This time around there's slightly more interesting characters that deliver some pretty funny dialogue (Personal favourite being Nomad's midget obsession). Story is pretty bare bones like the last game but the antagonist, Handsome Jack,  is so much better than the one from first game who I can't even remember the name of, with him being one of the best characters in the game in my opinion. Ending isn'tas♥♥♥♥♥♥poor as the first but still is pretty standard and meh with the only interesting element coming right around Chapter 15 or so. Gameplay's exactly the same so there's not much to say there aside from the UI which has been improved slightly but still can get annoying to cycle through sometimes when you want to do something specific like compare weapons or equip a weapon in a certain slot. What kills Borderlands 2 is that it can get so boring especially if you're attempting to do all / most the side quests. Having to drive / fast travel to an area then clear out all the enemies for the 15th time just to get to your objective gets old to the point where I had to stop playing the game for a while as it was so tedious. I was playing Single Player however so this is probably assuaged by playing with a friend or three. In summary, Borderlands 2 is an addicting and fun game that's worth a play if you enjoyed the first but can get dull in some circumstances and still has a few kinks that stop it being a great game.

I don't even know where to begin with this game honestly. I never thought a game could grab my heart, leave me in tears at the end, and with a positive outlook on life. It takes everything you would expect from an RPG or even a standard game itself and scrambles it to the point you don't know what twist to expect. Every NPC character has such heartwarming, witty, and amusing personalities. There's plenty to laugh at, identify with, and sympathize for.
It's hard to really talk about what's in this game without spoiling things. It's best to go into this game practically blind having only seen reviews, screenshots, and the trailer. If you've been on many gaming related websites (r/gaming, /v/, or Youtube Gaming) or art websites (deviantArt or Tumblr) it's difficult to avoid seeing the memorable characters and spoilers related to them. What else can I say about the game without spoiling things? Well if you're familiar with RPGs, especially Earthbound/Mother then you're in familiar territory. For what appears to be a small RPG game captilizing on NES era style graphics and nostalgia: There's plenty of little quirks and easter eggs to discover. The soundtrack is amazing, varied, and compliments every moment spot on. I haven't heard such memorable game music since Okami.
For anyone who can truly appreciate the fact that video games can be more then just another form of entertainment and for anyone who has a personality past the "war-driven" or "edgy" one that has grasped the industry in this modern age of gaming: This game.... no.... this experience is for you! This is one unexpected game I will never forget in my life!

INGREDIENTS
• 2 pounds mahi mahi (skinned, boned and cleaned) cut into 1-ounce strips
• 2 cups all-purpose flour
• 3 eggs, lightly beaten
• 4 tablespoons water
• 2 cups panko bread crumbs
• Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
• Vegetable oil, for frying
• 1/2 head savoy cabbage, finely shredded
• 1 bunch cilantro, leaves picked
• 1 bunch chives, chopped
• 3 limes, cut into wedges for garnish
PINK CHILE MAYONNAISE:
•	1 cup sour cream
•	1 cup mayonnaise
•	3 chipotles in adobo, plus 2 tablespoons of adobo sauce
•	1/2 lemon, juiced
•	Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
MANGO-RADISH SALSA:
•	2 limes
•	2 mangoes, diced
•	4 to 5 red radishes, diced
•	1 red onion, diced
•	1 tablespoon chili powder
•	1/2 bunch fresh cilantro, leaves chopped
•	1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
•	Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
DIRECTIONS
Prepare the fish. Cut the pieces of fish into 1-ounce strips. Set up abreading station of flour, lightly beaten eggs with water, and seasoned panko bread crumbs. Season all with salt and pepper.Dredge the pieces of fish in flour, egg then bread crumbs. Once all the fish is breaded deep-fry in small batches in (375 degrees F) oil.Drain on paper towels and season with salt. Keep warm until ready to serve.
Prepare the pink chile mayonnaise. Put the chipotles in a blenderand puree until smooth. Add the sour cream, mayonnaise, adobo sauce and lemon juice and continue to process until the mixture is consistent and creamy. Season with salt and pepper and refrigerate until ready to use.
Prepare the mango-radish salsa. Remove the peel and pith from the limes and cut between the membranes to remove the segments. Put these "supremes" into a bowl and squeeze over the juice from the membranes. Add the remaining ingredients and mix. Season and refrigerate until ready to use. You can also place all of the ingredients into a food processor and puree for a smoother salsa.
To serve, set up the tacos "family-style". Assemble the fish in a pile on a plate; the pink chile mayonnaise in a bowl; and mango-radish salsa in another. Set a pile of shredded savoy cabbage, cilantro leaves, chopped chives and lime wedges next to the fish. Toast the corn tortillas lightly over an open flame (on your stove top) and serve.

You may look at Rust and think its just a basic survival, multiplayer game. For the most part, you would be right. But boy, you are missing out if you haven't played Rust.
I am going to section this out to try make things easier.
RUST being made in Unity, definately feels like a Unity made game. Graphics are great, controlls are easy and familiar, gravity is perfect etc.
Although there is no storyline, you definately make your own story as you play. Playing RUST alone is no easy task, and I get bet you any money you will not enjoy soloing RUST. Your best bet is to either play it with friends, or try and join a Team or Clan. This makes for some fun social interaction, and a lot of ease on the mind when worrying if you will survive over night.
The game is pretty simple. Survive. It has a lot of characteristics of Minecraft. Cut wood from trees, mine stone from stone nodes, and build a house to survive. Though you are not trying to survive from creepers, instead you are trying to not get murdered, mugged and humiliated by other players areound the world. They will use C4 to blow up your house. They will use a bone knife made from your friends bones to stab you while you sleep. They will take your pants so you have to run around with your little johnson flapping around. But, when the tables turn, you can do the same back!
My overall review of RUST is that it is a great game. You get angry, happy, upset and excited all at the same time. You experience fear and joy in one action. Its wierdly satisfying. I would recommend this game to ANYONE who does not get too angry at a game.
I find this game to be extremely glitch low, which is a great plus
Remember. Your base WILL get Raided, no matter how good it is. So build it well, and make sure you have a backup plan. Learn from each experience and build better and better every time!
If you do decide to buy RUST, make sure you watch tutorials. You will need to know what things are and what people are talking about and how things work. Please do this for yourself.

I don't even know where to begin with this game honestly. I never thought a game could grab my heart, leave me in tears at the end, and with a positive outlook on life. It takes everything you would expect from an RPG or even a standard game itself and scrambles it to the point you don't know what twist to expect. Every NPC character has such heartwarming, witty, and amusing personalities. There's plenty to laugh at, identify with, and sympathize for.
It's hard to really talk about what's in this game without spoiling things. It's best to go into this game practically blind having only seen reviews, screenshots, and the trailer. If you've been on many gaming related websites (r/gaming, /v/, or Youtube Gaming) or art websites (deviantArt or Tumblr) it's difficult to avoid seeing the memorable characters and spoilers related to them. So if you've managed to avoid content related to this game and have some interest in it: Play it now! Then relish in the fan created art and covers created by the community.

What else can I say about the game without spoiling things? Well if you're familiar with RPGs, especially Earthbound/Mother then you're in familiar territory. For what appears to be a small RPG game captilizing on NES era style graphics and nostalgia: There's plenty of little quirks and easter eggs to discover. The soundtrack is amazing, varied, and compliments every moment spot on. I haven't heard such memorable game music since Okami.
For anyone who can truly appreciate the fact that video games can be more then just another form of entertainment and for anyone who has a personality past the "war-driven" or "edgy" one that has grasped the industry in this modern age of gaming: This game.... no.... this experience is for you! This is one unexpected game I will never forget in my life!

Before I begin, YES this game is in ALPHA and I completely understand that games in ALPHA are buggy, laggy and oftentimes broken at one point or another in the course of their development. As a gamer, I am not here to placate the development team or ruffle the feathers of the clearly loyal fanbase. I am here to give an honest opinion of what my experience with this game has been like at this point - WITH EMPHASIS AT THIS POINT -
First off, I am historically not a fan of FPS games but just because they are not my 'thing' does not mean that they are undeserving of play. I picked up this title after the prodding of several guys that I know, my husband included. I figured- I will get shot in the face a few times and we will laugh it up and I will be done with it altogether. So I gave it a go with about 35 bucks. I mean that's the cost of taking the boys to the movies one time so not too pricy. Besides- I have been wrong about games in the past.
So, I loaded it up- prepared to be irritated.
What I discovered was that I actually liked it, mind you this was before the recent debacle that removed persistance. I met up with my friends we looted and shot zombies. I became fond of the Winchester rifle because at least I only had to hit crap once with the thing before they dropped. Some mechanics were not quite there yet but that was okay- the game is in alpha. We made ourselved a little tent city in the middle of nowhere and started storing up supplies and bags, everything was great. We raided the airfield and we explored freely knowing that we had gear stashed should we meet with untimely ends.
I began to make notes of what I would like to see- given the fact that the development team made it very clear that they were open to suggestions and wanted the community to participate- I mean that is the point of an alpha release is it not? So when I felt I had played enough to familiarize myself with the gameplay and mechanics I decided to post some of my findings on their "Official Forums". Here is where my problem with this title began...
I attempted to create an account- there was a problem and it would do nothing but give me an error telling me to try again later. So I tried later, on more than one occasion on more than one day. No luck. So I found the e-mail for support and sent them one detailing my problem. The response I got was automated, and from my e-mail provider informing me that the address I copy/pasted did not exist. So I shook my head and got back in the game.
Then the game updated and persistance was gone... and so were the majority of zombies... WOW this is so great now we have a zombie survival game with no persistant storage and no zombies. I tried to play but the game quickly devolved into a shooting fest where the only point to play is to shoot each other in the face, respawn, grab a weapon and go at it again.... not fun. "Oh but the game is in Alpha...." I just want to punch the crap out of the faces of everyone who spouts that comment off. Yes this game is in alpha but at this point it is most decidedly NOT a zombie survival game at all.
Which brings me to my experience with early access games- I own several alpha stage games and none of them are being produced with the same apathy as this one. They do not post anything of any value as to the state of their game or EVEN the things they expect to fix in their next update. OR EVEN WHEN that next update might be. Sure they update their forums but .... oh yeah the forums.....
So I go back to the forums to try again this morning.... now it says my e-mail is in use....WTF so I go through the proceedure of captcha playing to get the site to send me my username and then password reset.... follow the instructions- use reset code.......INVALID CODE.... so yeah forums are a bust.
This is not to say that I cannot be patient about this or that I am unwilling to wait for fixes and deal with bugs and interruptions in gameplay. I am however not willing to deal with the lack of communication and availability of information given out by the developer as to the status of their project.
To compare- ARK is currently in ALPHA as well and was released only a month ago on steam. They make small fixes nearly every day. They update steam almost daily with a report of what they are working on, what is in the current patch and what they expect to roll out in the next update WITH a timeframe of "this week". To put it simply almost everytime I log into Steam that game updates... But no word from the DayZ team. Just saying.
Now I know they have announcements on steam that they do update- but these announcements include 0 valuable information for the average gamer and instead include vague statements about how near they are to whatever they are working on. Their Development roadmap for this year is also not on target....it seems to me that the team's idea is to grab money and drag this out while grabbing more money from players with no real intent to actually complete this broken pos.
SO- If you are looking for a FPS with no point beyond that and or a snakeoil salesman's promise that it will get better, than this is the game for you.
Here is to hoping that as this game improves as it continues to be developed, I really wanted to play this but at this point it is a waste of my time.

Very frequently I get off on a game for dumbing down it's subject matter. It's usually some really old franchise that was amazing, yet the publisher feels it necessary to dumb it down to appeal to more people.
Borderlands 2 is the straight antithesis of this practice, and frankly I was so terrified of Borderlands 1 being dumbed down I was initially skeptical of this game. However, almost all parts of the original have been touched upon in some way.
For example, Borderlands's storyline was immediately renegated to the sidelines as your entire game focused on just doing meaningless quests and getting fancier weapons. In Borderlands 2, not only is the storyline apart of the forefront but the reaccuring characters from the original only seek to strengthen your faith it wont start sucking later. Not only that, but the primary selling point of the original game, namely it's randomly generating guns have also been touched up. In the original your guns while being varied usually had similar animations to each other or looked dissimmilar. Here all the guns look wildly different.
Moreover Gearbox heavily impressed me with this game with it's mass amount of just general better design. The series mascot Claptrap for instance is far better developed into a pseudo-antagonistic/joke character that remains consistantly relevant in the game. The level design is far more varied, especially as the game goes on. The character classes and their powers are more distinctive and further add variety to the game in subsequent playthroughs. Add to that the ability to customize your character's appearance and the reinclusion of Co-Op. It remains a highly impressive sequel I can't really find any flaws with.

In Borderlands 1, every manufacturer produced EVERY type of weapon.
In Borderlands 2, some manufacturers produce some types of weapons
In Borlderands 1, loot  drops from enemeis almost 75% of the time.
In Borderlands 2, loot drops from enemies seemingly 20% of the time.
In Borderlands 1, weapon stats were noticibly different from one another.
In Borderlands 2, weapon stats are slightly different from one another.
In Borderlands 1, Legendaries were possible to find without grinding.
In Borderlands 2, Legendaries are impossible to find without grinding.
While Borderlands 1 had Weapon Proficiencies, Borderlands 2 has Badass Rank.
Which is a brilliant idea, but it's unfortunate that in order to keep gaining Badass rank you have to make a new character and go through the whole storyline again.
Needless to say, I was content with Borderlands 2 when it was new, but disappointed with it now I'm unable to do anything I want without having to grind for items, hours on end.

Well. This will be my first review of any game that I've played. Also my favorite game. Then you may ask, "Well why are you not giving it a good review if it's your favorite game?". The reason is as follows. I am a veteran from the very first post of the DayZ mod on the Arma 2 game made by the same people, which led up to this release. The game was intense. Everywhere you went, it was kill or be killed. There was barely any friendlies. The game itself was STABLE (For the most part). They had more guns than you could ever imagine. 50+ Guns if not more. Different variations in scopes, weapons themselves, etc. It also had planes, cars, etc. Now they have very little variety. To be fair, I do like the gunplay in the DayZ standalone. It's beautiful. If you're now saying to yourself "This guy is wrong! He should know Arma 2 and developing a new game is really hard, and there is a difference between a military simulator and a survival game!" You may be right, but if I'm mistaken who doesn't love absolute variety of weapons, and cars, and etc.
Not to mention how buggy this damn game is. Zombies attacking through walls, zombies managing to teleport to you when you're in a place no-one else can get to. Zombies somehow walking through doors...You get the picture. Also several instances of me falling through a ♥♥♥♥ing building! How would you feel if you had a char that stayed alive for over a week suddenly dies from falling through a building?
Now I will go to my final point. The abuse of early access. I quit playing this game for a while, to return several months later to find not a single update had been put out. SEVERAL MONTHS? And not a single thing had been put out? Look at H1Z1, it was very overhyped but they pump out updates every month at least! Look at Rust, supposedly a easier game than DayZ has a very hard learning curve and pumps out 3-5 updates PER MONTH. They also have a smaller crew.
If you have stuck with me through this, I thank you. To be honest, as much as I am starting to hate the Dev team, I love this game. I loved the concept. It was this game and mod that spawned the following H1Z1, Rust, and alot of smaller ♥♥♥♥♥ier games with zombie survival. There is a reason this game isn't doing as well as those others. I will stay with this game until its end, as I came in with this idea, and I do plan to go out on this idea with my ship.
Regards, Alex.

Before I start this review, I want to be clear that I don't hate this game.  It is absurdly overhyped, and has a lot of flaws, but it still has some very cool concepts.
The combat system is interesting, if admittedly barebones.  As you're likely aware, it's a JRPG-type game that features a bullet hell-esque combat system mixed in.  However, as aforementioned it is rather barebones, having two "options" to defeat an opponent (I'll explain the quotation marks later).  The combat system is always the exact same battle, and can get incredibly grating as you are constantly attacked by enemies when walking around, leading to just running from battles in later runs.  For a JRPG, the inventory system is astonishingly lacking.  It's about as basic as you can get, having no real management aspect and only being able to use or drop items.  These items however, are incredibly important as they are your way to regenerate health, which is especially needed on pacifist runs and certain bosses during genocide.
This is the main problem I have with Undertale.  It has cool concepts that ultimately fall flat due to lacking any form of depth.  The inventory system barely exists, the characters have little to no actual depth and seemingly only exist to set up the next punch line and further the story.  Speaking of punch lines, Undertale is known for its humor which, likely all humor, will greatly depend on what you find funny.  It has a very "lolsorandom" vibe to it, targeting the tumblr demographic which really brought this game to notoriety.  While I didn't hate the humor, the most it did was solicit a solitary chuckle, which is very likely in part due to my sense of humor not matching up with the game's.
Now I'll get into the real meat of my criticism, the explanation behind the quotation marks.  The game, for all intents and purposes, is built around multiple runs and your decisions between them recurring and coming back to haunt you.  Once again, a very cool concept, but it suffers from the same problem as the rest of the game in that it lacks any real depth.  You see,
Before grabbing your pitchforks, allow me to explain.  The game is, quite frankly, a VN in disguise.  The game is separated into runs or, as they're known in VNs, "Routes".  The decisions in the game are based upon whether you want to kill an opponent or not, and they're not actually decisions because if you want to complete a specific route you have spare every enemy, kill every enemy, or, in the case of a neutral run, have an even mix of spared and killed enemies.  Not only that, but you essentially have to play the runs in the order of Neutral, Pacifist, then Genocide, removing what little choice you had left.  Failing to do so results in missing information, and, if you do a specific run first,
.
In order to adequately explain that last point I have to dive into spoilers for the Neutral and Genocide runs of the game, so if you wish to avoid spoilers please skip this section of the review.
Now I get to the point that will likely upset a lot of people, if they haven't already stopped reading this review.
You see, there is no depth to them.  With the exception of a few, every character is exactly how you imagine they are from their first line of dialog.  For all the character development the game attempts, mainly in the pacifist run, none of it amounts to anything as instead of actually using it to flesh out the character, like by giving them motivations, back stories, and personality traits beyond what exists in a twilight fan fiction, they instead use it to deliver yet another punch line.  Upon completion of the game, I don't understand anything about these characters beyond their basic personality traits.  There is no actual depth to them, and I could never sympathize with them because there weren't people (I realize they literally aren't people, but that's beside the point), they were just cardboard cutouts of character tropes used to deliver the next punch line and progress the plot.
I realize I've hated on this game a lot, but honestly it's because of the potential this game had.  It could have lived to the hype, even surpassed it, if everything that's here was fully realized.  The framework is here to create a masterpiece, it just was never finished.  The ultimate failure of this game is not fleshing anything out.  The characters have the writing to be incredible, but lack the personality.  The connections between runs are interesting and could have been incredibly emotionally potent, but they have no real effect on the game and fall flat.  The combat system shows promise, but lacks depth and it's in the game too much.  For everything the game does right, it manages to backpedal on it and not deliver.  While the game is by no means bad, it is most definitely a disappointment.  Not because of the insane amount of hype around it, but because of the potential it had and ultimately fails at.  Undertale's greatest failure isn't that it failed its community, but that it failed itself in not fully realizing what it could have been.
4/10

You may look at Rust and think its just a basic survival, multiplayer game. For the most part, you would be right. But boy, you are missing out if you haven't played Rust.
I am going to section this out to try make things easier.
RUST being made in Unity, definately feels like a Unity made game. Graphics are great, controlls are easy and familiar, gravity is perfect etc.
Although there is no storyline, you definately make your own story as you play. Playing RUST alone is no easy task, and I get bet you any money you will not enjoy soloing RUST. Your best bet is to either play it with friends, or try and join a Team or Clan. This makes for some fun social interaction, and a lot of ease on the mind when worrying if you will survive over night.
The game is pretty simple. Survive. It has a lot of characteristics of Minecraft. Cut wood from trees, mine stone from stone nodes, and build a house to survive. Though you are not trying to survive from creepers, instead you are trying to not get murdered, mugged and humiliated by other players areound the world. They will use C4 to blow up your house. They will use a bone knife made from your friends bones to stab you while you sleep. They will take your pants so you have to run around with your little johnson flapping around. But, when the tables turn, you can do the same back!
My overall review of RUST is that it is a great game. You get angry, happy, upset and excited all at the same time. You experience fear and joy in one action. Its wierdly satisfying. I would recommend this game to ANYONE who does not get too angry at a game.
I find this game to be extremely glitch low, which is a great plus
Remember. Your base WILL get Raided, no matter how good it is. So build it well, and make sure you have a backup plan. Learn from each experience and build better and better every time!

Rust is a mutiplayer survival crafting game, It's qutie an overdone subject in recent gaming, but Rust one of the best ones I've played. Between frequent updates, great graphics, and a rather friendly community (depending on server) it stands far above most other games in the crafting/survival community.
Pros +
• Fast gameplay ( you could have a pretty good base in about an hour or two i you know what you are doing )
• Air drops and the relatively new helicopter forces players to fight for the best loot
• Voice communication is distance based and anonymous
• NO ZOMBIES ( personally I feel that zombie survival is an much overdone topic in the survival genre)
• Naked guys guys killing each other
Cons -
• Not optimized very well at the moment, but it is still playable on low and mid-tier system
• Kids playing usually dont know how to communicate, resulting in them killing you on sight
• There are some glitches currently, but with update every month or so, they sould be fixed soon
• Gathering gets a little stale after awhile, but building quarries stops the “grind fest"
but overall Rust is an 9/10 (will be 10/10 as soon as glitches are fixed and optimizations take place)

I was sick to death of this game. I couldn't stand the fact that everybody and their mom was doing nothing on the internet anymore except talking relentlessly about it. It made me cringe on the inside every time I saw a picture of it in my Youtube suggestions. I wanted to punch a wall every time I saw a picture of a skeleton wearing a red scarf or a blue hoodie, with no corner of the internet appearing to be safe from them. I was apalled when I got that news that it won the Gamefaqs contest, despite going up against literally every other game in existence. I remember thinking to myself, surely, no game in the world could possibly be worth the excessive amount of hype this EarthBound-wannabe was getting.
Then I played it.

Yes the fandom is a bit toxic.
But the game is great.
I'm not usually one to be moved by a video game's story, but this was very well done.
Plus I'm not sure any harsh critics stopped to think "Hey, this was all (mostly) created by one guy with relatively little game making experience. This is a pretty fine job. He even wrote and performed the whole soundtrack which is very good."
I also want to say that I was adamantly against playing this game despite everyone telling me to. When I did play it, I found I liked it. And when I figured out what this game was all about after finishing it for the second time, I realized that you can't just play this a little bit to get the full experience.
This game is more than gameplay. It is more than good story. It is more than good characters.
This game gives us what a good game should always be about: A story that actually involves the player, not one that the player is merely a passenger for. That's what books and movies are for.
This game touched my mind and my concience in a way that no story has ever done to me.
That is why I think this game will be one that I personally will cherish for a long time.
EDIT: It's been a while since I reviewed this game. The community has calmed down. I still listen to this game's music. I still play it now and then. Good game, good soundtrack.

Undertale is an extremely short, linear game and it actively tries to discourage the player from continuing on after getting the "true" ending. This is a huge detriment to its oft-plaised replay value.
Most of the tiny details and jokes will affect you the first time but then lose their novelty once you come back. You may notice upon a second playthrough that the world isn't quite as big, detailed or lived-in as it first seemed, and everything now just seems like you've seen it already. That's why there's such a large effort to datamine the game dry: the amount of content in-game is exhausted relatively quickly and so players are driven to tamper with the game's files and examine every last line of dialogue in the script.
The art style-especially in regards to the game's monster characters- is unique, timeless and leaves a lot to the player's imagination. That so many people like to create fanart of Undertale's characters says a lot about the strength of its character design.
It's very probable that the game is just too corny and simple to strike a chord with most older players. Ideally, I'd like a world where most people find and play Undertale around preteen age, years later having the same nostalgia for the game as people today have for Earthbound.
Buy Undertale for your twelve year old. Or play it with your little sister or something.

Undertale is, as you probably already know, a curious game. It's difficult to describe what makes this game so worthwile without spoiling anything, but my best effort is separated by the different game aspects below.
Gameplay: Undertale is a puzzle-RPG, with a battle system that consists of moving a pixelated heart around to dodge. The system is reminiscent of Touhou, and you do not have to take damage on any given turn. The puzzles aren't anything new to people familiar with the genre, and are generally rather easy.
In a battle, the player is presented with four options: Fight, Act, Item, and Mercy. Fight is a standard attack with your equipped weapon, the item menu allows you to use anything from your inventory of up to eight items, and the option to flee is found the Mercy menu. This leaves the two more interesting options: Act and Spare, the latter of which is also found in the Mercy menu.
When a monster's name appears yellow, it means you can spare them and sacrifice your XP to end the battle without fighting. The main way to make a monster spare-able is by using the Act menu. Each monster requires a different non-violent method, which can make the battle experience much more enjoyable. There's often more than one method to spare an enemy, some of which can be highly amusing.
Graphics: The graphics, admittedly, are somewhat poor. The style is decent, and some of the enviorments are nice to look at, but the game's visuals overall aren't really up to classic standards.
Music: Composed by Toby Fox, Undertale has an unsurprisingly wonderful soundtrack in an 8-bit style. The music fits well into every area and battle, providing a strong sense of atmosphere. I highly recommend buying the game's full soundtrack, as it will both reap legal music for the buyer and support for Toby Fox. There's also many musical motifs, which can actually be seen as spoilers if one listens close enough.
Replayability: The replayability for this game is both high and low, for different reasons. There are multiple routes you can take in the game which drastically alter the experience and even tone of the game, and MANY secrets to discover. Despite this, the game also purposely deters you from playing again, which may be enough for some players to quit after their first few runs.
Story: There's absolutely no question that the plot of Undertale is its' selling point. The characters are easy to attach to due to their charm and depth, and it's difficult to take a completionist route simply due to the cruelty potential in the game. The morality system is an important one, as you must remember your consequences are final. Trust me, there's no undoing the greatest mistakes. Depending on your course of action, the game can range from a comedy to a tragedy to a horror. It's vital you go into the game with as little understanding of the plot as possible, but Undertale showcases one of the best storylines in any video game.
Basically, go buy the game right now. Despite easy puzzles, slightly wacky humour, and sub-standard graphics, the game is one of the best ones PCs have to offer, if not the best. I can highly recommend this game to the majority of people, and have done so, only to have them show a similar love for the game.

I was apalled when I got that news that it won the Gamefaqs contest, despite going up against literally every other game in existence. I remember thinking to myself, surely, no game in the world could possibly be worth the excessive amount of hype this EarthBound-wannabe was getting.
Then I played it.

Yes the fandom is a bit toxic.
But the game is great.
I'm not usually one to be moved by a video game's story, but this was very well done.
Plus I'm not sure any harsh critics stopped to think "Hey, this was all (mostly) created by one guy with relatively little game making experience. This is a pretty fine job. He even wrote and performed the whole soundtrack which is very good."
I also want to say that I was adamantly against playing this game despite everyone telling me to. When I did play it, I found I liked it. And when I figured out what this game was all about after finishing it for the second time, I realized that you can't just play this a little bit to get the full experience.
This game is more than gameplay. It is more than good story. It is more than good characters.
This game gives us what a good game should always be about: A story that actually involves the player, not one that the player is merely a passenger for. That's what books and movies are for.
This game touched my mind and my concience in a way that no story has ever done to me.
That is why I think this game will be one that I personally will cherish for a long time.
EDIT: It's been a while since I reviewed this game. The community has calmed down. I still listen to this game's music. I still play it now and then. Good game, good soundtrack.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

When I first played this game, I started out just like I was playing a traditional RPG...and soon realized that was a mistake.  I assumed you had to kill everything and grind XP like usual.  What I didn't assume was that this game would emotionally change my view of video game stories.  After killing a few of the main characters in the game I resolved to spare the lives of everyone I met...and did just that.  The ending of the Neutral route was amazing and completely surprising.  So I decided to achieve all 3 endings of the game.
On my 2nd playthrough I spared every single monster until I reached the end of the game.  After what seemed like one of the greatest game endings of all time, a single plot twist caught me by surprise.  I fell in love with a character I should hate, along with all of the other characters who were so wonderfully designed.  As the credits came to a close, I couldn't bring myself to do what I had promised to do, and complete a Genocide Run and 100% the game.
After a few days, however, my emotional bond with the characters had worn off enough that I decided to give the Genocide Run a try.  I made it about halfway through, when I reached an extremely difficult boss.  After several days attempting this battle, I began to question my motives.  "Why am I trying to kill all of these monsters?  Why am I trying to 100% this game when I already achieved a great ending to it?"  I quit playing the Genocide Run and haven't tried it since.
My favorite thing about this game, however, isn't the characters, or the dialogue, or even the game mechanics (although those are all astounding).  It's the soundtrack.  I have fallen in love with every single song from the game, and have become emotionally attached to each one, as they bring back wonderful memories and scenes from the game. It's hard for me to heap enough praise on BL2. This game demonstrates what is possible at the cutting edge of game design with a talented, large, dedicated team working in harmony. At first, the claustrophobic start makes the game look smaller than BL1...but, the writing, settings, scenarios, personalities, art, just keep coming. About L15 I became amazed at how much I had seen, how much creativity kept coming, not yet halfway through the game. My admiration went epic when I made through Bloodshot HQ and looked at a blast hole in the floor where an underground stream, rendered beautifully, ran over concrete, cobblestones below that, and beams and rebar all around the hole. Magnificent detail! Well done, artists. Beautiful!
Gameplay? Slick. Smart. Seamless. I play often with friends. (Co-op is easy and sharp.) Everything PC Gamer published about how the producers listened to the BL fans is all true. I have been further delighted how the setup of a shootout: geography, types of enemies, your character type and that of your friend(s), create radically different situations and appropriate tactics. You might use the same approach a couple of times and then next time you realize you'll never make it thinking one-size-fits all. When things change, you' must re-think. Very smart. The characters in BL2 vary radically in style, and re-spec-ing them changes their play dramatically.
There are many games-within-games in BL2. You can roll down the main quest, be completionist with side quests, or chase "challenges". Then, as the game spits out additional heads and skins, you'll enjoy playing dolls, setting up your favorite look. Then  there's the most famous bit: guns / guns / guns. The myriads of guns affect your character's power and play style as much as any of the elements I've mentioned so far, meaning the variety exponentially multiplies again. Finally, one aspect I love much better than MMOs -- I spent hundreds of hours in LOTRO (and before that DAOC, EQ2 and WoW) -- is that this game really creates the sense of epic power in your character as you advance in level. I never felt that way in LOTRO. If I take my L31 Siren through earlier campaigns, she moves through like Sheba the Destroyer. It's ... well ... epic.
My son, a game designer, asked about the intrusiveness of cut scenes. There are virtually none aside from the cute intro screens for the bosses and major characters. Those are always clever and mercifully brief. The in-game stories are moved forward by fragmentary recordings a la BL1 and System Shock. I found these to be engaging, especially as they let you know who Handsome Jack really is, and where his bloody footprints have been. And without doing any spoilers, I'll also say that BL2 isn't afraid to kill some of your favorites. Nuff said. By the way, there is variety in how personality stories are advanced, too. For example, Tiny Tina's sad history you will assemble from meeting her, her tea party, and very brief recordings from a much later adventure area you would not associate with her. By the time you get those, her tale becomes clear. Not to mention the photo of her with Roland on the table in her cave. Brilliant. When I finish the game, I'll invite Tiny Tina to be my adopted daughter, and I'll raise her so the only explosions she needs are for enjoyment. Tina may be my favorite character in any computer game ever. Wow.
In closing, BL2 is getting my new record for primary life stealer while being a fabulous context for co-op friendships and immersion. It is nothing short of brilliant, with the kind of scope that both Peter Jackson and Cecille B. DeMille would appreciate. I'd like to put it in a special gallery in a gaming museum and say, "This is what the art of gaming can achieve."

Undertale is a wonderfully presented and told game where your choices and actions matter and make changes both small and large in your playthroughs. I feel that it’s best to experience what I mean by this instead of reading about it. These consequences show how amazingly well thought out and written this game is.
I love the 8-bit graphic art style of the game and the character designs look great. The sound design is also well thought out and presented, for example the tone for text being written to the screen changes for some characters when they speak is a small difference but helps these characters to stand out. The great soundtrack also helps with that giving characters and locations recognisable themes.
What I like mechanically about this game is that you can complete it killing no-one, everyone, or any number in between. One of the most interesting aspects of the game is the ability to "act" as a option during combat. With this you can analyse, talk to, or act in a certain way towards the monster you are in combat with and if you act the right way you will be able to end the combat peacefully with "mercy", which is just your way of saying you don't want to fight anymore. This makes the game such an interesting experience that makes it stand out from other games, you need to survive attacks long enough to figure out the right way to "act" that lets you end the combat peacefully.
I have completed it twice now getting one of the neutral endings and the true pacifist one, and I definitely want to play multiple more times in order to get a different ending and see interaction changes. To me, this is a sign that Undertale is a fantastic game that on finishing it my desire is to play it again in different ways.

When I first played this game, I started out just like I was playing a traditional RPG...and soon realized that was a mistake.  I assumed you had to kill everything and grind XP like usual.  What I didn't assume was that this game would emotionally change my view of video game stories.  After killing a few of the main characters in the game I resolved to spare the lives of everyone I met...and did just that.  The ending of the Neutral route was amazing and completely surprising.  So I decided to achieve all 3 endings of the game.
On my 2nd playthrough I spared every single monster until I reached the end of the game.  After what seemed like one of the greatest game endings of all time, a single plot twist caught me by surprise.  I fell in love with a character I should hate, along with all of the other characters who were so wonderfully designed.  As the credits came to a close, I couldn't bring myself to do what I had promised to do, and complete a Genocide Run and 100% the game.
After a few days, however, my emotional bond with the characters had worn off enough that I decided to give the Genocide Run a try.  I made it about halfway through, when I reached an extremely difficult boss.  After several days attempting this battle, I began to question my motives.  "Why am I trying to kill all of these monsters?  Why am I trying to 100% this game when I already achieved a great ending to it?"  I quit playing the Genocide Run and haven't tried it since.
My favorite thing about this game, however, isn't the characters, or the dialogue, or even the game mechanics (although those are all astounding).  It's the soundtrack.  I have fallen in love with every single song from the game, and have become emotionally attached to each one, as they bring back wonderful memories and scenes from the game.  I have become obsessed with listening to the songs and covers of them on YouTube.
If you haven't played this game yet...DO IT.  I absolutely, highly recommend it as one of the best games I have ever played in my life.  I love the story, the songs, the people, the jokes, the mechanics, the gameplay, and I even love the tears that I shed playing through it.  Whatever you choose to do, whether you have a rad time, a sad time, or even a bad time, you won't regret buying this game.

DECENTLY LONG READ AHEAD: YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.
People say this game is bad, they're right and they're wrong. Don't let my hours fool you, I've had my fair share of DayZ Standalone for some time.  It states specifically in the game description that this game is in Alpha, so dont point fingers at the devs because your game experience wasn't as planned.
If your expecting a funny occurence that I've seen, you will get it at the end of this review. If you are looking for a decently crafted review, then by all means look on. If you're just going to thumbs down because you don't like text..well..there's a special place for you.
DayZ: A zombie survival MMO game. You are tossed on the beach of an island which you have no idea where anything is (Unless you've played before..). Your objective is simple and should be well known throughout any zombie game: Stay Alive. You are to search the environment for supplies to sustain yourself for as long as you plan on living, if you can't find any of these, you're as good as zombie bait.
Yes, this game does have bugs, occasionally if you get a vehicle your wheels will burst for some dumb reason, zombies will glitch through doors etc. etc, but as I said before the game is in Alpha and I have faith in the developers to fix these soon.
However if you do manage to keep yourself from getting any of those bad things to happen, then you're lucky. To a fault. If your hunger or the zombies don't kill you, the people wanting your supplies will. There are certain types of players you will run into, this one being one of the many: Bandits. You can't really distinguish this player from others unless they are well armed and have the best gear one can get, if you encounter these people the solution is simple, kill them before they kill you. I follow the shoot on sight guideline, so to a fault I'm considered a bandit. I give them a fair warning to back off, but if they press on, they die. If there is one thing this game has taught me,  don't trust your friends unless you're both outfitted with good gear. One of you will end up killing each other over a gun or a can of baked beans. Or they will just kill you for fun.
There are a ton of great things though. Rarely do bugs ever happen (Personal Experience) and depending on your server or server population, you won't run into many players. A good way to gear up is to join a low populated server and search everything until you're ready to go into online games. Good people are also common, they will save your skin or maybe drop you a few cans of food or a canteen or two. The game is fun if you know what your doing and getting into.
That's the end of the serious stuff, here is where the people wanting a quick or random laugh. I was running through Elektro and found a car. It ran and everything. I entered and began to drive forward until I heard some noise in the backround. This wasn't a zombie or anything, this was someone playing their boombox on max volume. I got out of the car and waited around the corner holding my Longhorn scoped pistol looking down the street. A few moments later someone came around blaring "Remember the Name" by Fort Minor with a decent lump of gear. I couldn't resist shooting this guy, so I took aim and fired. I killed him and looted his stuff. 10/10 I Don't Remember Your Name.
The rating I give the game thus far is a 8.3/10. It's worth the buy for something to do.

Undertale is an emotional roller-coster ride that plays with your emotions.
The game's tagline: A game where no one has to die, is strongly present thorught the game, encuraging one style of playthrough over another. While this deliberate pressuring seems a bit forced, and a bit overbearing, like a goat mother that wants what's best for you, I can forgive it, as this is Toby Fox's first game.
The characters of the game all have their own unique personalities, themes, and attacks.
Each boss character in the game is memorable. Each boss has their own gimmik as well. Some might have you just be persistant, others my actually change how the battle plays out as well.
Even the common monsters are memorable. Every monster has it's own style of attack, and personality. A personal favorate of mine, that made me laugh was the Tsunderplane. Anyone that is familiur to the term Tsundere will get it.
This game has memes, lots of them. There are even subtle refferences to other games, either in text, or musical form.
Chrono Trigger, Mother, Final Fantasy VI, and Super Metroid to name a few.
The graphics of the game may be simplistic, but it leaves the player to imagine what the world looks like. But even with the simplistic style, the game's graphical asthetic can look awesome at times.
Then there's the battle system. A unique spin on the traditional RPG. Oh, sure, you can just go kill everything, but that is a sure-fire way to HAVE A BAD TIME. Your game, your choice. But if all you do is attack, then you are missing out on a major machnic of the game's combat; ACTing. You can raise your stats, and lower the stats of your foes. You can even cause foes to let up on their attacks, making them slower, or even have them heal you!
I would love to see an acting system in future RPGs. It doesn't have to be all mercy-like, but being able to mess with the heads of your foes can be entertaining.
Also, the Music, is what brings the experience all together. Those emotional moments, tense moments, and unsettling moments wouldn't be without the musical score that Toby Fox created. For someone who self-taught themselves to compose music, they did a good job. Toby even takes a nod at classic Nintendo games, with reusing melodies in multiple tracks (Dogsong, for example, has it's melody used in many other tracks, give it a listen) Also the differnt choices in sound samples is interesting. From NES-Era Chiptunes, to SNES Era samples, some from Mother II, some from Final Fantasy and Chrono Trigger.
The final thing to mention is secrets; this game is full of them. However, if you are hyper-sensitive, you may never find them. As finding secrets involves playing this game, like a game. Resetting. saving in spicific spots, then re-loading without saving. Staning in a spicific spot, etc.
Heck, this game even has is't own Herobrine-like entity in it, kinda. Some may see it, others may not. It's appearence is random. But I heard that Time Traveling, can give you clues. I heard it's often reffered to as G-
Overall, it's friggen $10! It's not long, it has replayability (so long as you don't get too attatched to the game world), and is sure to be a delight. Unless you are some sort of cold, heartless, "human".
