There may be a few spoilers in the reveiw below, but i'll try not to touch on any major plot details.  That being said, there is one plot twist at the end, so if you have not yet gotten to the end, look for a WARNING: SPOILERS in all caps so you can skip ahead until its safe. If you're too scared to read below, just know that I think that this game is amazing and that I would recommend it.
Undertale has recently taken over the internet with countless videos and playthroughs exitsting on the internet. Of course, with all this attention, there are bound to be some haters. Some people say this game is overrated and its just a wanna-be Earthbound. However, I disagree. I beleive that this game is UNDERRATED. The game constantly breaks the fourth wall, but not in a way that we're used to. See, everyone know how RPGs works, but Undertale knows how gamers work. Most modern games focus on realism and violence as key (sometimes necessary) aspects of a game, but in Undertale you aren't forced to use violence. In fact, the endings where you kill are considered worse than the endings where you don't. Spoiler here, though you can skip if you haven't played yet, I won't judge) It also breaks the fouth in the very first minutes of the game. When players first start the game and meet flowey, they expects the diolouge with him to be the obligatory tutoriel at the beginning of every other game they have ever played, and it even starts out looking that way, until Flowey shares his "friendliness pellets".
I don't know one person who was not shocked and enraged when this happened, and rightly so. This is a huge example of how undertale knows how gamers works, instead of gamers knowing how Undertale works. (SPOILER WARNING OVER).  However Undertale doesn't use this as a feature to troll gamers, in fact, its quite the opposite. Undertale uses this to expand the gameplay and the story. And in doing so, it manages to pull the player into its world, and make them feeling they are acually there, and that there action have REAL consequences other than not getting the best ending. Its a level of investment into a game that I can't say I have felt towards a game in long time, if ever.
While we are on the topic of endings, Undertale has a LOT of endings. And it gets to the point where your actions in past playthrough impact what ending you get. It makes every playthrough feel new, even though you're just going through the same area's as last time. WARNING: SPOILERS APROACHING. If you have not gotten to the end then I suggest you run now. (Don't worry, I'll tell you when It's safe to come back). OK, so you'e gotten so close to the end that you can taste it, you can feel that there are just a few more rooms until the long-awaited final boss. But then, you come across sans, who tells you that all the EXP you've earned along the way - isn't experience points, and the LV you've gained isn't level. He says that they are acronyms for "execution points" and "level of violence" respectively. This was probably a shock to first-time players who had been used to getting EXP in other games, and did it in Undertale to get some more HP or to level up. What if they didn't realize you could spare Toriel and killed her on accident? Other games treat leveling up and EXP as GOOD things, so naturally you would think its a good thing in Undertale as well. But it isn't, so once people see this, most of the time they see the error in their ways and then try a pacifist run.
Its safe to start reading again is you left for the spoilers
But theres no need to worry, unlike in OTHER rpgs, a pacifist run does not mean that battles don't become fun. This is because instead of putting you in typical combat senarios, when its your opponents turn, instead of them slashing at you or something- the enemy sends a barrage of bullets at you, which you need to dodge. This allows the game to remain fun even when you're not fighting. Also, when doing attempting to spare a monster, it is essentialy a puzzle where you need to perform certain actions in certain orders, in order to make the enemy hesitant to fight you. It's definatly a fun alternative to slashing your oppenent until someone falls over.
So, you may be thinking, why? Why are so many people willing to spare every monster they find, even if it means the game gets harder. After all, it leaves you with only 20 HP and all the pacifist sidequests give you no direct bonus. I'll tell you why. It's the emotional bond that Undertale creates with the player and all the NPCs. Every character isn't just a 1 dimensional item or quest dispencer! Every character has a personality trait that makes them unique, and every character is quirky and fun. Even the NPCs that stand still and don't so anything have clever writing that makes you WANT to talk to NPCs, which is something not a lot of games can say. You want to see these characters develop, and see them acomplish their goal (which is also your goal) of escaping the underground. It's like I mentioned before with the whole "absorbing you into the game's world" thing. You feel like your actualy bonding with these characters, instead of helping the main character bond with other characters.
There's so many other things I could talk about as to why this game is great, but I think I'll leave it here. So if you haven't yet played this masterpiece, then do yourself a favor and play it. Its only 10 dollars and it will pay for itself in no time.
Also the soundtrack is really good.

Undertale is an emotional roller-coster ride that plays with your emotions.
The game's tagline: A game where no one has to die, is strongly present thorught the game, encuraging one style of playthrough over another. While this deliberate pressuring seems a bit forced, and a bit overbearing, like a goat mother that wants what's best for you, I can forgive it, as this is Toby Fox's first game.
The characters of the game all have their own unique personalities, themes, and attacks.
Each boss character in the game is memorable. Each boss has their own gimmik as well. Some might have you just be persistant, others my actually change how the battle plays out as well.
Even the common monsters are memorable. Every monster has it's own style of attack, and personality. A personal favorate of mine, that made me laugh was the Tsunderplane. Anyone that is familiur to the term Tsundere will get it.
This game has memes, lots of them. There are even subtle refferences to other games, either in text, or musical form.
Chrono Trigger, Mother, Final Fantasy VI, and Super Metroid to name a few.
The graphics of the game may be simplistic, but it leaves the player to imagine what the world looks like. But even with the simplistic style, the game's graphical asthetic can look awesome at times.
Then there's the battle system. A unique spin on the traditional RPG. Oh, sure, you can just go kill everything, but that is a sure-fire way to HAVE A BAD TIME. Your game, your choice. But if all you do is attack, then you are missing out on a major machnic of the game's combat; ACTing. You can raise your stats, and lower the stats of your foes. You can even cause foes to let up on their attacks, making them slower, or even have them heal you!
I would love to see an acting system in future RPGs. It doesn't have to be all mercy-like, but being able to mess with the heads of your foes can be entertaining.
Also, the Music, is what brings the experience all together. Those emotional moments, tense moments, and unsettling moments wouldn't be without the musical score that Toby Fox created. For someone who self-taught themselves to compose music, they did a good job. Toby even takes a nod at classic Nintendo games, with reusing melodies in multiple tracks (Dogsong, for example, has it's melody used in many other tracks, give it a listen) Also the differnt choices in sound samples is interesting. From NES-Era Chiptunes, to SNES Era samples, some from Mother II, some from Final Fantasy and Chrono Trigger.
The final thing to mention is secrets; this game is full of them. However, if you are hyper-sensitive, you may never find them. As finding secrets involves playing this game, like a game. Resetting. saving in spicific spots, then re-loading without saving. Staning in a spicific spot, etc.
Heck, this game even has is't own Herobrine-like entity in it, kinda. Some may see it, others may not. It's appearence is random. But I heard that Time Traveling, can give you clues. I heard it's often reffered to as G-
Overall, it's friggen $10! It's not long, it has replayability (so long as you don't get too attatched to the game world), and is sure to be a delight. Unless you are some sort of cold, heartless, "human".

Ohhh Undertale.
How do I say how it's made me feel without perverting your expectations in such a way as to forbid it clicking with you, the reader?
This game is special. Very special. Undertale stands alone.
This is a game that you should play with as little knowledge as possible. With that said, just know this:
There are three 'routes', 'paths', or ways to play this game. Each way changes the journey and ending, but also changes the way it will play out when you restart the game and play it again. Each time the overall story and vision of the game will become more clear to you.
The very fact that you can save or reset the game is both a mechanic and part of the storyline in this game. You will have to play through at least two times to get the true ending to the game.
My first playthrough I thought it was a good, unqiue game.
My second playthrough, I considered the game a masterpiece.
My third only cemented the conclusion of my second.
Thank you Toby Fox. Thank you so much!

There may be a few spoilers in the reveiw below, but i'll try not to touch on any major plot details.  That being said, there is one plot twist at the end, so if you have not yet gotten to the end, look for a WARNING: SPOILERS in all caps so you can skip ahead until its safe. If you're too scared to read below, just know that I think that this game is amazing and that I would recommend it.
Undertale has recently taken over the internet with countless videos and playthroughs exitsting on the internet. Of course, with all this attention, there are bound to be some haters. Some people say this game is overrated and its just a wanna-be Earthbound. However, I disagree. I beleive that this game is UNDERRATED. The game constantly breaks the fourth wall, but not in a way that we're used to. See, everyone know how RPGs works, but Undertale knows how gamers work. Most modern games focus on realism and violence as key (sometimes necessary) aspects of a game, but in Undertale you aren't forced to use violence. In fact, the endings where you kill are considered worse than the endings where you don't. Spoiler here, though you can skip if you haven't played yet, I won't judge) It also breaks the fouth in the very first minutes of the game. When players first start the game and meet flowey, they expects the diolouge with him to be the obligatory tutoriel at the beginning of every other game they have ever played, and it even starts out looking that way, until Flowey shares his "friendliness pellets".
I don't know one person who was not shocked and enraged when this happened, and rightly so. This is a huge example of how undertale knows how gamers works, instead of gamers knowing how Undertale works. (SPOILER WARNING OVER).  However Undertale doesn't use this as a feature to troll gamers, in fact, its quite the opposite. Undertale uses this to expand the gameplay and the story. And in doing so, it manages to pull the player into its world, and make them feeling they are acually there, and that there action have REAL consequences other than not getting the best ending. Its a level of investment into a game that I can't say I have felt towards a game in long time, if ever.
While we are on the topic of endings, Undertale has a LOT of endings. And it gets to the point where your actions in past playthrough impact what ending you get. It makes every playthrough feel new, even though you're just going through the same area's as last time. WARNING: SPOILERS APROACHING. If you have not gotten to the end then I suggest you run now. (Don't worry, I'll tell you when It's safe to come back). OK, so you'e gotten so close to the end that you can taste it, you can feel that there are just a few more rooms until the long-awaited final boss. But then, you come across sans, who tells you that all the EXP you've earned along the way - isn't experience points, and the LV you've gained isn't level. He says that they are acronyms for "execution points" and "level of violence" respectively. This was probably a shock to first-time players who had been used to getting EXP in other games, and did it in Undertale to get some more HP or to level up. What if they didn't realize you could spare Toriel and killed her on accident? Other games treat leveling up and EXP as GOOD things, so naturally you would think its a good thing in Undertale as well. But it isn't, so once people see this, most of the time they see the error in their ways and then try a pacifist run.
Its safe to start reading again is you left for the spoilers
But theres no need to worry, unlike in OTHER rpgs, a pacifist run does not mean that battles don't become fun. This is because instead of putting you in typical combat senarios, when its your opponents turn, instead of them slashing at you or something- the enemy sends a barrage of bullets at you, which you need to dodge. This allows the game to remain fun even when you're not fighting. Also, when doing attempting to spare a monster, it is essentialy a puzzle where you need to perform certain actions in certain orders, in order to make the enemy hesitant to fight you. It's definatly a fun alternative to slashing your oppenent until someone falls over.
So, you may be thinking, why? Why are so many people willing to spare every monster they find, even if it means the game gets harder. After all, it leaves you with only 20 HP and all the pacifist sidequests give you no direct bonus. I'll tell you why. It's the emotional bond that Undertale creates with the player and all the NPCs. Every character isn't just a 1 dimensional item or quest dispencer! Every character has a personality trait that makes them unique, and every character is quirky and fun. Even the NPCs that stand still and don't so anything have clever writing that makes you WANT to talk to NPCs, which is something not a lot of games can say. You want to see these characters develop, and see them acomplish their goal (which is also your goal) of escaping the underground. It's like I mentioned before with the whole "absorbing you into the game's world" thing. You feel like your actualy bonding with these characters, instead of helping the main character bond with other characters.
There's so many other things I could talk about as to why this game is great, but I think I'll leave it here. So if you haven't yet played this masterpiece, then do yourself a favor and play it. Its only 10 dollars and it will pay for itself in no time.
Also the soundtrack is really good.

My gripes aren't with the gameplay:
- I'll preface this by saying I knew what I was buying into. I had over 100 hours into the Mod. I knew it was early access, but seriously, my pacients has run thin.
- The core fundementals of the game aren't even apparent after 1 year of development. Zombies, thrist and huner are still broken. I mean, what are the developers doing with their time?
- Even though it's (EA) Early Access, the UI is vistually ugly and really cumbersome.
- Even before the game was released, the ARMAII Engine was out of date and clunky. Why they didn't build this on ARMAIII is beyond me. The players and zombies are too glitchy, so much to the point, that it can be confusing and gamebreaking. But I can't complain I knew this before I bought it.
My point is, the development time is far too slow. I know this is EA, and I can live with that, it's the time it's taking the developers to actually make progress with the game. Yes, I believe there's a few gameplay things that need to be changed (like making it slightly less realistic), but I haven't included it in this review becuase it's irrelevent - the premise is great and I loved the Mod. To reitterate, it's taking far too long to develop this game (especially after how much they initially made off sales). The porting to xBox is the final kick in the teeth.
Overall, DayZ was only ever popular as it was the first of the genere; it kicked off zombie survival. And that's it. Development is very, very slow and the core mechanics are broken. There are better Survival games out there with further development. Avoid this, I wouldn't be suprised to see this abandoned after some time. If you want to play DayZ, play the Mod.

It really pains me to gives this game a thumb down but here it goes...
Rust is no longer what it once was. The core mechanics of the game have shifted quite a bit. In it's current state there is little to no progression. The current meta is essentially a race to a radsuit, then you become rambo and prey on the weak.
Many items have become obsolete or are considered "Roleplayer" items. Rust used to feel like it was teeming with activity, now its an endless search for that fresh wipe... Which you will never have a hard time finding one because most servers besides the few officials (which are riddled with hackers) die within a day or 2 so the clear solution is to wipe to attract those server jumpers.
This game has immense potential but is falling very short of the mark. It actually often feels like the game is being reverse developed... Things that don't seem to need fixing are overhauled and reworked, while glaring issues get left by the wayside.
TLDR; Good game, however the current state of it is terrible. Avoid until things change... And when they do I will gladly update my review (3K hours is a lot to dump into one game, I love Rust and it hurts to see what it's become).

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I had a village once. With my friends and some people i met while playing in the server.
We had our own houses and we spent most of our time hunting for airdrops, i almost got killed by an naked in one of those hunts.
One day we found an airdrop near an very large base, little time after that, there was some dudes shooting at us.
My friend killed one of them with an revolver, he got some of the loot in the body and we ran away.
3 days later we had and oil jack and a quarry.
We were very happy, we had everything.
But our downfall was about to begin.
The dudes from the south showed up near the village one day ready to create trouble, they killed me first.
I warned the others and after some time we were ready to kill them.
We failed miserably.
they got out weapons and then they locked themselfes in a shack.
They were saying we were the bad guys (they were trying to make nakeds attack us) because they were outnumbered.
I had enough of those lies, i went to bed.
The next day there was a hole in the shack and they were gone.
We restarted the oil pump and the quarry.
We got new weapons and we were doing fine.
But then, when we were offline, a newbie friend that had a house in the village just taunted the entire server, saying that His house was "impossible to raid".
They raided his house and the founder's house too.
The founder was mad because of that, probably blaming us for all that happened.
He moved out of the village and i never saw him again.
I finally gave up.
and then everyone in the village stopped playing.
im glad it happened, now i know how to create an vilage and how to counter raids.
Rust isn't a game that you can understand fully by just watching videos, you have to do the mistakes yourself to learn how to do it right.

I walked into this game with not very many expectations, as I admittedly am not often one to play indie games, and got this game after seeing a short video on it and thinking it could be slightly enjoyable. What I ended up playing was easily the best game I have ever played. The best soundtrack I have ever heard in any game, with the track undertale being my favorite track at the moment. I listen to the soundtrack on a daily basis, and is some of my favorite music ever created. It captures the emotion and tone of the game perfectly.
It features a mind blowing story; there are so many cool theories behind certain parts of the game and so much hidden lore. The tone of this game is pitch perfect, seemingly managing to be both incredibly charming and unnerving at the same time. The characters are lovable, and all the characters, even the smaller side enemies, have their own unique stories and personality. The end game of undertale is incredibly exciting, and is done extremely well; saying any more than that would spoil it.  Absolutely everything you do has a point, and there are always consequences for your actions.
I am glad this obscure indie game got the attention it deserved by the internet, massive kudos to Toby Fox for making the only game I have ever played that I consider to be a 10/10 perfect game (Using gamemaker for crying out loud!). The absolute pinnacle of game storytelling and sound design.

claptrapという、タイヤの付いた皮肉屋で自虐屋で自信過剰なキューブによるものが大きい。

コンピューターにも嫌われるAI、拷問にも得意種目をもつ憎い余裕。
プレイヤーは彼に対し何度もmeleeボタンを押すのではないだろうか。
世界も負けじとイカれていて、どこもかしこも殺人が絶えない。

Finding guns is way to easy compared to actual survival games like DayZ or 7 Days to Die. The only probelm I have with pvp is that meds are extremeley broken, in games with similar health regen machanics you have to stop to use meds or at least slow down to a crawl, but in rust you can chase a guy for 10 min shooting him the whole time but because he has 20 meds it's nearly impossible to kill them unless you have really good aim and gun control. I also don't like to current focus on vehilces, I get that they have been hinted at and anticipated fro a long time but I would much rather Facepunch make Rust more of a survival game instead of add cars. But all those complaints are negligable in my overall opinon of the game as I have met to many good friends and had to many good experiences to not recommend this game. Also it's the most active early access game on steam so expect hours of content to be continually added.

It's funny how the original mod was
more polished and in a better state in 2012 than it's standalone mod offerring.
I've been playing since DayZ's inception. One week after the first public release of the original mod to be exact. I've had countless experiences with friends, across servers, timezones and custom maps. I've been there, done that. DayZ mod has always been a hassle to play. Both technical and mechanical reasons mostly hindering a enjoyable experience. The hook of a tension filled zombie survival simulator was indeed in there, but thanks to broken animations, cumbersome clunky controls and cumbersome inventory screens, that tension filled action was mostly obscured.
So when the prospect of a standalone game that fixed up the performace, animations, controls and focused exclusively on DayZ's strengths became present, I was pretty optimistic.
DayZ Standalone Released on 16th Dec 2013 to Steam's Early Access program. It's been nearly two years since that release date and the quality of the game has hardly improved, With a host of features that were present in the mod version either completely missing or off track for development. In the interim we've seen DayZ's original creator leave the development team, wipe his hands of the project and move onto greener pastures. We've seen dozens of comparable zombie sandbox survival comes come and go, And we've seen the development team languish in their efforts to try and improve the game. But what astounds me is that the experience is on the level from an ARMAII mod from Q2 2012. With hardly in improvements in this "Early Access" period.
Trying to get a fun, visceral experience out of DayZ standalone is like trying to get blood out of a stone. Good luck with that one.

Honestly? One of the best games I've ever played, period. It might even be my favorite now, and my previous favorites were hard to beat. I'm pretty picky when it comes to games and I can be quite critical, but I can find very little that's actually wrong with this game.
Incredible characters and writing with such unique flavor that it's hard not to fall in love with every single person in the game, even the bad guys.
It starts out as an RPG that you think is going to probably be decent, but it ends up being one of the most deeply emotional, philosophical and morality-challenging games ever.
An incredible soundtrack composed of over a hundred songs that are absolutely beautiful, and each one was thought out carefully to fit every scenario that they're played in.
The story is rich with thought, emotion, fantasy and pure love poured into its creation. Toby Fox did a phenomenal job with teaching through a video game, and he has pushed the limits on what a video game is meant to be.
I laughed so hard I was brought to tears. There were so many feels that I was brought to sadder tears. It's an emotional rollercoaster that grips onto you and wont let you go, and keeps you wanting to see what will happen next. Believe me when I say this: When you reach the end of the game, you might be rethinking your own world views in the real world.
This game is, quite simply, something special.

I had Hopes for this game, it claims to be a survival game just like Dayz, it has the same problems at the base level as Dayz so, here are the Big problems
1. Claims to be a survival game but is a glorified deathmatch:
Let me explain, Just like dayz this game is supposed to be a survival game, This means that this game should make you struggle to keep yourself alive, from the enviroment alone, it should make one struggle to find food and water, or it should make it hard to survive attacks from predators, MAKING PLAYERS THE ONLY THREAT IN A SURVIVAL GAME IS WRONG. Making players the only tangible threat is what breeds boredom which will lead to players killing on sight "KOS" just to make the game bareable, of course there are jerks that will kill you for no reason but a survival game should punish that heavily ideally by maintenance of weapons, Attracting very dangerous predators, or by using very Rare and precious supplies in the act of killing another player, a survival game should make one think, and plan ahead. It should reward players for socialising, or at the very least socialize in a meaningful way, Sadly, this won't happen very often with how the game is set up, ammo and guns are common as you can just craft them, you don't need to eat all that often and food and water are plentiful, the only saving grace would be if rust had some NPCs that would tear a player a new one if he or she wasn't careful which it doesn't, the addition of an LMG and Scope are just two instances of making it even easier to kill players and encouraging playstyles that may be detrimental to the enjoyment of others eg. killing freshspawns and rooftop camping.
2. The community:
Don't get me wrong, there are some people in this game that try to socialize and have reasons to kill or raid other reasons besides for stuff they don't need, they may set up shops but the vast majority are players who just draw♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on signs or mess with new players, griefing them, which is somewhat understandable as there is nothing to do unless one decides to mess with players, however the thing that makes the community unbearable is that a lot of players on this game have a laser focus on killing, alienating other players when someone thinks differently and when one tries to criticize the game, many of them will come up with weak excuses, the more immature ones will just claim that you're♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off because you got your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you.
3. Development:
I will not deny that the game is having features added to it, The foundation of the game either remains unchanged or had a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥patch to attempt to please those who were complaining about a feature that is a part of it's foundation, eg. Blueprint system and crafting times. The game also had a lot of updates that encouraged a deathmatch or team deathmatch mentality, The game is in development which means that the devs should focus on the foundation first and then build upon that foundation, while there is a foundation it is an incredibly shoddy one as evidenced by the complaints on the facepunch forums regarding blueprints, crafting times, and other issues located at the core of the gameplay. Facepunch has also been giving reasons to play as a group but giving very little incentives to have players socialize and form a group. It is obvious what FP is trying to do but FP does not know how to get the desired outcome.
Rust isn't a survival game in it's current state and unless facepunch step up it's game rust will never be a survival game, it is instead like Dayz in which it is mind numbingly boring unless you try to kill another player, there is little reason to socialize, there are no other real dangers besides other players, there is every reason to kill everyone you see.
TLDR; Rust is not a survival game in it's current state, it is a glorified deathmatch with crafting and building elements chucked in, if you want a hardcore survival experience then pass it up, if all you want to do is kill and grief other players than this game is for you!

It really pains me to gives this game a thumb down but here it goes...
Rust is no longer what it once was. The core mechanics of the game have shifted quite a bit. In it's current state there is little to no progression. The current meta is essentially a race to a radsuit, then you become rambo and prey on the weak.
Many items have become obsolete or are considered "Roleplayer" items. Rust used to feel like it was teeming with activity, now its an endless search for that fresh wipe... Which you will never have a hard time finding one because most servers besides the few officials (which are riddled with hackers) die within a day or 2 so the clear solution is to wipe to attract those server jumpers.
This game has immense potential but is falling very short of the mark. It actually often feels like the game is being reverse developed... Things that don't seem to need fixing are overhauled and reworked, while glaring issues get left by the wayside.
TLDR; Good game, however the current state of it is terrible. Avoid until things change... And when they do I will gladly update my review (3K hours is a lot to dump into one game, I love Rust and it hurts to see what it's become).

Compared to the first game, Borderlands 2 is an improvement on the concept the first was based on. Gun names VIA procedurally generated loot. are simpler easier to decipher and each manufacturer has a gimmick that makes using their guns worthwhile, as opposed to the first game's "strategy" of pick ATLAS and win.  Grenades, Shields, and Relics are also generated this time around. The story while laced with humorous references is interesting enough that it will keep your attention the first playthrough. The game can be replayed again in a mode that organically raises your lv. to 50 (as of the time of this review). The DLCS in addition to offering new side stories add raid-bosses.
I personally wouldn't recommend single player as I feel the co-op is the main draw of this game, but unless you can track down another person who is going into it blind or somebody who is willing to go your pace while you're getting your bearings You might need to play the game in single player before you try a co-op party.
This all being said your Co-op interactions are based entirely on the people you bring along. Keep this in mind when trying to play with friends, acquaintances and random matching’s.

What would it look like if Chrono Trigger, Earthbound, The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening, Off, and a bullet hell were all packed into one game?  You'd pretty much have Undertale.
Undertale is an RPG in the loosest terms, for it vastly breaks the norm within its own game category.  The combat is unique blend of turn-based fighting and bullet-hell style dodging, and the game tends to poke fun at classic JRPG elements more than follow them.  However, Undertale's greatest strength is in its character development and compelling narrative.  With constant decision-making, many fourth-wall-breaking scenarios, a flat-out GORGEOUS soundtrack, and tons of easter eggs, Undertale is the kind of game that requires more than one playthrough to fully enjoy it.
Just make sure you don't kill EVERYTHING on your first playthrough, or "You're going to have a bad time."

I picked up Undertale in the Christmas Steam sale, so I got aboard the Untertale train pretty late. I had managed to avoid spoilers, so I was playing through it blind, but most of the way through my first playthrough of this game, I have to say I thought the game was kind of overhyped.
Sure, the writing was pretty funny at times, and the music was good, and the schtick of an RPG where you could talk your way through everything instead of killing was different. But I didnt get the story, and some of the boss fights were just tedious, to the point where I was pretty close to just quitting instead of continuing to slog through dying over and over and over on the final boss.  When I finally got past him to the end of the game, it was with more of a sense of a grand FINALLY! than a grand finale.
But then, without putting spoilers in this review, lets just say that at that point, the pieces of the story that I had been missing finally clicked into place, and my appreciation of the narrative blossomed exponentially.
I no longer think this game is overhyped; in fact, I don't think it has gotten nearly as much attention as it deserves.
Since then, I have played through the entire thing, start to finish, two more times (something I have never wanted to do for any other RPG, at least without a couple years in between, and certainly not back-to-back-to-back playthroughs).  Each time, I have gleaned more hidden gems of absolutely marvelous storytelling (there is a metric buttload of secrets all over the place.)  The dialog and events are by turns charmingly funny and incredibly, heart-wrenchingly sad; no game has ever made me laugh OR cry as much as this one has.  I can't recommend it highly enough.

Not as good as borderlands 1.  They claim to have more guns than Borderlands 1, yet all they did was add more worthless guns. It ultimately comes down to the fact that they construct the guns based on level, rarity, stock, barrel, sight, 1 or 2 accessories, and I believe the receiver. You change those configurations around, and you get the different guns. However, with just those configurations, you wouldn't get "billions" of guns, or whatever their marketing schtick is. What they do, is add little changes like, "this gun has a different point or two of damage," or, "the fire rate is 5.6, instead of 5.5." These incremental changes, while fitting the term, "it's different", don't equal the kind of different the users are looking for. They're looking for fundamentally different guns, or an actual change in the effectiveness of the gun. Sure a gun that is the same, but does 5 more points of damage is an improvement, and will replace the prior gun, but if you're doing hundreds, or thousands of points of damage, it's not really the change I was looking for.
I'm a little disappointed with this sequel.  Sure it has some improvements, but not much.  I'm willing to sacrifice story for gameplay, and I'm sorry, but Borderlands 1 had better gameplay over Borderlands 2. Borderlands 2 has a lot of filler, very repetitive filler.
All the same, it does what it set out to do, which is being more borderlands. I will recommend it, but I still find Borderlands 1 to be superior. More guns, does not equal more excitement. It just means more worthless guns to slog through, and sell at the vendors. It means more disappointment as you find a bunch of rares and epics that really aren't something better than a gun you might have been using for a few levels, or hours/days. If nothing else, offer a way to turn in a bunch of older guns, to upgrade to something truly better. However, to a developer that wants to milk their franchise for all it's worth, it's better to rely on a random loot system, and bore your gamers out of their mind.
Borderlands the pre-sequel shows that more is not always better, and Borderlands 2 gets by on a thread. It's only an upgrade from Borderlands 1 in certain ways, but the gun system actually got worse.

Compared to the first game, Borderlands 2 is an improvement on the concept the first was based on. Gun names VIA procedurally generated loot. are simpler easier to decipher and each manufacturer has a gimmick that makes using their guns worthwhile, as opposed to the first game's "strategy" of pick ATLAS and win.  Grenades, Shields, and Relics are also generated this time around. The story while laced with humorous references is interesting enough that it will keep your attention the first playthrough. The game can be replayed again in a mode that organically raises your lv. to 50 (as of the time of this review). The DLCS in addition to offering new side stories add raid-bosses.
I personally wouldn't recommend single player as I feel the co-op is the main draw of this game, but unless you can track down another person who is going into it blind or somebody who is willing to go your pace while you're getting your bearings You might need to play the game in single player before you try a co-op party.
This all being said your Co-op interactions are based entirely on the people you bring along. Keep this in mind when trying to play with friends, acquaintances and random matching’s.

I've been one of these people who didn't instantly buy Undertale when its popularity was booming back in 2015. Now i've finally decided to give it a try after seeing so many reviews about it, and boy, have i not been disappointed.
Easily one of my favorite games now. On par with masterpieces like Witcher 3, even tho it does many things differently, which is mainly the reason why its such a great experience.
PROs:
- Very unique and fun combat system, actually requires some skill in certain parts of the game.
- Hilarious NPC's with their own backstories, motivations and more persoanlity than their counterparts in most AAA titles
- Despite being a rather short game, it offers a decent amount of replayability with 3 different endings and many references.
- The game remembers your actions and will rub it in your face, for example if you decided to reload an older save and  do something differently
- A great story that will draw you in if you allow it, with plot twist and many feels. OH THE FEELS!
- Awesome soundtrack
- Very good price
- Goat Mom
- Skeleton puns.
CONs:
- Only real con i could think of is that some people who are not amazing at playing games that require fast reactions and precision could find it difficult getting through certain fights in the game.
Conclusion: Don't judge a book by its cover! Considering the low price, i don't see any reason why someone shouldn't atleast give this game a try. If the NES-style graphics don't put you off, and you like quirky humor and well written, relatable  characters, you should really consider it.

If you are a Solo player and hate working with people DO NOT BUY THE GAME. They recently made a new system that rewards players with xp, allowing them to unlock survival itmes, which basically makes the game close to impossible to play solo. Clans Will DOMINATE smaller groups. If your looking for a game that does Xp systems and leveling correctly in a multiplayer style, check out 7 Days to Die. Their Xp system rewards the player on specific actions they do. For example If I craft alot of cloths my Tailoring skill will go up, allowing me to craft higher quality stuff. In Rust If I go afk and just mine trees with a click bot ill go high up on the leveling. Right now I just cant recommend the game because of how un freindly it is to solo people, and how great of a GPU it requires.

I was originally reluctant to play this game because of the unending amount of "retro" games coming out. However, after reading the ridiculously positive reviews, I decided to try out this game and boy, am I glad I did.
Sound
The amazing track to this game will be one of the first things you experience and is undeniably AMAZING. The 8-bit style music matches the look and feel of the game perfectly, and I found myself humming these tunes to myself when I wasn't marathonning this game.
Visuals
While the "retro" genre has been oversaturized in the steam market lately to cover a developer's laziness, this game just feels right. While calling the game "pretty" can be an overstatement at times, I never felt as if it was just a way to rush the game out to the market. Honestly, I feel as if a more modern graphical style would have taken some of the charm out of this game.
Plot (No Spoilers Here)
This game's plot is very basic at first, but really picks up about 3/4 of the way in. Its quirky and weird sense of humor genuinely made me laugh out loud several times and I couldn't bear to put this game down in its enamoring 9-hour-story. It's funny, it's creepy, it's sad, it's epic, and, it's fantastic.
Gameplay
Wow. Just wow. This game immediately shows its originality in its opening few minutes, and my jaw was on the floor from the sheer creativity of it all. The game has an interesting system of kill or spare, where you can kill an enemy or convince them to stop fighting you. Killing will give you EXP, while sparing gives you gold. However, when you kill an enemy, they're dead. Forever. To the point where random encounters will result in no enemies appearing because they are all dead. This original take on RPG syatems feels quite new, and you will find yourself questioning your morality several times throughout the story (if that is the path you choose to pursue). The puzzles here are not very challenging, but are generally accompanied wih hilarious dialogue, so you won't mind much. Overall, this game puts a new spin on an old genre that is extremely enjoyable.
Scores
Music-10/10
Visuals-9/10
Plot-10/10
Gameplay-10/10
While this may not be the longest or best looking game out there, it's fourth-wall breaking moments, multiple endings, and undeniable charm make it a MUST PLAY.
Overall score- 10/10

Even two SMGs with the same animation may have so different stats that they apply to different playstyles altogether. You will find favourites, especially amongst brands(I love the old-style semi automatic Jakob revolvers and TORGUE shotguns). The variety is also in the characters, with different playstyles being built with each skill you take or don't take. Want to be a phantom that dashes from enemy to enemy unseen? Do that! A pet master that makes everything go "BZZZZAP!"? Be my guest! Dual wield Machine gun and rocket launcher? Why not?! The game had me laughing out loud numerous times.It knows it's not a serious game and embraces the sillyness. First off, I need to make something clear: Undertale is more like a book. I'll explain why later.
Undertale looks to be a more traditional styled RPG game, at first glance. Y'know how those are: Adventure times, get money, get better loot, have a dedicated healer in your party, all that nonsense.
Within your first minute, though, the game throws a curveball at your expectations: Combat is more of a bullet-hell type, rather than swing-take damage-repeat until you need to heal. With enough practice you can get through the game without taking any sort of damage. Flowey tells you to catch the bullets- I MEAN 'friendliness pellets,' moments later a woman named Toriel comes and finishes the rest of the totorial.
This very first area of the game is where the main motto of the game can come into play: You don't have to kill anyone.
In this beginning level, you can easily get the feel of how the rest of the game will be, combat-wise anyway. You can use your 'Act' menu to lower the defenses of your enemies, or simply convince them not to fight you at all and leave with their lives. You can still kill them, but this is more of a timing thing instead of numbers: Hit the center dead on and you'll score critical hits all the time. Choose who to show Mercy and Spare, or choose who attack and kill.
And right here is where my first point comes into play. In terms of Gameplay, that's pretty much it. Covering the gameplay is a rather well written story that unfolds as you play. Not killing a thing can give you one ending, while killing Everything (good luck, by the way) will nab you another. Go down the middle road and kill some vegetables or an airplane with a crush on you, maybe a couple of dogs, and you will get a third ending.
I find the characters all to be rather interesting, as well, but I will only reveal the two most major ones from the beginning areas. From a lazy skeleton to a nerdy lizard-lady, all the way to a 19-year old catman working at a McDonalds joint, Every one of them is rather unique. Save for encounters, rarely will you ever meet the same character twice.
For a book, I say Undertale is worth $10. Hell, I've spent more on Magazines.
Personally, however, I don't think it deserves all the super high praise it's been getting, Sure, it's good, great even, but as a game I've played better. Best Indie Game of 2016 perhaps, but nowhere near GOTY material.
Music's pretty good, too.
Definitely worth it

What started out as a small project with large ambitions for developer Gearbox has quickly become a raging goliath in the open world fps genre series. WIth the 1st Borderlands being a runaway hit, many were left wondering if they could do it again. While the storyline in the original game was serviceable, players felt that it wasn't quite complementing the fun that is involved in acting the plot out. This time round however, Gearbox has hit overdrive and produced a story worthy of the Pandoran setting, which has become a one of the most interesting environments to explore for quite some time. With crazier characters, hilarious sidequests and references galore this plot will keep you immersed for the full duration. Be it hunting down the mutant ninja turtles to renaming the aptly named "Boner Fart" everyone will have a blast. Of course the "Gazillions guns" is back in the sequel with even more Gun vendors and types. Gearbox has refined, polished and enhanced everything that was so great in the 1st Borderlands game and added its signature style to boot. Multiplayer is fantastic and with an overhauled perk/skill tree you will be able to play your character HOW YOU WANT and make use of every single perk.

Borderlands 2 follows pretty much the same concept of the first game: Shoot and loot, quests, references and sillyness. But even though the game mechanics are practically the same, that doesn't mean things haven't improved.
The story to begin with, wraps up the events of the first Borderlands, something that was much needed and even improves it's value as kick starter of the story in Borderlands 2. It makes much more sense now, and Gearbox even bothered to explain what happends in the time gap between both games. The cartoonish aesthetics were kept and improved with excellent light effects and use of physX, without putting much pressure on the GPU and unlike BL1 with very few bugs. There's now much more loot, new elemental effects, less skill points, new shield effects, unlockable skins and heads, a new class, challenges, quests, and a vast etc. This means Borderlands 2 offers a much more unique experience than it's predecesor and countless hours of fun.
Now on the bad side: Slow start, the games takes about 2 or 3 hours to break in. Co-op is a must, in BL1 you could still take all bosses solo with a decent character, now all of the hardest bosses require you to play with a team which is fun, but frustrating if you don't have a good set of leveled up people in your friends list willing to play at any given time. Normal playthrough is also enhanced by playing with a friend.
All things considered, if you  liked BL1 you'll like BL2, and the corolary: 8,7/10.

"The friendly RPG where nobody has to die"
Yes, but everyone can die, and it's more fun that way. I know what you're thinking, these characters that I can spend time with, get to know them, become friends with them, but to that I say you are only seeing one side of the coin.
Now serious talk here, that is the general idea of the game, choice (albiet sometimes one sided) is something you either have or you don't (The hundreds of lpers that got coaxed into true pacifist) But the main focus is not the choices you make but the actions you take.
Each action has a silver lineing and a consequence, and because of this you're going to be replaying this game a lot, much like how Star Fox 64 had you replay for the stages on an alternate path, you replay Undertale for the reaction of the actions that you have taken upon the Underground. Like any Bethesda game though some of the characters will forget about what you've done via a handy reset (Worse case scenario, they have deja-vu)
Now Undertale is an RPG yes, but the combat is engaging much like the Mario and Luigi/Paper Mario series's. Player attacks are timing based and enemy attacks are bullet hell based and depending on actions you take might actually play out like a puzzle game, some monsters can actually change some of mechanics of this battle system.
Story and writing, let me ask you, did you enjoy Mother/Earthbound?
The writing can be both humorous, serious, sad, scary, puns, zany, meta, and dogs. Although one gripe I do have is the middleground final boss, not to spoil anything but the line between reality and fiction is blurred in this instance and it feels out of place because under normal circumstances, there wasn't a mention of reality in the slightest, unless if your the kind of person who changes his mind easily but I imagine most people would stay on the path they've chosen.
Music: Arf!
Overall I would say definately check it out, I mean it's kinda hard no to, the fandom is a god dang tsunami of widespread, The characters are interesting, the story is great, the split paths build replayability. It's a great time overall.

First off the dev team is terrible. All they do is add more and more items without working on core mechanics. Zombies and melee combat are still broken. Seems to me that may be something they would want to work on but apparently not.
As far as gameplay, DayZ is nothing but a CoD deathmatch on a large map. I'm aware tons of PvP morons are going to start their nonsense but the "player interactions" that are supposed to "make this game" dont even exist. It's just KoS all day every day. The ONLY time I've ever had fun was while playing on private PvE servers but the fun is still ruined because then there is no PvP what-so-ever.
A zombie survival game should be about finding other survivors and teaming up to first, combat the zombie threat, then, once your resources are to the point zombies are no longer a threat, combat the human threat, but EVERYONE just runs around KoSing. The players ruin this game just as much as the devs. Survival is NOT just about KoSing and IS about working together to overcome the odds.
If you want a TRUE zombie survival experience get 'Project Zomboid'. You can join a public server and find an equal amount of players that want to work with you to build a base and survive the ACTUAL zombie hordes; and players that want to kill and take your stuff. In PZ you can have a 'Walking Dead'-esque experience where you and some friends build your walled in community and go to war with another walled in community but NOT on DayZ. Would only recommend this game to people who want to play Call of Duty with broken zombies in the background.

Undertale is an odd game. On the surface you see nothing more than an ugly 8-bit world with the most basic of mechanics. This is one of the many, many surprises this game offered. When I first bought it, it was after my brother convincing me to spend the money, to which I though it wasn't worth. As I played a I found that I was horribly mistaken, this is a game that should be on everyone's list.
As you wander this small world (1 run through the game should take 6-8 hours) you come across some of the most lovable creatures. From comedians to gameshow host this game makes you learn to love everyone, even the supposed bad guy. This game defies every trope in modern games, and does it in a very special way. I am somewhat embarrased to say it, but I began to love the characters like real people, the game actually makes it feel like the consequences matter, that the world you wander is breathing behind your screen. Even when you quit the game it may react. All the pain, the laughs, the love, all of it I could feel from just a bunch of 8-bit sprites.
I don't want to spoil anything, as this is a game that should be played totally blind the first time, so I'll keep it short. Undertale is a game that, while short in length, will leave a lasting impact on the player. You may be a hero, a monster, or something inbetween, just expect a feels trip the whole way.

I have 144 hours in this game and I just cant recommend it to anyone in its current state.
I bought Dayz when it was first released and for a while me and my friends loved it.  We were able to look past the bugs and just enjoy it, after all it was in alpha so we forgave many of its short comings.  Dayz has now been in Alpha for a year and a half with no sign of getting out of it anytime soon (Possibly Q4 2015).  The Devs seem to have forgotten the basis of building anything, first start with a strong foundation then build up from there.  Dayz has a broken and cracked foundation and tons of features built on top of it.
What I mean by this is that Dayz's basic core mechanics are terrible.  The engine is horribly optimized which causes many players even with the beefiest rigs to have severe performance issues.  Zombies which are in many respects the core focus of the game are inherently broken. With glitchy moments, terrible A.I. and hit detection that seems to decide when it wants to work or not.  This is intensified with the devs decision to make the zombies fast which only serves to highlight how awful they are.  The menu system also decides when it wants to work as does the interaction system, many times you will find that even though an object is in plain sight and reach of your character the game just wont allow you to pick it up, and if you do you may not even be able to equip it.
The devs have not put the focus on fixing the basic gameplay mechanics, instead the continually keep adding "features" to a game that I would argue is broken at its core.  These "features" include picking berries, more cities and towns, more buildings, additional survival mechanics, vehicles, hunting, fishing, wildlife, and the list goes on.  All of this stuff sounds amazing but its really not because its build on a shoddy foundation.
This game really could have been great, and maybe one day it will be.  But for now just save your money.

In the mindset of an average RPG, entering this game was such a breath of fresh air. You could go the typical way and go genocidal. You could go through the game in a neutral fashion, doing either/or. Or you could even go merciful as shown in the trailer. The game has so many ending, so many pathways it can go. With that being said, the battles are so meaningful. Every. Single. One. Notice how in the average RPG, battles are just a way of grinding levels, adding playtime to the game as a whole, or just as an unnecessary obstacle (most of the time). In Undertale, every battle means something. You're meating a new creature from this whole new world beneath our feet. It makes everyone from the game feel...real. Everyone seems genuine, even the "enemies". It's a beautiful experience that came at a time where games aren't seen as an artistic medium. At a time where it may not be socially accepted by everybody. At a time where games strive to be taken seriously. Using fantastic writing, lovable characters, and unique game design, maybe it will be able to change minds.
In short, I ♥♥♥♥in' love this game. If you haven't tried it yet, play it or atleast watch a Let's play or two about it. The best mistake I've ever made. 10/10

This game is really quite interesting. Not in a good or bad way, just interesting. Let me some this game up in pro's and con's fashion:
Pros:
- Amazing, beautiful soundtrack
- Enticing story
- Cool looking enemies
- Unique battle system
- Some deep and rich characters
That's it for pros. Everything else in this game (so far) I see is simply not good. Let's start with the graphics; the most controversial topic of all. Let me just put this out for the world: I adore retro-style graphics. I live and breathe it, like games like Super Meat Boy. This game looks like it took NES graphics,♥♥♥♥♥♥on them, and chewed it up before being bought. It's not HD retro graphics! It looks like something the Atari 2600 would muster! Trust me, there ARE ways to make the game look good whilst maintaining retro graphics! But this was not the way to go. Bland colors, ugly sprites, etc.
Next, let's talk about characters. Everyone won't shut up about Sans and Papyrus, and it's easy to see why. They are quite funny. But, they are extremely under-developed and 1-Dimensional. You see no other side to these characters. What you see was what you get.
Next agenda is how people say how you can go about without violence. This speech mechanic is not at all what I thought it would be. It is literally an attack in how it functions. It's not say, in Mass Effect with your options to say something. No. You have a choice of attacks, and you keep using the same. one. over. and over. until the enemy "submits", or they literally die. It's literally calling an attack something else.
My third problem is the price. This game looks and feels like a homebrew or a video game done within a week. It should not be more than $5.00, much less $9.99. If it was significantly less cheaper, I wouldn't really be mad at it.
My next issue with the game is its clunkiness. I do love RPG's that have multiple routes branching out, but here, it kind of seems clunky. At no point in the game, do I ever have to return to a single point and it all feels linear, even when I have no idea where this place is in the map.
Finally, I hate how people compare this game to Earthbound. Sure, you have equipment. But is it shown on your character? Do you have any stats? Do you have any different attacks, or a magic attack? No. You can't have a party or a team.
Let's end this game on a positive note. I like the battle system, as long as people don't shove the whole "no violence" thing down my throat. It is very skill based, and it is quite fun to find the patterns in some attacks. Finally, the music. God this music feels like it belongs in some triple A title, not an indie game. It is so good that the soundtrack is better than the game itself.
CONCLUSION
Don't buy this game. Buy the soundtrack. If this game goes on sale for less than $5.00, then buy it.

Story:
Years ago, monsters and humans lived together in peace until humans waged war on the monsters. In the end, the monsters were imprisoned in a mountain. In 201X, a young child falls into a hole and lands into this kingdom of monsters called the Underground. A young child of ambiguous race and gender must then go through Underground and find a way home.
The story itself is very simple. It's more about you interacting with the world and all the characters around you and your actions affecting the world in small ways. The game is also very self aware that at least two or maybe three characters are aware that this is all a game. Its very meta and the meta stuff can be thought provoking. And yes I tried the No Mercy run, didn't finish it.
Gameplay:
I have no idea what genre this game is? Is it an RPG with it's battle system and level system? Is it one of those bullet hell games with the way you avoid enemy attacks? Is it a horror game with some the more unsettling parts of the game like the No Mercy run? But I think it might be an adventure game with its focus on puzzles and ability to get out of any situation in a number of ways from fighting to they give up, killing them or talk to them in a number of ways.
The battle system is one of the most interesting I've ever played with. You can either talk or fight with enemies and depending on what you doing, can kill them or spare them, with killing being the only way to get XP and LV. Every foe has their own attacks(Except Jerry but no one likes him) so every encounter is different and memorable, and like any good game, they add new ways to dodge attacks, sometimes just for a fight.
Now for moral thing and its pretty interesting. this game remembers everything you do from killing a boss to just meeting someone for the first time. And I mean everything. And if you think loading a previous save will undo a mistake you made...Hehe. Fat chance.
Presentation
The art is like Shovel Knight with it's retro art and music. While area's are pretty bland,all the people you meet there are very colorful. even the black and white sprites don't look too bad. At least they look better than the monster from FF13(I will never let that go.) The music is also very good with lots of goofy and awesome tracks and some brilliant boss themes. Though I will say there are a few tracks that are, shall we say, uncomfortable.
Conclusion
While it's not as great as everyone makes it out to be. It's still a very good game that's worthy of being the 2016 best game contender.

After over 150hrs of playing Rust I think I can finally rate this game. At the beginning let me say that I have mixed feelings about it.
It's indeed a rough gem at this state of development. Game has lots of things to offer, mechanics are very interesting and fresh, developers are updating this game very often and it has absolutely lovely bulidning mechanics. I kinda like the concept of loosing everything once your base has been raided, but I will get to that later .
Honestly, I can't wait to see final release of this game, because I'm sure it will be amazing and full of content. Devs are really spending our early access money on improvements - unlike devs of DayZ Standalone.
Unfortunately the game also has it flaws. At this state it's optimazed poorly, but I believe it will be changed.
Rust community is full of sick jerks and even if you would like to play it differently they just won't let you. Everbody is killing on sight and the best way of survivng in this game is to do the same thing.
In my first part of this review I said that this game has lovely buidling mechanics, which isn't exactly 100 % true. Although game gives you almost unlimited possiblities of building your base it fails to secure it. Toolbox system in my opinion is terrible as hell and the sphere around your base genrated by toolbox is glitchy. Let me give you an example - I had a base with 5 toolboxes around it and there was also one inside. Somehow people raided it using well-known tactic of buidling twig ramps right next to my buidling (even though toolbox was 1m away). It shouldn't be possible to do so, but somehow they did it and ignored toolbox.
What's the point of securing your base with walls and doors if players still can get inside by bypassing toolboxes with twigs and basically destroying walls?
Another thing is crafting system. In general it's a wonderful idea, but some object are too easy to obtain and others take too much time to craft and gain resources for them. Example: gun powder. It takes 10s to craft 10 pieces and you need thousands of them. Take too many time to craft such basic thing. Example2: buidling your base (even big ones!) is very easy while gathering resources and crafting C4 takes too much time and we all know that you need a few C4s to raid even a simple, small base.
Loot system - loot system is too boring in my opinion. Collecting just blueprints parts, blueprints and sometimes other rarely items is boring. There should be something more then mindless grinding.
Last thing that bothers me is Rust map. It's not too big and there aren't many things to see. Just few, small boring loot areas, empty forests and deserts ,some mountains. I would love to see some more complex structures.
Overall I can recommend this game, becuase I know it will be great once it's released. I have mixed feelings about it, but even right now despite all the things I mentioned as flaws it gives you a lot of fun even though it can frustrate you sometimes. Try it for yourself. It's cheap and it's on sale during each steam store sales.

A fantastic indie title. You can tell Toby Fox and friends really put their heart and soul into making this game great. The combat is unbeleivably fun, and turns turn-based combat on it's head by fusing in bullet-hell mechanics. Each and every character, even the ones in "random battles" have personalities and feelings. Things you may genuinely take into consideration when decided how to handle each battle. The game gives you the potential to completely destroy all who oppose you, or traipse through the game in attempt to harm as few people as possible. It is 100% possible to beat the game without killing anyone, you just have to think outside the box for some of them. There's also a fantasic story behind the game, that rounds off with an amazing ending. I would recommend anyone who thinks they're interested in the game to at least give it a try. Also the music is top-notch, totally original and fun to listen to music.

Story:
Years ago, monsters and humans lived together in peace until humans waged war on the monsters. In the end, the monsters were imprisoned in a mountain. In 201X, a young child falls into a hole and lands into this kingdom of monsters called the Underground. A young child of ambiguous race and gender must then go through Underground and find a way home.
The story itself is very simple. It's more about you interacting with the world and all the characters around you and your actions affecting the world in small ways. The game is also very self aware that at least two or maybe three characters are aware that this is all a game. Its very meta and the meta stuff can be thought provoking. And yes I tried the No Mercy run, didn't finish it.
Gameplay:
I have no idea what genre this game is? Is it an RPG with it's battle system and level system? Is it one of those bullet hell games with the way you avoid enemy attacks? Is it a horror game with some the more unsettling parts of the game like the No Mercy run? But I think it might be an adventure game with its focus on puzzles and ability to get out of any situation in a number of ways from fighting to they give up, killing them or talk to them in a number of ways.
The battle system is one of the most interesting I've ever played with. You can either talk or fight with enemies and depending on what you doing, can kill them or spare them, with killing being the only way to get XP and LV. Every foe has their own attacks(Except Jerry but no one likes him) so every encounter is different and memorable, and like any good game, they add new ways to dodge attacks, sometimes just for a fight.
Now for moral thing and its pretty interesting. this game remembers everything you do from killing a boss to just meeting someone for the first time. And I mean everything. And if you think loading a previous save will undo a mistake you made...Hehe. Fat chance.
Presentation
The art is like Shovel Knight with it's retro art and music. While area's are pretty bland,all the people you meet there are very colorful. even the black and white sprites don't look too bad. At least they look better than the monster from FF13(I will never let that go.) The music is also very good with lots of goofy and awesome tracks and some brilliant boss themes. Though I will say there are a few tracks that are, shall we say, uncomfortable.
Conclusion
While it's not as great as everyone makes it out to be. It's still a very good game that's worthy of being the 2016 best game contender.

I wasn't entriely sure what to expect when I began Undertale. When I first opened the store page, I shrugged it off as a minimilistic game that didn't seem very intriguing. Boy was I wrong. Do not let the 8-bit style deter you from playing this wonderful game. Where it lacks it art, it makes up for it (and then some) in story line and soundtrack. Undertale masterfully utilizes aspects of RPGs in a way that not only connects the player to  the story, but engrosses them into a world that seems all too realistic. Your decisions heavily weigh on the story you see, and each decision gives you a different experience. The characters are well written and allow the player to truly see the workings of the world the play in. I have never played a game with so much charm, and it is very easy to see all the time and effort put into such an amazing game.
Do yourself a favor and go into this blind.
You know indie dev's are becoming better than AAA studios when their games are experiences rather than games.

This is game is one of my favorites I've played in a while. The game is best experienced going in blind, so I won't spoil anything. The characters are great, and have a lot of personality. I like the enemy designs, too. While playing the game, you'll have the choice to spare monsters or kill them, so there are different endings depending on your actions. There is Pacifist, which means killing no monsters and making friends with the main cast, Neutral, which is killing 1 or more monsters, or killing no monsters but not befriending all of the cast, and Genocide, killing every monster. Also, You learn more about the world and characters during each playthrough, so I would try all of the endings. If you have ever played any of the games in the Mother/EarthBound series, this game is similar to those, except you have no party members or PSI. I do reccomend this game if you have the money for it. Also, the hardcore fanbase turn a lot of people away, but the fanbase doesn't affect the game.

This is legitimately one of the worst games on Steam. No, it isn't Slaughtering Grounds bad, nor is it anywhere close to most awful simulators. But, this game has fallen from grace so hard that it is virtually impossible to bring it back up. I got this game for full price at the time, I believe around $30(!). It took a great while to download, and while downloading I watched videos anticipating the standalone's greatness. I started the game. It crashed. Okay, that's all fine, it happens. I started it again, and got into the main menu this time around. I trogged around the main menu with my mouse jittering. The game started. My character was plopped down into a server with around 25 people. I hoped to find some others to converse with. I ran into a house finding: a red shirt, some boots, some gloves. Okay I'm all set for clothing now. I run into another building: A shirt, two jackets, some shoes. I guess I'm having bad luck. I run into another. Same stuff. I run into another. the same exact thing. On my way out, I hear a zombie near the house. I prone and attempt to sneak around this seemingly invisible zombie. It couldn't see me, I thought. Here is where the biggest problem with DayZ comes into play. The zombies are evil killing machines that will stop at nothing to kill you. I literally mean nothing. They go through doors, they climb up ladders, they sense your prescence from MILES away. Couple this with the fact that loot is almost impossible to find makes this one of the most frustrating games ever devised. The adverts said you could explore almost every building, but they didn't say that nine times out of ten, you find useless articles of clothing or a useless melee weapon that is nearly impossible to hit a zombie with unless you stand still and take hits.
The community isn't very forgiving either. It is a deathmatch fest and you are just a pawn in the upper tier's game. They own you, and you can't do anything about it. DayZ suffers from absolutely ridiculous AI that breaks physics achieve their goals, Improbable looting spawns, and absolutely no help from the community, save for a few special folks. On top of all of this, Dean Hall, the creator of DayZ, is moving on to a new game. This looks to be drawing near the end of the lifespan  for poor DayZ. With so little updates, and updates getting updates to them (that is incredibly dumb), DayZ will just become a garbage abandoned game project that will sadly never flourish. DayZ may be the only game I have played that actually made me want to play the original MOD more. With more and more titles on Steam becoming abandoned projects, it really is a shame to see DayZ fall so far from being one of the most loved mods to one of the most hated standalones.

Im a hardcore gamer and I believe im an honest person, so just listen to what I say because I have alot of experiance with this game, DONT BUY THIS UNLESS YOU HAVE MOUNTAINS OF PATIANTS FOR DEVELOPMENT! This game provided a plethora of hype in the first months of development, so dont be persuaded to buy this game purely on the basis that the review status is "Mostly Possitive" because the truth is, they arn't. Hear me out, and the thousands of dissapointed customers when we say "this game is dieing". Sure, there are still quite a few individuals who choose to actively emerse themselfs in DayZ but the game play is essentialy spawn, die (because you got a terrible spawn), spawn, run for 10 min to the nearest populated town for some action, die, spawn, loot aimlessly, die, repeat. My point is that there are quite a few mechanics to the game but there is a huge lack of dynamic. From what I've observed, those who purchase this game play for 2 hrs then almost inevitably rage quit because they can't handle the absolute chaos brought about by bugs and desync. The main problem is purely the sheer lack of TLC for this game.
The Life Story Of DayZ:
In the begining there were millions of people who couldn't wait to get their hands on a copy of standalone. Those who bought it were joyfully emersed in a world full of rife M4A1/Mosin fire, and bambi mortal combat madness. Then came the leaked items, promises, and bright vissions for the future. No one knew that the developers couldn't keep to their word. And so days, months, then years passed by and people waited, and waited, and waited until they could no longer wait for dire bug fixes and a myriad of vital features to keep the fan base interested. The game sank like a rock in a pond, all because the "reasonably pased development" was not so reasonable after all.
Please, don't waste your money on this game.
Months waithing for a single miniscule update is not worth your time, and its certainly not worth $34.99.

All you need to know is that this game has been abandoned by its creator.   The staff still working on this is updating minor graphics on buses, trucks and such.   The game has been in Alpha for a long time, and unfortnately shows no signs of ever emerging from it.   Once the cash stops flowing in from sales, buyers will no longer see any updates.    DayZ stand alone should serve as a prime example of how not to make a game, or treat your customers.
Want some examples?  Here is but a few...
It's a zombie survival game,  which has only a handful of zombies on a map so huge that its almost impossible to walk from one town to another without starving to death or dying of thirst.
Character creation is a joke, you can customize all you want, you wont actually get to see your character since most servers don't have 3rd person.
Optimization is non-existent,  even on medium settings you'll lag and jitter around, you'll swear your character has a neck injury the way you sluggishly turn from one side to another.   Perfect in a game where other players can snipe you to death in a single shot from half a town away.
The interface is about as friendly as the cockpit of a 747.   With keys that work or don't depending on their mood, and a customization menu that is sub-chaptered due to its length.
The world is rather good looking, but due to thirst and hunger, which is almost constant, you will suffer blurring.   Your framerate says you've got AA and high textures on, but everything looks as if you're staring at the world through a camera lens covered in vaseline.
Did I mention its a zombie survival game that doesn't have more than handful of zombies in it?
For those who played the Arma2 mod on which this standalone abortion of a game is based on, you will be sorely disappointed with this half hearted attempt to improve on the famous mod.   In truth this stand alone is quite a few steps back, wait....  its essentially the original mod rewinded back to its first release.   To charge money for this game is insulting, and there are very few titles on Steam today that stoop to the level of DayZ stand alone.
There are literally dozens of other titles that copy DayZ and do a much better job for a few dollars less.   After logging off over 7 months ago, I can honestly say that the game hasn't gotten any better, in fact it seems to perform worse than it did on release to open Alpha.
**TLDR Version**
AVOID this game,  look up other titles that are zombie survival, or check out other survival games in general since there are virtually no zombies in DAYZ.  This game is utter trash.
