I should probably write a review here considering this is now my favorite game ever.
The writing, story, and characters are all the best I've ever experienced. There is a ridiculous attention to detail in every single room, every single encounter. For the most part it's a humorous game, in the same vein as Earthbound, poking fun at your expectations, surprising you with creativity and depth that's completely lost in most all other games nowadays.
However, it's also an extremely serious game. I have never cried more than I have playing Undertale. I have never been mind♥♥♥♥ed more than I have playing Undertale. It will make you feel for these characters, for the world they are in. You have the power to take it all away just by resetting your save.
The soundtrack is probably never going to be topped. Simple as that. And I say that as a die-hard Grant Kirkhope fan. Click Clock Wood is a fantastic song, but it can't make me cry. From intense battles to emotional moments, the music is always perfect for the occasion, and there's so much of it.
The gameplay is also fantastic! One of the main selling points is that Instead of just attacking, you can befriend the monsters. Learn more about their personalities, make them happy. These aren't random goblins. These monsters have families, friends, feelings... Every fight is a puzzle to figure out what's needed to spare them. All the meanwhile, their attacks must be avoided in a bullet hell style of gameplay! I find it to be like the next step up from Action Commands in Paper Mario, or how in Mario & Luigi games you can avoid attacks entirely. This is definitely the most fun turn-based RPG I've ever played. I only wish there was a Hard Mode to turn on... But, a lot of players will probably find it hard enough already.
I can replay Undertale and still laugh and cry at so many parts, even when I know exactly what's coming. You can do new options and get completely new dialogue. You can do something completely stupid that you wouldn't think anyone would ever think to do, and get new dialogue for THAT too!
There is a reason everyone is talking about it. There is a reason it's been given multiple Game of the Year awards. And unlike Skyrim, it's actually not regurgitated garbage stretched out to fill 200 hours.
Well, I don't know if anyone will see this review or if it's any good or if it'll impact anyone choosing to buy it or not, but, there ya go.
10/10: You're gonna have a good time.
PS: This should win, like, five of the Steam awards.

Undertale is a strange beast of a game. It has attracted a HUGE following (noteably on tumblr, for better or for worse,) and many people claim that this came will CHANGE THE GAMING MARKET AS WE KNOW IT. Let's see why.
TL;DR: Game is an experience, for ten bucks, give it a try.
For one, let's look at the pros.
-Storyline with depth
-Multiple endings
-Clever programming
-Humor
-Nice pacing
-Lovable characters (Opinion, count this if you wish)
Now the cons.
-Frankly overused (in my personal opinion, count this as a con if you wish) retro style
-Unoriginal JRPG-styled game
-Difficult and near impossible fights without a guide
-Boring graphics
-So much walking and backtracking
-Annoying random encounters
-Easily dated in a few years
I honestly cant think of any more. I find that the game isn't bad, but it isn't great. I don't see why to obsess over it, and I definitely don't see why people think its so good. Maybe it's personal choice, but it's not creating or revolutionizing anything. It's like earthbound. It's an experience, not a game.  It's not anything new, other games have done the 'mess with your mind' stuff and breaking the fourth wall, other games have done the bullet dodging mechanic, and it's earthbound with a twist. However, it does it well. So should you buy it? Eeeeh. It's up to personal preference. But for the love of the lord, please don't contribute to the god-awful fandom. At least the god-awful part.

Although BL2 tries to sell itself as a carnage filled gun-fest, its true triumph is its artistically enthralling world jam-packed with wildly creative content. Torchlight II has more rewarding loot and Bulletstorm has better gunplay, but if you want a wacky trip across diverse and detailed environments full of quirky characters, distinct enemies, and a smorgasbord of loot, only BL2 will satisfy.

Just looking at the reviews, people are clearly upset about what this game has become. I never played rust when it was 'good' so I cannot really compare my experiences to anything, but the overall message I am getting from the community is "Rust sucks now!".
When I first started playing rust, not that long ago, I was completely fixated on it. I had no idea what to expect when I started it up, in all honesty, I assumed it would be just another minecraft clone. This game actually made me more nervous or happy or scared than any other game I played. Some of the most tense moments of the game were when I was crouching behind a rock in the dark and the pouring rain, naked and clutching a stone, listening to the sounds of gunfire and screams. I can still experience this feeling whenever I play it. The fact that there are huge, powerful clans who could kill you on sight makes the experience even more haunting and really ramps up the whole 'Post-apocalyptic' feel that the game is aiming for. Even making friends ingame is like some sort of TV drama, you never know if you will be the back-stabber or the 'back-stabbee' (Hopefully that makes some sort of grammatical sense).
I can see where people might be coming from with the negative reviews and you could say that I don't have enough experience with the game to make a valid point, Fair doo's, either way. But I still kinda like the game, regardless of it's flaws.
In conclusion, It gets a 8/10 from me, go get it when it’s on offer or something.

Borderlands is back and better than ever. Borderlands 2 comes and takes all the great mechanics and ideas from Borderlands 1 and makes it even better than before. Tons of new loot, new quests, new characters, better graphics, better optimizing, and a far better story makes this one of my favorite games ever. The game takes place on Pandora again but a fella by the name of Handsome Jack has taken over and is drilling his way to another vault and you have to beat him to it. The characters from the previous game come in and you get to meet up with all of them. Jokes from other games and internet are common in this game and humor is laugh out loud funny frequently. The amazing CL4 TP (also known as Clap Trap!) unit is back and funnier than ever. The shooting in this game feels fantastic and the loot is awesome. You can get loot from finishing missions or just killing enemies and finding chests. The graphics and art style is really nice and the optimization is fantastic. The only thing that isn't very good about graphics/optimization is that the PhysX isn't very good and it murders the frame rate. Just disable it on any system. Only thing that was really nice about it was some of the blood, which just looked cartoony. The sound effects were really great and the voice acting was good. The storyline will take you over 10 hours if you just rush right through it as a gunzerker (other classes take longer from what I am reading). I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys good FPS and RPG games. 97/100

Undertale is a strange beast.
At its core, it's an RPG mixed with a bullet hell game with some puzzle elements. The thing is, neither style of game that is represented in this game feel spectacularely amazing, there's tons of other games that nail the core gameplay of these genre a lot better. It's the mix of these genres that make this game feel interesting. Also, Undertale adds it's own little twists.
The RPG-Part plays as you'd expect. You walk around, randomly encounter enemies and can then choose between multiple interactions. Either attack head-on, leading to a simple, timed button press, use items or flee.
What Undertale adds to this formula is a way to talk enemies out of fighting. Not only is this very amusing, it adds a sort of puzzle element to every fight.
The "Defense-part" of the fight is where the bullet hell style gameplay comes in. Instead of just watching an animation of your character getting attacked, you instead have the ability to dodge the attacks of your enemies. Each type of enemy has a bullet hell pattern unique to that character and I must say, some encounters are pretty damn creative.
All of this combined makes for a much more interesting RPG experience, as it makes combat a lot more active than passive.
However I would argue that the bread and butter of this game is its characters and the dialogues you can have with them. Not only is it entertaining, it can also be touching at times, which is something I didn't really expect, judging by the simplistic artstyle of this game.
Sparing enemies in combat can also open up even more dialogue, which is why I definitly recommend this sort of playstyle. All in all, it made me want to spend more time exploring the world of this game which, in scope, isn't all that big but the varied cast of this game makes up for it.
However here in lies one of the flaws of Undertale. Direct combat is just...really boring. I started off doing a neutral run of the game but then switched to doing a pacifist run because it just lead to way more interesting gameplay. And I get it, it ties in with the whole theme and I guess also message of the game, but still. It just makes me not even consider combat as an option of playing through the game simply because it's an uninteresting mechanic. Which kinda sucks since it is a requirement to do so if you want to experience every ending.
I still highly recommend this game, as it is truely something special. It's really hard to describe in just text form so really, go ahead and try it for yourself.

My favorite game of all time will always be Undertale, even with a small amount of play hours and that it is not replayable, the story (in which you can choose your own path) is the best story in a video game that I have ever experienced or ever will hope to experience. This games storyline can expose who you are as a person, and in some cases, help change and form that person. There are 3 different ways to play Undertale, Genocide, where you kill everyone, Regular, where you spare some and kill some, and Peaceful, where you have to strive to not kill ANYONE or it reverts back to Regular and you can’t get the special ending that is just touching. By the way it is really hard not to kill anyone, but one of the mechanics is to try and talk it out, instead of attack. It’s such a great mechanic and makes up a massive part of the game. It was made by 1 person over the course of 13 years in Game Maker studio and is the best game I have ever played. The density of awesome per minute is infinite! Highly recommended, if you have any time on your hands play this, even if it doesn't seem like your type of game. Just sit down and play for half an hour, and I promise you will not regret it.

Seriously, though, this is really one of the better games I've played. I care most about Story, Atmosphere, and Characters, and this game pulls each of those off with flying colors. Characters are the especially strong point, with characters that you really get to know and love. The best thing of all, though, is how to even leave alive the characters that can become your friends is a choice that you make. You could kill everyone here, which somehow makes your friendships that much more beautiful.
The game also tries to subvert what we expect out of video games, from the "tutorial" to Determination. Personally, I could've used more of this, since you still end up as the powerful person who pulls out their desired ending through pure force of will and character. Not everything can or should be Noir, though.
All in all, this really is an amazing game. The graphics aren't much and the gameplay isn't a focus, but the game itself perfectly wraps together every aspect of itself into a beautifully cohesive whole that nicely balances humor and staggering despair.
Go play it. You won't regret it.

[SUPER SUBJECTIVE, PERSONAL REVIEW ALERT]
I know people are looking for objective reasons to why games are good or not, and i couldn't fulfill that need, thus, this banner.
It's really hard to find the right words to describe this game. A big part of why this is my favorite game now, is personal. I always liked retro games, partly because i didn't have a choice. I didn't and don't have the best pc available... Far from it in fact, most of my computers couldn't even run the newest games on the lowest settings.
But besides personal biases, this game is masterfully crafted, and the attention to detail is truly astonishing. The story is a great meta-commentary on RPGs and gaming in general, messing with the players head in a number of ways. But it doesn't devolve into a joke and memfest of 4th wall breaking, the game has it's humor, wich i again found really good, and laughed my♥♥♥♥♥off multiple times, but it got a broad range of emotions out of me, from tear-shattering laughter, to the edge of crying. It builds a cast ofreally strong and interesting, diverse characters, who you (or at least i) couldn't help, but get closely attached. And don't even get me started on the soundtrack... I listen to it on a daily baisis for almost 2 weeks now.
You may have noticed, that i haven't touched on the story. That's because (as many have stated before me) saying even a  word about the story. would spoil part of the experience, you have to experience it yourself. I don't know how did i avoid being spoiled, or even hearing about the game for months after release, but even if you are spoiled, it's worth it for the ride. This review turned out much more personal, than i originally wanted it to be, but i couldn't stop myself, this game touched me like no game has ever have. After each playtrough i looked at a completely different perspective at the characters, and the world. There are no more words for my amazement for Toby Fox's masterpiece, just these words: Please, do yourself a favor, and play this game.

Undertale is a strange beast.
At its core, it's an RPG mixed with a bullet hell game with some puzzle elements. The thing is, neither style of game that is represented in this game feel spectacularely amazing, there's tons of other games that nail the core gameplay of these genre a lot better. It's the mix of these genres that make this game feel interesting. Also, Undertale adds it's own little twists.
The RPG-Part plays as you'd expect. You walk around, randomly encounter enemies and can then choose between multiple interactions. Either attack head-on, leading to a simple, timed button press, use items or flee.
What Undertale adds to this formula is a way to talk enemies out of fighting. Not only is this very amusing, it adds a sort of puzzle element to every fight.
The "Defense-part" of the fight is where the bullet hell style gameplay comes in. Instead of just watching an animation of your character getting attacked, you instead have the ability to dodge the attacks of your enemies. Each type of enemy has a bullet hell pattern unique to that character and I must say, some encounters are pretty damn creative.
All of this combined makes for a much more interesting RPG experience, as it makes combat a lot more active than passive.
However I would argue that the bread and butter of this game is its characters and the dialogues you can have with them. Not only is it entertaining, it can also be touching at times, which is something I didn't really expect, judging by the simplistic artstyle of this game.
Sparing enemies in combat can also open up even more dialogue, which is why I definitly recommend this sort of playstyle. All in all, it made me want to spend more time exploring the world of this game which, in scope, isn't all that big but the varied cast of this game makes up for it.
However here in lies one of the flaws of Undertale. Direct combat is just...really boring. I started off doing a neutral run of the game but then switched to doing a pacifist run because it just lead to way more interesting gameplay. And I get it, it ties in with the whole theme and I guess also message of the game, but still. It just makes me not even consider combat as an option of playing through the game simply because it's an uninteresting mechanic. Which kinda sucks since it is a requirement to do so if you want to experience every ending.
I still highly recommend this game, as it is truely something special. It's really hard to describe in just text form so really, go ahead and try it for yourself.

Seriously, though, this is really one of the better games I've played. I care most about Story, Atmosphere, and Characters, and this game pulls each of those off with flying colors. Characters are the especially strong point, with characters that you really get to know and love. The best thing of all, though, is how to even leave alive the characters that can become your friends is a choice that you make. You could kill everyone here, which somehow makes your friendships that much more beautiful.
The game also tries to subvert what we expect out of video games, from the "tutorial" to Determination. Personally, I could've used more of this, since you still end up as the powerful person who pulls out their desired ending through pure force of will and character. Not everything can or should be Noir, though.
All in all, this really is an amazing game. The graphics aren't much and the gameplay isn't a focus, but the game itself perfectly wraps together every aspect of itself into a beautifully cohesive whole that nicely balances humor and staggering despair.
Go play it. You won't regret it.

[SUPER SUBJECTIVE, PERSONAL REVIEW ALERT]
I know people are looking for objective reasons to why games are good or not, and i couldn't fulfill that need, thus, this banner.
It's really hard to find the right words to describe this game. A big part of why this is my favorite game now, is personal. I always liked retro games, partly because i didn't have a choice. I didn't and don't have the best pc available... Far from it in fact, most of my computers couldn't even run the newest games on the lowest settings.
But besides personal biases, this game is masterfully crafted, and the attention to detail is truly astonishing. The story is a great meta-commentary on RPGs and gaming in general, messing with the players head in a number of ways. But it doesn't devolve into a joke and memfest of 4th wall breaking, the game has it's humor, wich i again found really good, and laughed my♥♥♥♥♥off multiple times, but it got a broad range of emotions out of me, from tear-shattering laughter, to the edge of crying. It builds a cast ofreally strong and interesting, diverse characters, who you (or at least i) couldn't help, but get closely attached. And don't even get me started on the soundtrack... I listen to it on a daily baisis for almost 2 weeks now.
You may have noticed, that i haven't touched on the story. That's because (as many have stated before me) saying even a  word about the story. would spoil part of the experience, you have to experience it yourself. I don't know how did i avoid being spoiled, or even hearing about the game for months after release, but even if you are spoiled, it's worth it for the ride. This review turned out much more personal, than i originally wanted it to be, but i couldn't stop myself, this game touched me like no game has ever have. After each playtrough i looked at a completely different perspective at the characters, and the world. There are no more words for my amazement for Toby Fox's masterpiece, just these words: Please, do yourself a favor, and play this game.

This game is a blast. It has had optimization issues which makes running it on high end PCs near impossible for some people, but other than that this game is basically flawless.
You start off as a random naked man with a rock and a torch, starving and dehydrated, trying to fight off bears, wolves, and the your inevitable execution by your fellow players. This game is extremely harsh and unforgiving, you die, and you lose everything you worked for. If you are the kind of person who doesn't enjoy hardcore experiences then this game isn't for you. It's a game of chance - you die and lose it all, but when? There's a million ways to die and one of them will catch up to you no matter how good you are.
Most of the negative reviews of this game are by people who are upset that their fellow players don't bend over to accomodate them. I've always been able to find and make new friends, meet friendly survivors and so on, even on the most crowded public servers. Rust is a dog eat dog world. 90% of the people you meet will try to kill you upon seeing you, but that other 10% will spend what little life they have with you until the bears catch up. Constantly being in fear of someone wearing military fatigues armed with an LMG and high explosives is part of the thrill of the game. If you can't hide or armor your base, then you deserve to get raided, leaving your safety to a straw shack in the middle of a pasture is no one's fault but yours.
I'd give this game a 9/10. It's come a long way since legacy started and is only going to get better as time goes on.

This game has things going for it -- an innovative combat system, the choice to kill or spare every monster you encounter, and a meta-game that has a suprising and interesting effect on the game.
The problem with the game is that it is BORING.
The "puzzles" are trivial and just tedious to get through.  The boss fights start out fun, but quickly get boring and repetitive because it can take 10-20 rounds to win.  There is very little variety to the boss fight mechanics, either spam fight or spam spare until you win.  The first time you figure out how to spare a new monster is fun, but then each subsequent encounter is tedious.
With all of the glowing positive reviews, I was expecting this game to be one of those that I will want to stay up late or skip work to play.  Just the opposite, however; I cannot bring myself to play this game more even if I have nothing else to do.  Most of the time, it is just not fun.

Now I know this game is called overrated occaisonally, and I can see where it's coming from. I don't agree with that opinion AT ALL, however. This is one of the best games I've ever played, and at forst, I could BARELY TELL WHY. And then I realized:This game is absolutely amazing. The soundtrack is great, the combat is unique and challenging ((at times)), the boss fights all have unique properties, and the game certainly has an interesting sense of humor, certainly bringing a skeleTON of laughs. But above all that, it was the emotional attachement to the characters as you play the game as a pacifist. At first, this game had just been a suggestion from a friend, and I knew very little about the game. The trailer does NOT do this game's slay/spare system justice. It doesn't tell about how the bosses and overall story will change. !!(Spoilers for a quick sec)!! At first, I was convinced I couldn't save Toriel, and I was forced to kill her. As I saw her tumble into dust and saw her heart break, I felt as if something had socked me in the chest. Then, I discovered you COULD save her, and I reset the game and did so; however, this game does not let you forget your sins. Flowey reminded me that I HAD murdered her, but this incedent made me realize how strongly the game made feel for a character, despite having them on screen for less than half an hour. And I knew from that moment on, a genocide run would be impossible.
Bottom line: GET THIS GAME.

Given the incredible praise Undertale receives it's easy to dismiss this game as an overrated indie darling which players just love because it's got a couple of funny characters. But by the time you've bought it, played it through and seen the True Pacifist Ending... You will understand just why it gets its rave reviews.
I'd compare this game favourably to Earthbound, in that it's a slightly quirky RPG... But at the same time it's sort of a deconstruction of the RPG genre and of video games in general. I'm not personally keen on traditional RPGs like Final Fantasy and Chrono Trigger, but this game I found very interesting. It's got the humour and writing of the aforementioned Earthbound with a bit of Persona mixed in there, the you-have-to-know-exactly-what-to-do-to-get-the-best-ending factor of Mass Effect 2, music reminiscent of old RPGs like Final Fantasy and Pokémon and an original, gripping story which does its best to reel you in, so much so that its fishing pole ends up deep inside your throat. It also breaks the fourth wall very frequently, but never, it seems, in a cliché or overused way, with fourth wall breaks doing everything from affecting gameplay to affecting the entire game as a whole.
The story revolves around a small child who, by accident, falls down a hole in a mountain and finds themselves in the World of Monsters. This is just the first step on an incredibly weird journey, which progresses differently depending on the protagonist's actions. The game heavily recommends you don't play this game like a traditional RPG, and if you do you will be chastised. Continuing such pursuits will set you on a dark and dangerous path of death and destruction, or rather, that's what you'll leave in your wake. On the other hand, if you take the game's advice and elect not to kill everything, sparing your enemies and finding alternate means to resolve conflicts, you'll find that the game becomes less of an RPG and more of role-playing puzzler as you try and work out what placates each of the game's monsters, meet a host of weird and wacky characters to befriend and ultimately reach your end goal - but what is that goal, exactly? That's for you to discover. The puzzles aren't overly original at times but they still provide enough enjoyment to make it worthwhile.
The combat is also an interesting spin on the old RPG formula. It takes the form of short bullet-hell sequences which see you dodging attacks thrown at you by your enemies. As a result the game distances itself further from the traditional RPG, making the combat much more interesting for players who opt to take the "pacifist" route by giving them something to actually do, the feeling that they are playing an actual game rather than just watch streams of text telling them that an enemy has taken a chunk of their health whilst they try and placate the enemy.
It helps not to see this game as an RPG in the traditional sense, more as a deconstruction and even an affectionate (on occasion) parody of the genre - and yet, at the same time mixing in the fantastic story, likeable cast of characters (Papyrus, a determined skeleton with a fascination with puzzles and spaghetti, and Undyne, a hotheaded, aquatic warrior who can never turn down a challenge, are my personal favourites)
As for the music, at times it's unremarkable and not really very memorable, but at other times it is spot on. When it needs to it can be riveting and rhythmic, creepy and unsettling, or warm and heartfelt, alongside a range of other emotions. It's certainly one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard in a game.
There isn't really much to criticise other than the game's encroaching strictness. If you slip up once, then you've messed up your entire game. And the game remembers EVERYTHING. Even if you reset, the game remembers.  Additionally, if, as above, you play it like you would a traditional RPG, then the game will NEVER forgive you. You'll have the bad ending as a permanent smudge on your record, and no matter what, you can't wipe the blood off your hands. While this does serve as an interesting incentive to get things right, it causes unnecessary tension at times. Very often I found myself worrying that I'd missed something or done something wrong, and it alienates players who know nothing of the game who might well end up "doing it wrong" on their first go. Also, some of the enemies in the game don't seem to be as creative as others in terms of their design or writing - for instance the "tsunderplane" which is just a tsundere aeroplane. That's just kind of weird, not funny or unique. Even some of the main characters fall victim to this - Sans and Papyrus the skeletons are obviously named for the fonts their dialogue is presented in. Occasionally the game also draws on Internet culture for its humour and inspiration, which at times is quite clever (like having one of the characters being a closet otaku and using anime as their basis for their knowledge of humanity), but at other times seemed to me to be a bit of a cop-out.
Overall, Undertale is amazing in terms of gameplay and story, unique in its gameplay and execution and is overall a fantastic experience, albeit one that requires some dedication. It's like a spiritual successor to EarthBound, with a similar charm, art style and wit, whilst also tossing in some interesting new mechanics and features which future games will likely try to emulate. It's probably not for everybody, but even so this comes with my very high recommendations and a solid score of 9/10.

Even if you play on pubs though, the game is worthwhile. The post-apocalyptic atmosphere, the survival aspect - and what I know is the direction of the ultimate game - are very fun. And BTW if you have a comp that can deal with the graphics on high - it IS absolutely beautiful.
Make sure to get out of the cities that you hear the most about. Explore the streams, find the hidden cemeteries grown over in the wilderness, and scour the ruins around Chernarus. I've yet to get bored.

Yes, this is Diablo with guns, but simply describing it doesn't do it justice.  It is an excellently executed first person shooter with oodles of customization and personality.  What really sets this game apart, though, is the writing.  The characters are well developed and make you love or hate them appropriately.  They are not afraid to hurt you in the story.  They aren't afraid to make permanent consequences that you will have to deal with which is something most games don't do or don't do in a way that comes across as emotionally effective.  Single-player is OK, but it shines multiplayer.  Find a buddy and keep a character levelling with them.  The first playthrough is challenging-ish.  The second one is a beast and really fun.  I cannot recommend this game enough.

Borderlands 2 is a blast in co-op, and an improvement over its predecessor in almost every way, but still retains that lonely, barren feeling when played solo.  Missions and environments are more varied and interesting; classes, skill trees and weapons are more fun; PC-specific improvements including adjustable FOV, better gamepad compatibility etc. Vanilla vs vanilla it decimates the original Borderlands.
There isn't as much enemy variety as I would've liked and, while the environments are more varied, they're still mostly limited to inherently barren environments (ice, desert, wastelands).  I would've liked to see more lush environments but perhaps this is being/will be addressed in the DLC.  There are minor bugs like your loot falling through the earth along with real problems such as inventory space being extremely limited, considering it's a loot game.  In spite of this, the game is polished and solid all the way through.
One of the top quality games of the year; got the nasty taste of Diablo 3 out of my mouth. Highly recommended if you plan on co-op.

Very punishing group-based survival FPS game which relies on basebuilding. The graphics are good and the building mechanics work well. Getting 60 fps may be hard sometimes which does not help with the competitive gunplay. The gunplay takes time to master, there aren't a lot of different guns but they are all quite different. This is probably a disadvantage because when you finally - after a lot of hard work - get a good gun you will quickly lose it because you suck at it. Don't even think about playing alone unless you are on a small freshly blueprint-wiped server. Even then, prepare to have your♥♥♥♥♥kicked and lose everything you own.
[TL:DR]
When starting out, what you can gather and build on your own in 2 hours, you can do in 15 minutes with a group. And time is of the essence because every minute someone can pass by and shoot you to pieces while you are gathering or building. You do need to gather a lot of resources, obviously this goes a lot faster with more people. With some friends around you will also have a lot more protection. Just because of this i don't recommend this game when you want to play alone. You will lose. Everything. Again. And again.
There is no lack of players. Since many people keep playing this game i guess there must be something rewarding in avenging your earlier failures onto innocent, usually naked others. Unfortunately, unless you have a good group, being able to kill people who are not naked takes too long to accomplish. Don't think you can go and make some friends in-game. Everyone is extremely hostile and backstabbing. Even so, if you bought this game and don't have anyone to play with, i recommend you to try to find some other players to team up with anyway. Try the chat, try other places like Steam groups, forums, reddit, etc. It will be hard, but easier and ultimately more efficient and rewarding than trying to survive on your own.
Playing with a group is much more rewarding because you will have an advantage over the many players who try to play alone. With some luck, and a lot of blood sweat and tears you will be able to have a great time. However even here the game can be relentless. I was with a group on a freshly wiped server. We played for 2 days, created a large 'secure' castle with a 'secure' loot room, killed some people, got lots of loot. Was fun for while it lasted. Came back on day 3, the loot room was completely robbed empty. It was either cheats or luck that allowed them to find out loot room.♥♥♥♥♥♥happens. But this was the third time in a week that a new base of ours was raided empty. One of our other bases was completely taken over, all the armoured doors removed and replaced. No one wanted to continue playing after that.
Rust can be fun when you are playing for a short time with a friend or two, preying on the weak until a stronger person or group steals everything you have. You will get tired of and even angry at the extremely punishing experience.
Recommended for playing with a large group (several experienced people online at any given time), building an extremely secure base (there is no overkill when it comes to security in Rust), and pwning because together you are Alpha and Omega.
I'd love to see different factions in this game that will benefit from working together so that even newbies and solo players have a reasonably safe place to settle. Or a karma system that will provide penalties to the strongest and most evil of players. Get negative karma when you kill and loot someone, and extra when its your own faction or someone who is not carrying a weapon. Being able to spot evil players from a distance and get extra positive karma when you kill them. Etc. This game really has a lot of potential but needs careful balancing of forces. The upcoming update will revamp the XP and Crafting system which may lead to some more balanced gameplay.
[ /TL:DR]
To enjoy playing Rust for a longer period of time you really need the advantage of larger and better numbers and better gear. Getting the gear is so hard that you also need friends for that. However the community is incredibly hostile and finding friends in the game is really hard. You will need to play a lot and lose a lot before you can grow strong enough to have some proper fun. The best moments are when you kill people while you have a disadvantage, when you really feel like you were smarter or more skilled than your opponent. Or when you actually get to defend your base or fight to get in other bases. But these moments are very rare. Overall i can not recommend this game because it relies on group play too much and at the same time does not facilitate group play in any way.
Note there are community servers that are smaller and have other restrictions or types of gameplay that could improve your single player experience but since they are unreliable my recommendation is for the base game as it stands in Early Access.

This game is a blast. It has had optimization issues which makes running it on high end PCs near impossible for some people, but other than that this game is basically flawless.
You start off as a random naked man with a rock and a torch, starving and dehydrated, trying to fight off bears, wolves, and the your inevitable execution by your fellow players. This game is extremely harsh and unforgiving, you die, and you lose everything you worked for. If you are the kind of person who doesn't enjoy hardcore experiences then this game isn't for you. It's a game of chance - you die and lose it all, but when? There's a million ways to die and one of them will catch up to you no matter how good you are.
Most of the negative reviews of this game are by people who are upset that their fellow players don't bend over to accomodate them. I've always been able to find and make new friends, meet friendly survivors and so on, even on the most crowded public servers. Rust is a dog eat dog world. 90% of the people you meet will try to kill you upon seeing you, but that other 10% will spend what little life they have with you until the bears catch up. Constantly being in fear of someone wearing military fatigues armed with an LMG and high explosives is part of the thrill of the game. If you can't hide or armor your base, then you deserve to get raided, leaving your safety to a straw shack in the middle of a pasture is no one's fault but yours.
I'd give this game a 9/10. It's come a long way since legacy started and is only going to get better as time goes on.

Rust is at its heart, a game of its time. It follows the trope of 'survival sandbox game with multiplayer' pretty to-the-letter. I have heard this game referred to as an 'Online ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ry simulator', and I feel that this descriptor captures the game perfectly.
The largest emphasis is on survival type gameplay; you start out with bare-bones equipment and work your way up what is basically a survivalist tech-tree to get better items to improve your survivability. At the very least, gameplay wise the survival gameplay is great. You can really enjoy the crafting and you get a great sense of progression. I felt that this was the 'enjoyable' segment of the game and this kept me playing for as long as I did. The idea behind the game is good, the gameplay is decent, at least, that is until you meet other people.
I would not recommend this game whatsoever. I would not wish this game upon my worst enemy. This game is able to make any person a misanthropist; it will make you despise your fellow human being and realise that the internet is a horribly toxic and disgusting place. This game is 'internet-to-the-nth-degree', and you will want to shower after a session from the vile and horrible people you will meet while playing; by this point, it's just a hate-filled troll fest.
The game is great in ideas and gameplay, but horrible in execution. Until measures are taken to reduce the toxicity, which I don't believe will ever happen (as the game has been in alpha plenty long enough to have had this addressed), I would not just 'not recommend' this game, but I also actively believe this is a game that should never have been made. It doesn't fill any niche that DayZ didn't already fill, and it just stands there as a monument to everything bad in the gaming world today.
This game is part of the reason people still don't take gaming seriously as a form of media, and I despise and loathe that it is so popular, and that I have to give this game a bad review.
To sum up quite simply; the fairly-decent survival gameplay of Rust simply isn't worth dealing with the toxic fanbase that populates it.

Undertale is one of those games that comes along once in a blue moon and stirs something deep down within a person that  we try a great deal to keep burried.
It's a game that's hyper self-aware and is filled with humor from start to finish.  It doesn't take much to realize that the game is playing a hilariously cruel and kind joke on you, the player, by having you go through it in whichever fashion you choose.  It neither rewards you for choices nor punishes you for them, the consequencesf your choices are completely up to you.
Timewise expect to spend ~ 6 hours for a full playthrough.  That may not seem like a lot, but it's deceptively short and you will want to play it at least one more time to reap everything this game has to offer.
The soundtrack is fantastic and really brings back some memories, tying old nostalgia to modern day melodies is something that has been very well done and there's not a moment in playing the game that the music does not sound appropriet.
I've only invested about sixteen hours into the game but looking back and knowing what I know now I would have no issue with paying much more for the experience and joy this game has brought me.

At this time, you are likely reading this review because the hype you heard: friends saying to buy and play it, or you saw some videos or neat music on Youtube.
Don't let aparent overexcited hype dissuade you from the game. $10US is cheap for what it offers, easilly enough to make your own judgment. If your friends feel as strongly they might have offered to buy the game for you.
As a retro style game it makes good use out of the graphics of the age. The music while sounding much like the 16-bit music it's trying to emulate is very catchy and has already spawned many remixes of the themes on Youtube. The box 'Combat' system is interesting and often enough surprising to keep you on your toes. There are many Easter eggs and side bits are numerous and often require different playthroughs to see them. Battles change on depending on your playstle; you might fight one monster one way, or another by a different path.
The characters are interesting, often endearing. They react to how you play the game; even the random NPCs you meet have different reactions based on how the game progresses. The humor is goofy at times, but still quite amusing. The story is well written and easilly captures people's heartstrings depending on your emotional investment in the game.
I highly recommend taking the chance and play without any spoilers or guides just for the fun of it on your first playthrough. My hat is off to Toby Fox on the depth placed into this game. I hope to see more from him.

At this time, you are likely reading this review because the hype you heard: friends saying to buy and play it, or you saw some videos or neat music on Youtube.
Don't let aparent overexcited hype dissuade you from the game. $10US is cheap for what it offers, easilly enough to make your own judgment. If your friends feel as strongly they might have offered to buy the game for you.
As a retro style game it makes good use out of the graphics of the age. The music while sounding much like the 16-bit music it's trying to emulate is very catchy and has already spawned many remixes of the themes on Youtube. The box 'Combat' system is interesting and often enough surprising to keep you on your toes. There are many Easter eggs and side bits are numerous and often require different playthroughs to see them. Battles change on depending on your playstle; you might fight one monster one way, or another by a different path.
The characters are interesting, often endearing. They react to how you play the game; even the random NPCs you meet have different reactions based on how the game progresses. The humor is goofy at times, but still quite amusing. The story is well written and easilly captures people's heartstrings depending on your emotional investment in the game.
I highly recommend taking the chance and play without any spoilers or guides just for the fun of it on your first playthrough. My hat is off to Toby Fox on the depth placed into this game. I hope to see more from him.

1: Get a weapon
2: Gather Materials
3: Put Down a Base
4: Secure the Base
Etc...
Rust was probably one of the most intense games I have ever gotten into and I don't regret it at all. If you choose to buy this game watch your back.

Incredibly glitchy, and game will be in beta for the next decade before being replaced with something new.
Fast, persistent, and almost invincible zombies.
Gameplay suffers from the same bugs as all ARMA titles. Glitchy and frustratingly sluggish controls. Delays in online interactions make they gameplay frustrating.
Extremely difficult to find guns, ammo, meds, food, etc.
Online gameplay system tries to achieve realism, but due to the way they implement online interaction it creates an aggressive PVP openworld. There is no benefit for working together with other player. The best thing you can do is kill them and take their gear. There is no system that rewards cooperation like in real life because the gameplay does not allow for persistent items and constructive unions between players.
Players log off (its a video game after all) and login at different times later. The game does not account for this, and there is no way to continue working with people as you would in real life. Therefore the game system creates an environment where players have no choice but to promote PVP violence and murder to attain assets in the game. The world is just to big and gear to hard to come by. It would be realistic and funner if people were playing 24/7. Its not when everyone can log off and become disconnected unable to reach fellow players for hours later. How is that realistic?
After a while playing this game gets very repetitious boring.
A PVP open map like DayZ would be great if the map was smaller so players can gear up, interact with players, and die several times in a single playing session.
I love these large realistic maps. But it does not work well with the way the game play style. It makes the game frustrating and boring. Wondering for hours leaves little else to do beside attack other players before logging off.
There are many more open world FPS games out there that do what DayZ is trying to do so much better (IMHO). Many are in beta but I think they pull off rewarding cooperation. And that is an element totally absent in DayZ. And something that would be very realisitc to include in a zombie apolocolypse? I mean in real life who wouldn't work together to survive?

Very punishing group-based survival FPS game which relies on basebuilding. The graphics are good and the building mechanics work well. Getting 60 fps may be hard sometimes which does not help with the competitive gunplay. The gunplay takes time to master, there aren't a lot of different guns but they are all quite different. This is probably a disadvantage because when you finally - after a lot of hard work - get a good gun you will quickly lose it because you suck at it. Don't even think about playing alone unless you are on a small freshly blueprint-wiped server. Even then, prepare to have your♥♥♥♥♥kicked and lose everything you own.
[TL:DR]
When starting out, what you can gather and build on your own in 2 hours, you can do in 15 minutes with a group. And time is of the essence because every minute someone can pass by and shoot you to pieces while you are gathering or building. You do need to gather a lot of resources, obviously this goes a lot faster with more people. With some friends around you will also have a lot more protection. Just because of this i don't recommend this game when you want to play alone. You will lose. Everything. Again. And again.
There is no lack of players. Since many people keep playing this game i guess there must be something rewarding in avenging your earlier failures onto innocent, usually naked others. Unfortunately, unless you have a good group, being able to kill people who are not naked takes too long to accomplish. Don't think you can go and make some friends in-game. Everyone is extremely hostile and backstabbing. Even so, if you bought this game and don't have anyone to play with, i recommend you to try to find some other players to team up with anyway. Try the chat, try other places like Steam groups, forums, reddit, etc. It will be hard, but easier and ultimately more efficient and rewarding than trying to survive on your own.
Playing with a group is much more rewarding because you will have an advantage over the many players who try to play alone. With some luck, and a lot of blood sweat and tears you will be able to have a great time. However even here the game can be relentless. I was with a group on a freshly wiped server. We played for 2 days, created a large 'secure' castle with a 'secure' loot room, killed some people, got lots of loot. Was fun for while it lasted. Came back on day 3, the loot room was completely robbed empty. It was either cheats or luck that allowed them to find out loot room.♥♥♥♥♥♥happens. But this was the third time in a week that a new base of ours was raided empty. One of our other bases was completely taken over, all the armoured doors removed and replaced. No one wanted to continue playing after that.
Rust can be fun when you are playing for a short time with a friend or two, preying on the weak until a stronger person or group steals everything you have. You will get tired of and even angry at the extremely punishing experience.
Recommended for playing with a large group (several experienced people online at any given time), building an extremely secure base (there is no overkill when it comes to security in Rust), and pwning because together you are Alpha and Omega.
I'd love to see different factions in this game that will benefit from working together so that even newbies and solo players have a reasonably safe place to settle. Or a karma system that will provide penalties to the strongest and most evil of players. Get negative karma when you kill and loot someone, and extra when its your own faction or someone who is not carrying a weapon. Being able to spot evil players from a distance and get extra positive karma when you kill them. Etc. This game really has a lot of potential but needs careful balancing of forces. The upcoming update will revamp the XP and Crafting system which may lead to some more balanced gameplay.
[ /TL:DR]
To enjoy playing Rust for a longer period of time you really need the advantage of larger and better numbers and better gear. Getting the gear is so hard that you also need friends for that. However the community is incredibly hostile and finding friends in the game is really hard. You will need to play a lot and lose a lot before you can grow strong enough to have some proper fun. The best moments are when you kill people while you have a disadvantage, when you really feel like you were smarter or more skilled than your opponent. Or when you actually get to defend your base or fight to get in other bases. But these moments are very rare. Overall i can not recommend this game because it relies on group play too much and at the same time does not facilitate group play in any way.
Note there are community servers that are smaller and have other restrictions or types of gameplay that could improve your single player experience but since they are unreliable my recommendation is for the base game as it stands in Early Access.

Despite selling more than a million copies of Dayz SA, the game has progressed fairly slowly. Assuming this money could have been used to speed up the development process, the current state of the game shows otherwise as many of the projected timeline goals were not met by the developers. Brian Hicks talked of porting the game to console, and introducing vehicles such as helicopters etc. by around the 2014-15 year. Those goals have still not been met. Apparently, the devs are still struggling with optimization, design features such as the global loot economy, etc.
Only time will tell whether or not Dayz SA will improve over the Dayz Mod. Hopefully with the extended time frame, the developers will be able to create a fairly stable and entertaining game.
In it's current state, I would advise anyone looking into Dayz SA to hold off on purchasing the Alpha version of the game. In the mean time, stay posted with everything Dayz related and consider buying the game in the future when it's in a more polished/complete state.

are rather simple and will be familiar to those oldschool RPG lovers. The main difference between this game and other RPGs is that you don't
to kill every monster you meet. Taking even this one simple notion into account, your entire playstyle may change drastically, leading you to different mid-game changes, and, of course, endings.
in Undertale combines 8bit and instrumental parts, is very well written, and greatly compliments the art and the story, making it into a whole brilliant work.
being a simple game, Undertale refers to older RPG games and up-to-date media, has its own unique traits and manages to touch on complex matters, making not the pixels you control, but you, the player himself, an active and responsible for his doings figure.

You're a survivor, that is, with no job but to survive. That's the appeal of the alpha; since there are no objectives--and thus no hope--your only option is to keep surviving until death inevitably overtakes you. It's bleak, yes, but in many ways, it delivers a sense of realism you don't get in many zombie games (or open worlds in general, for that matter). Given time, there's a truly great and memorable experience waiting to be explored, one that will come into its own with new and better weapons and more interactive elements such as vehicles. But as Bohemia makes so clear from the moment you boot up DayZ, this is an alpha. It's incomplete, and it shows. Yet Chernarus is well on its way to growing into the clothes that the developer has stitched for it, and if you feel you've got the steely will necessary to survive, DayZ is ready to test it.

I'm a man of consequences: I like feeling that my decisions in games are affecting the story in some way, unlike a vast majority of games where it only LOOKS like you can affect outcomes through dialog, but, in reality, they don't. I'm happy to find a game that really put effort into player choice.
Unlike probably a vast majority of people, I didn't start playing the game because of the hype, in fact, I missed that train. I did some research after hearing about it and thought "Hey, this looks fun and charming, might as well try it out!" I do not regret my decision.
The game itself is very story driven. Though it has a combat system, it's not the main focus of the game, which is nice, considering I was more interested in progressing in the story than fighting monsters. To summarize the story without spoiling it: I have not cried or laughed so hard since playing To the Moon.
Everything from the music to the characters just seems perfect to me, in my opinion. They tie themselves in so well, and for once, I felt a connection to each of the main characters. It encouraged me to look farther into each character rather than "be done with the area and move on".
If you aren't into slower-paced games, this probably isn't going to be the game for you, since the first time I played, it took me well over 8-10 hours to play. But if you're looking for a charming story, definitely consider picking up this title, especially for the True Pacifist arc.

Rust is truly one of my favorite games. It is an intense multiplayer survival game. Facepunch has taken the best elements of Minecraft and the best elements of dayz to create something truly amazing. Rust achieves what many games strive for. It creates amazing action sequences that will make you think you are in a scripted call of duty campaign until you realize that everything happening around is real. Totally unscripted. You are fighting for your life. It is totally player controlled. Dying in rust will truly hurt you because you are fighting for everything you have worked towards not to mention your pride.
I logged my 112th hour into rust and I have hardly felt time pass. You are easily sucked into this world and you get up hours later realizing that it is 4am and you have homework, at which time you sit down to play more rust.
The only downside of rust is the fact that if you are not playing with friends, the game will be extremely difficult. It is still an enjoyable experience, however, but to get the full experience of rust, you need to play with friends.
Another problem is the wonky gunplay. I am not new to FPSs as a whole, however I find aiming and shooting in rust to be quite awkward. This can take away from gameplay but not enough to warrant not playing the game.
Overall review: 8.5/10

You're a survivor, that is, with no job but to survive. That's the appeal of the alpha; since there are no objectives--and thus no hope--your only option is to keep surviving until death inevitably overtakes you. It's bleak, yes, but in many ways, it delivers a sense of realism you don't get in many zombie games (or open worlds in general, for that matter). Given time, there's a truly great and memorable experience waiting to be explored, one that will come into its own with new and better weapons and more interactive elements such as vehicles. But as Bohemia makes so clear from the moment you boot up DayZ, this is an alpha. It's incomplete, and it shows. Yet Chernarus is well on its way to growing into the clothes that the developer has stitched for it, and if you feel you've got the steely will necessary to survive, DayZ is ready to test it.

So. Borderlands. What if Diablo was turned into a first-person shooter on a world that takes notes from Catacha? Borderlands happens. The first game was the test,as it were. Borderlands 2 is the logical next step,taking all of the successes of the first game,ramping them up,improving on the failings (like plot...Seriously,the Vault from the first game was a container of tentacles and disapointment) of the preceeding title,all while adding new variety. Plot is now VERY well done,although particularly savvy players may be able to point out major twists a little early. The loot system,which was famed and lauded from the first game,got expanded upon MASSIVELY,and now each manufacturer's products are easily identifiable and have a unique gimmick,such as ammo capacity,throw away exploding guns,or ALL EXPLOSIONS,ALL THE TIME. I found myself pulling my hair out at times,but this game was made for four-player co-op,so I guess that's just my recluse showing. Shoot n loot at will!

While the first game was nothing to sneeze at, Borderlands 2 brought that little bit more to the table this time around, taking notes from what was successful, and what wasn't last time. With a more colourful cast populating Pandora this time around, and plenty of interesting little tidbits, such as plentiful quotes of Hamlet, Borderlands 2 seems to have put on the big boy pants quicker than you can say buyer's remorse.

I'm a man of consequences: I like feeling that my decisions in games are affecting the story in some way, unlike a vast majority of games where it only LOOKS like you can affect outcomes through dialog, but, in reality, they don't. I'm happy to find a game that really put effort into player choice.
Unlike probably a vast majority of people, I didn't start playing the game because of the hype, in fact, I missed that train. I did some research after hearing about it and thought "Hey, this looks fun and charming, might as well try it out!" I do not regret my decision.
The game itself is very story driven. Though it has a combat system, it's not the main focus of the game, which is nice, considering I was more interested in progressing in the story than fighting monsters. To summarize the story without spoiling it: I have not cried or laughed so hard since playing To the Moon.
Everything from the music to the characters just seems perfect to me, in my opinion. They tie themselves in so well, and for once, I felt a connection to each of the main characters. It encouraged me to look farther into each character rather than "be done with the area and move on".
If you aren't into slower-paced games, this probably isn't going to be the game for you, since the first time I played, it took me well over 8-10 hours to play. But if you're looking for a charming story, definitely consider picking up this title, especially for the True Pacifist arc.

I understand why this game is popular.
I understand why people think it's the best game we got since *your favorite game here*
I understand why it has a big community.
I don't understand why all of the above is actually bad.
Don't get me wrong, this IS a great game.
The story is great, the characters are interesting, unique if not even quite bizarre, the fighting system is challenging and funny, and the music... man, the music is just awesome.
But (yeah, here comes the BUT):
I don't like that it shows up everywhere on the Internet.
People telling Let's Players to play this game in YouTube comments.
People referring to it in places that have no connection to it at all.
People who use this game to gain attention.
I know a lot of communities have done this stuff in the past, the prime examples being Furries, Bronies, and Five Nights at Freddy's fans (maybe Homestuck, too, I never bothered with anything related to it, so most references and jokes might've gone past me with me not knowing/noticing it).
But this just shows that people have learned nothing from that.
The "fans" still feel the urge to rub their favorite thing into other people's faces, no matter if the reaction is positive or negative.
We still have the "Like this or you're a big mean poopy pants" and "Stop liking stuff I don't like or else I want you dead" arguments.
There still are those people who make it their hobby to roleplay as their favorite character.
Also, Fanfictions.
TL;DR
The game is great, the (annoying) majority of its community isn't.

Then nothing changed till came 0.40. Since then they started to make DayZ the clothing and gear simulator (honestly speaking I liked it really much). Since that moment that was normal that every next update had to bring a lot of new items into game. The game was lacking on game features, but we had huge variety of clothing to wear.
Around 0.50 they added persistance across the servers - the feature that made all items saved their position on the server so they stayed after every restart. The best feature of DayZ to me so far.
Everything had been cool and nice till this fu*king loot spawning system in 0.55  came - the loot wasn't spawning in the place for long time if somebody took it before. The said that they had made it like this to prevent server hoppers, and to make players fo further inland.  Reality was more brutal than DEVS thought and the server hoppers got all the gear at the coast and inland before normal players got it, so basically hoppers had everything - ordinary players had axes, if they knew where to find them lol. In the place where you had usually found a gun before, in this update you found an apple, nice isn't it?  Some people got used to it. Some people even found a guns. Very few people had even fun of the game. It was the worst patch in DayZ's history but still some people learnt how to adapt.
In 0.57 they destroyed all the mechanic that they had been making for 6 months atleast. They turned off persistance and made the loot economy exactly like 1 year ago - 100% same things spawn on every server in the same place. In this patch probably the "tent people" left the game, because they can't store items in tents and can't make the game pure "picnic party". Now the game looks like if you spawn in cherno and you know where to look for the gear, you will have AK and all other necessary gear to kill - in less than 20 minutes. I would like to add, that the same gear in 0.55 had consumed more than 3 hours to find.
But guys- don't worry that they turned off half of nice features of the game and made the game twice as exensive - we still deserve some new items! In this patch we got all new radiator texture on the only garbage car in this game; static helicrashes, static cars - exactly like on 16/12/2013 - real life BACK TO THE FUTURE  :D
After 800 hours I realized why it's called horror and survival game - because every date of next patch is so scary, that you want to stay in the patch you are now, because you are so afraid of unknown. And every next patch is survival, bacause all game rules and mechanics drastically change so you have to adapt if you want to survive next patch.
The sentence: "When life gives you lemons, make lemonade" takes on a new light in this game.

In 15 hours, I have completed this game twice. Once on a neutral ending as my first playthrough, then true pacifist ending. Honestly? 15 hours well spent. I cant say too much without spoilers so i'll just say this: Anyone can die, anyone can live. Your actions have consequences.
Undertale is not your regular RPG. Combat can be devided into two routes. The violent route being the Attack command, or the passive route with the Action and Mercy commands. Attacking involves timing your button presses to deal as much damage as possible per hit. When an enemy attacks you, it creates a bullethell minigame where your own skill determines whether or not you take damage. You will at scripted points in the game, aquire status effects such as being forced to jump over obstacles instead of floating around or being stationary and having to block incoming attacks with a single direction shield. The soundtrack is incredible, fitting perfectly with the locales and fights throughout the game.

Undertale is not your regular RPG. Combat can be devided into two routes. The violent route being the Attack command, or the passive route with the Action and Mercy commands. Attacking involves timing your button presses to deal as much damage as possible per hit. When an enemy attacks you, it creates a bullethell minigame where your own skill determines whether or not you take damage. You will at scripted points in the game, aquire status effects such as being forced to jump over obstacles instead of floating around or being stationary and having to block incoming attacks with a single direction shield. The soundtrack is incredible, fitting perfectly with the locales and fights throughout the game.

Undertale is deceptively simple. There's essentially three routes to take (good, neutral, bad). The gameplay is essentially turnbased combat mixed with bullethell mechanics and solving puzzles that are perhaps challenging if you were playing. Seeing through all three of the endings will take your probably around 10 hours at the very maximum.
That's frontloading the bad stuff about the game. If you let your initial impressions of "why am I playing this 8-bit indie game" get the best of you, you're going to miss out on probably one of the best stories I've seen in a video game.
As far as the plot goes, it's not the whole arc of the story that really resonates with everyone, but moreso the little things along the way. It's truly the journey, not the destination. The game actually makes you feel connected with the characters around you (and like a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥if you forgo any attempts at connecting with them) with the character development, humor, and massive soundtrack that happens throughout the game. It's a game that proves that in order to make an immersive, interesting world, you don't need cutting edge graphics or in-depth gameplay. You just need to put in a little love and care into making something that you can feel is worthwhile.
This game reminds me a lot of the Stanley Parable, in the sense that it's a short and sweet game, but it's meant to be played "blind". Any interaction with the community beforehand really dulls the experience (although I'd say it's nonetheless worthwhile despite any potential spoilers). "Oi m8 did you get the X ending where you do such and such?" Discovering things on your own make it all the more satisfying, and I think the community as a whole really ruins it. It's hard to say "just play the goddamn game" with only screenshots and short bursts of gameplay, but any more and it'd be dulling the experience.
Just play the goddamn game. If you don't like it, you'll probably figure that out before your first 2 hours of gameplay so you can get your $10 back from Steam.

The original review was stupid long so I edited it to be less... ridiculous.
GRAPHICS: Excellent. The sprites are detailed, the palettes are delightful and convey the mood of an area well, and the battle sprites are a joy to look at.
SOUND: Absolutely stunning. Each track is unique, but they are all interconnected somehow, which adds yet another layer to the game. Toby Fox, everybody. Toby Fox.
GAMEPLAY: The challenge comes from trying to show mercy, not from actually fighting. Not all enemies can be spared using the Mercy button, so try everything. It's all part of the message. The bullet hell parts are quite fun as well.
Also, make sure to check the flavor text for everything.
CHARACTERS/STORY: The characters are appealing, interesting, and easy to get invested in. The story is excellent, and consists of three paths: Neutral, Genocide, and Pacifist. If you're playing for the first time,
.  The story is best experienced alone, so I won't say any more.
OTHER (WRITING/HUMOR/ATMOSPHERE): Of course, the humor won't be for everyone, but I found it to be incredibly funny. It can also be scary, or  sad, or anything else. The writing never pulls punches, and it all comes together to form a unique universe.
There are lots of hidden secrets, so make sure to play multiple times.
CONCLUSION: It's a shame that this became such a #CRINGE game, because it really is very good. Two years have not been kind to its fans (often for justified reasons), but the game is just as good as it was. So if you're interested, ignore the fans and everyone holding it up as the pinnacle of gaming. Ignore me, even. I don't care. But if you're interested, give it a shot, because it's a worthwhile experience.

This is a very popular game so I'll try to stay moderate in this review, but I will say that I really liked it. :)
Undertale was an entertaining, funny game with wonderful dialogue that anyone can play regardless of skill/experience with games. Its message had quite an impact on me, and the emotional moments worked very well thanks to this game's phenomenal soundtrack. The message is simple but not as one-dimensional as you'd might expect, and no matter how you play you'll get a worthwhile ending. Multiple playthroughs are kind of a drag due to the story's frequent use of surprise to make the game fun, but a certain game mechanic makes it so that a second playthrough will hae some new content that makes it worthwhile. There's also a lot of commentary on the nature of games in general that really does make you think. Combat was a little tedious but significantly more enjoyable than most other RPGs I've played, boss fights were challenging and unique enough to be a lot of fun, there are a LOT of clever hidden secrets, and while some characters have less depth than others, all are immensely likeable (at least for me!) Certain areas were a little slower but overall the pacing is excellent with little to no filler. I enjoyed slowly piecing together the story through little snippets of information throughout the game. Humor may not be for everyone, but I personally liked it a lot.

If you liked Borderlands, you will like Borderlands 2. That's not to say that this is simply "More Borderlands," but the humor and themes carry over nicely. The graphics got a little facelift, you still have to tweak the settings a bit to get rid of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thick cell borders, and the controls are exactly the same.
The classes are all different, and much better. I hated Brick in BL1, so I figured I'd try the new melee class firsrt and give Gearbox a chance to apologize. They apologized, I accepted, and there was awesome make-up sex. The Assassin class is fantastic. In a game that is explicitly about shooting, this is a melee class that can hold its own.
Other differences from BL1: AI. The enemy AI is far superior in BL2. In BL1, sniping was a breeze. Seriously, I almost never missed a shot. Guys mostly just ran in a straight line and let you draw a bead on them. In BL2, it's a little trickier, and I chalk that up to improved AI.

While there are a handful of minor niggles, inexplicable removals and non-beneficial changes in the game, pretty much all else about this game is either better than the first or at the very least faithful to it. The universally loved artwork style and Diablo-esque loot-grabbing gameplay style has not changed one bit and remained as addictive as its sleeper hit predecessor.
One thing to keep in mind though - the game, unlike similar high-profile sequels, does rely on prior knowledge of the events in the Borderlands universe, as unlike other recent sequels (ehem, Crysis 2), there does exist some continuity for the overall story to make actual sense. So, if you have not yet played the first game, Borderlands 2 is one of the few AAA sequels that may require you to pick up a copy of the first game from the bargain bin.
Save for some unforeseen event like a surprise Half-Life 3 release this year, Borderlands 2 is, by all means, the biggest if not the best title of the year.

You can also choose to do things non-violently by opting to talk to monsters and figure out how to get them to leave them alone.
...stop reading this review.  Don't read ANY reviews.  Especially the wordy ones done by wanna be "pro reviewers" that go on and on about nothing, and occasionally outright spoil things.  Just get it and play through it.  Do it as "blindly" as you can.  Approach this thing with an open mind, experiment with everything you can think of, then think outside of the box and experiment with things you WOULDN'T have thought of otherwise. This game is worth the 20 dollars, or the 10 dollars if you are getting this on the Luner New Year sale AKA Steam being real sick and giving us a sale for a holiday 7/206958833 people celebrate in America and the UK combined. This is an addicting game at first, and when you run out of content you can go on a modded server or legacy. I got this game when the new Rust was just coming out, barely played it because of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ laptop issue, but still had it. I thought it was addicting then and I got between 9-15 fps the entire time. Once I finally upgraded, this was one of the first games I played. It is a super fun game to play with friends, in fact I think that is the only way it should be played. For the time I played it activly I was playing between 2-8 hours a day, I had over 40 hours in the past week on serveral occations. If that doesn't prove it is a good game, I don't know what is. I would reccomend modded servers A LOT. With regular wipes, and increased gather rates, it is a lot of fun to get started into and seeing all the different plug-ins and what the community is like on each modded server. I have tried to play vanilla, yet it is very challenging. Me and a friend (even though we didn't know what we were doing at the time) played on a vanilla server for 7 hours straight and made zero progress. We had one goal in mind on that playthrough, get at least ONE gun blueprint. We came out with anything BUT a gun blueprint. In conclusion, try out all the gamemodes and different types of servers there are in Rust and find which one fits your fancy. For me and my friends, we spent time on a battlefield server, had some fun with that, but eventually settled down on a server called Rusticity. A fun server for all, and I would reccomend it a lot. The server is good for trading BP's for supplies, and it isn't too OP, just a 3x gather rate and all the normal plug-ins such as TP, Homes, and all that other good♥♥♥♥♥♥
I hope this very LONG review helped you out in some way shape or form, even though no one is going to read this.

DayZ Standalone represents, as a game and in its development process, the most flagrant abuse of Steam's Early Access program. It is an indictment of the "give us your money now and we'll fix it later" attitude endemic in the industry. Yes, I know it was an alpha but looking at the big picture, it's clear DayZ Standalone was and continues to be more of a money grab than its Early Access peers e.g. Unturned and Killing Floor 2. The big difference is that these latter two actually deliver on their basic gameplay premise whereas DayZ continues to fail to do so.
Terrible melee hitboxes and garbage like zombies consistently glitching through walls was acceptable in DayZ Mod but is complately unacceptable in a game explicitly developed to remedy the Mod's deficiencies. A few hours into the game I knew I wanted to return it based on seeing the same awful pathfinding, teleporting, and glitchy hitboxes from the mod. Building from scratch had accomplished very little. They've had over a year to address these basic gameplay issues but surprise, surprise, they're still here.
Unexpectedly long development times aren't new in the gaming industry but for the developer to abandon the project after a phenomenally successful round of funding is irresponsible.
It's been over a year but now that Valve does refunds, I've requested one. At no time during that period when the developer was busy not fixing the core gameplay and instead adding pistol grips and mad cow disease did I believe that the finished game was going to released in a reasonable time.
Yesterday was E3 and the former developer is apparently working on new games. Hopefully Lord GabeN bans him from (ab)using the Early Access system since he has a proven track record of failing to keep his promises.
DayZ Standalone is destined to follow the same over-hyped and severely delayed path to mediocrity Duke Nukem Forever did. To the Duke's credit, at least his game didn't bilk you for thirty bucks for the privilege of pre-alpha testing during those years.
NOT RECOMMENDED
DayZ Mod, Arma III, H1Z1, even Unturned are better alternatives.
