Ok, so I'm just gonna say it. This is my favorite indie game of all time. This thing kind of blew me away. When I bought it I knew all the hype surrounding it, and when I started playing it, I could not see what was so special about the game. I mean, it was funny, and the animation on the characters was charming, but nothing really was that spectacular. The game got eventually got better, and ended up finishing the game for the first time (Neutral Ending), and thought to myself that I could try again from my latest checkpoint to get the True Pacifist ending. One of the best decisions I made in my gaming life, because this gave me all of the story I had missed and made the relationships with the characters I ended up saving worth it.
This game changes according to your decisions, the world reacts very much extremelly to them. If you end up doing what is called a Genocide run, you will probably feel like a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥ at least I did. I tried starting a Genocide run FOUR times, before I actually was able to continue with it, because I didn't want to do make myself do those things. It's rare for a game to make me hold back on my decisions.
The story, is really good and interesting, but what makes this game excel are its characters. From the sweetheart Toriel to which is probably the most awesome skelleton in any videogame, the great Papyrus, along with his lazy brother Sans (yes those are names of letter fonts), the characters really bring this game home to me.
In terms of gameplay, it's pretty much an RPG that revolves around exploring, solving some simple puzzles and reflex-based combat, In these terms it's pretty competent, but not anything extraordinary. Like I said, it's the storytelling and characters that make this game be so acclaimed.
Another thing that is awesome is the soundtrack, composed by the very same person who did the almost the entire game by himself, Mr. Toby Fox, which ranges from Electronic, Ambient, Piano tunes, Rock to Electro Swing. FANTASTIC!
Overall, this game is freaking awesome, it stays with you and makes one hell of an impact. My 2nd favorite game of 2015, just below The Witcher 3 (my fav rpg of all time) and above MGS V. Go out, buy it, and experience this gem by yourself.
PS: Toby Fox, ♥♥♥♥ YOU for THAT particular boss battle in the Genocide Run, but still great game :3

You will see people tell you that Undertale is overrated, overhyped, and has an obnoxious community. Forget what those people are saying and play this game for yourself, whether they are right or not, it won't matter, because for better or for worse this might be one of the best experiences you'll receive for a good long time. You really shouldn't read an in-depth review even over mechanics, it's somewhat better just to go in without really knowing about it intrincally. That said:
Pros:
- The writing is really nice and flavourful, it reminds me of Earthbound (you will hear this a lot) on how every character has something interesting to say and nearly every object has some fun description instead of a small detailed one of what it does. The game also knows when the best time to drop certain humour in place for a moment it's not needed, in which case those descriptions suit themselves to the tone needed. Good stuff.
- There really is just flavour everywhere, the game feels very alive and wonderful because the world feels real, and its quirkiness reflects on it much more wholey, other than just feeling like individual characters or parts are weird or silly, the whole world of the underground has this difference that not many other in-game universes can attest themselves to.
- The pacing feels good, a little slow to start, for a reason that you can imply from when you play it, but basically it feels like this game is exactly as long as it needs to be while just leaving you with a desire for more of it. Not more of the individual storylines of whichever route you take, more just a desire for it itself.
- The stor... you know actually I think I want to cap off this review with something different.
I want you to look at the overzealous undertale fan you can first fine. Look at who they are, look at their blog or their youtube comments, or their twitter, or their steam. Find a time when they weren't this. I can gurantee you, there will likely be a time when they thought this was all cringey, and that it was weird and immature, for any kind of fandom or whatever. Look at it like this: Undertale managed to break down that person's insecurities and rejection of fully outwardly loving something, and letting people know they did. Yeah, it might be annoying or obnoxious, but look at how much they're enjoying themselves, unconventionally fufulling themselves with the fandom of a video game. That overzealous fanboy is a better review than any I could make, it's not to say that this is what this game will do to you, more than it will, at any least, make you realise that it's okay to show love, and it's okay to be comfortable with it.
Think about the first sentence of this review. Think about why Undertale might be overrated, overhyped and have that community. The first reviews came before the larger community picked it up, no one is being bribed (people actually think this? it was almost a one dog team come on), the reason it has so much love that makes people adore a game so much isn't coming from anything pre-conceived, or artificial, the game naturally creates that love in you, more than any pre-established series can. Why does it do that? Well, go and see for yourself. That's why this love you can see wherever you go is a better review than this could ever be.

If you don't like joining clans and just like playing solo or with a buddy do not get this game! This is as much of a co-op game as i have ever seen. Guaranteed you will spend most of your time gathering stone and wood just to build and secure a small building which most likely will be raided, wasting all the resources you've gathered.
So like I said It's not a single player or small group friendly game at all. Big groups dominate servers by building near resource heavy areas, guarding them and killing anyone that travels near. Supply drops that can give you a better chance for guns and attachments will always be taken by groups in which you'll never get. And at the end of the day you'll end up just begging for weapons and better building plans in chat.
And all the while you are basically on a timer. Each server that runs this game wipes either weekly on large servers or near once a month on smaller servers. Completely wiping the server of structures built by players and often resetting player data, meaning any crafting plans aka blueprints -bp- (weapons, armor, ect.) you may have found and memorized will be lost. Putting the game on a wipe timer means you are definitly going to either overplay this game or play extremely casually.
I've played this game for 70 hours, and honestly I felt like I acheived nothing at all in the end. Maybe a few laughs as it is fun the first few hours but it immediately turns into a farm fest really quick. At the end I basically was just hoping to log on and see my fort be raided so I could stop playing.

I'm going to go against the wind here and say that I didn't find this game that exciting. I believe part of that reason is because I (1) didn't have too much time in my life to play it, (2) Only played alone, and (3) I wasn't very hyped for the game to start with. I only did play 11 hours at the writing of this recommendation.
My main criticism of the game is that it is too repetitive - the quest structure itself annoyed me to no end. A lot of the quests involve going back to areas you have already explored to perform an objective or another which you have already done multiple times before. There is no multi-quest tracking, so I've found myself always opening the quest menu to see what I had to do in one area for multiple quests.
The game is probably more enjoyable with friends; but if you're planning to play alone and don't have much free time on your hands, I'd stay away from it - the quest design feels like work.
Best played with a friend.

Let me begin in saying this.
If you liked the first Borderlands, then you have a decently small chance in not liking this one.
However, staying away from the cons for this game. It's not that bad, it's actually really fun! The character selections you get at the start (without the dlc) is good. It's nice to see same powers for some characters in the sequel. However, with the dlc, it adds in two new characters. Krieg a friendly Psycho and Gaige the Mechromancer. Summons a huge bot that can melt down any enemy in the game if built correctly or you can use the bot as a support and put shields on you and your party members.
I would most definently say to play this with friends. A full party is the funniest and a great time. The NPC doesn't seem to be card board cutouts like with the "Pre-sequel." Everyone has a meaning and a great story behind them. A very selected amount of NPC you talk to have great stories. Getting the GOTY edition is a great idea, but if you can also get the Headhunter DLC as well, then it branches out and tells you more about the story and with certain characters. The humor is a bit childish for the most part. With the other part, it's amazing. I would spend 10 minutes almost just laughing at a simple creative joke, playing with friends makes the experience 100x better. I recommend picking this up with the mind set of finishing the game more than twice and with friends.
Playing this game for around 42 hours and played it on launch with friends, I would say it's worth getting the GOTY edition rather than getting this basic one. The GOTY edition isn't that much more compared to DLC you can buy seperately. Even though this game has a few bugs still, and they took out some great farming methods. I still rate this game a 7/10. It's great, the gunplay feels perfect and the story creates an atomsphere so perfect you can feel that anger in a bandits voice as he tries to murder you. I recommend picking this up as the GOTY edition to save money.

The game that made me feel like an ACTUAL hero.
Will I was trying to drag myself out of my Star Wars-fueled mentality.  I ran across this game during the winter sale and didn't think anything of it.  After about a few days of the Old Republic (KOTOR and SWTOR), bought this game to welcome myself back to school.  I didn't know much about the game nor had I seen any YouTube vids on it.  All I knew was that there were skeletons in it and a weird heart thingy.  Then I started to play it.  I was gonna be disappointed if I bought a generic RPG.  When I met Flowey for the first time I was about to quit the game after the first chance I get to save.  When Flowey explained to me how the underground works I had flashbacks of playing Skyrim for the first time.  After meeting Toriel and getting introduced to the gameplay I had grown attached to her clingly nature (which says much of me) I could not bring myself to hurt her or even kill the monsters in the ruins.  After a while of fighting her she didn't even want to kill me either.  It was at that point I knew I could play the game without killing people.  If I fight, I would weaken my opponent and spare them.  I could talk people down instead of crushing their heads.  Normally I play RPGs I care only about getting stronger by slaying creatures, doing quests, and beat the big bad dude then game over.  I would be god like in power but not really care about the beings slaughtered in my quest to become the best.  Here it was different.  After I learned I could win by not being the Conquerer, the Destroyer of Lives, the avatar of Death itself, I kept rolling with it.  Mind you this was my first playthrough of the game.  I didn't learn until near the end of the game that doing this results in a pretty somber ending.  I had almost made it through without killing till I reach the second to last boss that made it near impossible to end the fight without him being killed.  I even spared the last boss and it told me that there was still a better way to end the game if you learn the truth behind Flowey.  I was still heartbroken by the murder and anything to fix it was welcoming.  After learning the flower's past I gained an ending I'm proud of.  An ending where everyone in the game is happy with.
In this game you can play it like an RPG and you won't be wrong for it.  After all, in an RPG you kill enemies and monsters to get EXP.  The more EXP you gain the more you LV up and when you LV up you become stronger.  Killing the enemy becomes easier and easier.  Until one day you are strong enough that no one or nothing can hurt you.  If that is what you  enjoy I won't stop you from having that kind of fun.  Just remember, are you really a hero if you must kill to get you happy ending?

After devoting countless hours to this game (all over the course of one month mind you) it's hard to judge my experience with a straight yes or no.  A maybe is best.  A maybe with a lean to yes, but a lean to no; damn...that's still a maybe.  Well let me explain this in a little more detail...
Rust, like various other multiplayer PvP/PvE crafting games, suffers from some major game-breaking issues.  Some of them are hardwired into the game's design and some if it is just based on the player's own short-comings.
First off, this game requires committment.  You can try to do it alone - and i've developed some strategies for doing this successfully - but you're better off with a group, and even then...you gotta hope it's a large group.  With the servers being run 24/7 and any number of players activevly playing, Rust becomes a full-time job when you're having to manage, gather and constantly protect your base/belongings.  And even IF you have a large enough clan to have an 24/7 online presence, all it takes is a clan of close-to-equal number to tear everything down.  But such is Rust...
Secondly, hackers everywhere.  I don't need to elaborate any more.  The last time I played we had to deal with all sorts of hackers.  You have the ones that can nail headshots from miles away.  The ones that can no-clip and teleport into your base.  Fortunately if you're playing a well moderated server, you're only a tweet away from contacting a mod (with some delay if they aren't actively checking their Twitter account).  But such is Rust...
Lastly - and it's hard to go into exact detail without boring any potential reader of this review - is the work-in-progress nature of Rust.  There's some bugs here and there and a few of them can lead to more rage-quits if not properly recognized immediately.   This section of my review might even become outdated in previous Rust updates, so I dont feel any need to go into exact detail.  You'll come across things as you play.  Stuff like building-restriction boundaries having small "blank spots" where other players will manage to build and climb over your walls.  Lots of progress in my last playthrough was set-back due to crap like this.  But such is Rust...
But hey...here's one BIG positive thing to be aware of!
The community!  Sure every once in a while there can be some sh!theels who really wreck the experience, but I guess it's a matter of perspective.  If you're a small fish, you're gonna get stomped.  So adapt.  That's easier said than done.  My first week in Rust I got raided pretty hard by some people who knew the game better than me and had the resources to ruin all the work I did single-handedly. but once I was with a group of people who were doing pretty well, we were doing the stomping.  Let Rust take you over.  All is Rust and Rust is all.  Once you embrace the experience and find a way to coexist in the madness, it becomes a really unique experience.

|-Spoiler Free Review-|
Undertale. A game so hyped up on certain corners of the internet you need to have your eyes closed to miss it. Luckily, I got to play it having only a few minor elements spoiled. A fresh run for all intents and purposes, which is the most recommended way to go in to it. After playing it myself, I also give that advice.
Many reviewers have differing opinions of what constitutes spoilers, so even spoiler free reviews may ruin small bits of the game. Tread carefully when reading other people's opinions on the game. I'll do my best not to include anything specific here.
On to the game:
Undertale is a 8 to 9 hour 8-bit story-driven rpg where your decisions in the story affect how the entire game plays out. Each decision you make changes how the other characters respond to your presence. This mechanic makes combat more meaningful in a genre where most fights are treated only as a means to grow stronger.
|-The Battle System-|
The battle system in Undertale is most similar to the Earthbound series. All the fighting takes place in turn-based combat from the perspective of the player character.
There are two twists to the formula.
1.) Enemy attacks are a form of top-down arcade shooter. Your ability to survive depends on how well you can dodge their unique patterns.
2.) Arguably the most important aspect of the game: You can attempt to spare every enemy you encounter.
Killing the monsters is usually quicker and easier than sparing them. On top of that, sparing monsters does not award the player with experience. With this in mind, the player needs to decide whether or not it is worth the trouble to leave each hostile enemy they meet alive.
|-The Story-|
The biggest reason most people try Undertale. Someone recommends the game and, more than likely, it is the first thing they'll talk about when trying to convince you.
Bottom line?
It's good. Not great, but good. It has a couple interesting twists here and there, but for the most part it follows a predictable path. Now that isn't necessarily a bad thing, but don't go in expecting a new classic of storytelling. If I get specific on the why it'll tread into spoiler territory, so let's move on to what I believe is the strongest part of the game.
|-The Characters-|
Undertale has a boatload of funny and endearing characters. Even the random battle enemies have unique personalities and interactions. Outside of the various areas you visit, they help to fill in the world and make it believable. In many rpgs random npcs mostly just have throwaway lines that don't have any impact on you at all. In Undertale they almost always have another joke to tell, or something that adds a little more to the overall story. It's definitely something I wish more games would do.
That's without starting on the main cast. In order to avoid spoilers I will say that for as much care and effort that went into the random npcs, much more was put into the named characters you encounter. Every one feels like they are necessary to the story, and none of them feel like they were tacked on just for the sake of it. Some of their interactions, on the other hand...
|-The Writing-|
For the most part, Undertale is well written. I wouldn't say it's a pinnacle of writing, but it does its job. It is servicable throughout, and there are only one or two times where it takes you out of the experience. Usually, this happens when the game is attempting to convey sadness, desperation, or sentimentality. It goes from heartfelt to hokey real quick. Some of those moments are well done, however.
The jokes are Undertale's strength. There are so many so frequently that I wonder if they started out with the idea that they were going to make a game with a ton of puns and awkward humor, and then try to fill in a story around the jokes. Most are well done but, as to be expected with so many attempts, some fall flat.
|-The Music-|
The music is great. If the characters are the strongest part of the game, the music is a close second. Like the characters, each piece of music makes each different area, situation, and boss fight feel all the more unique. From the monsters to the places they accompany. The retro-style of the music goes hand-in-hand with the visual style to create a cohesive world.
|-Overall-|
I played Undertale having only heard that it was good, and I tried it with relatively neutral expectations. In the time since, I have seen many people laud it as the game of the year (or all time, even). With that in mind, is Undertale as good as many people claim it to be?
In my opinion: No.
Undertale is good. It is worth playing. It is of a quality I wish every indie game would be. But it's not perfect, and its flaws were apparent to me as I played through it.
For many people, Undertale is the first game that they've played of this quality. The first game that gave them meaningful impact for the decisions they made. For them, it is the game of the year, maybe even the best game they've ever come across. It is none of these things for me, but that is not something I can hold against them.
All in all, Undertale is a game I am glad I played, regardless of its shortcomings.

|-Spoiler Free Review-|
Undertale. A game so hyped up on certain corners of the internet you need to have your eyes closed to miss it. Luckily, I got to play it having only a few minor elements spoiled. A fresh run for all intents and purposes, which is the most recommended way to go in to it. After playing it myself, I also give that advice.
Many reviewers have differing opinions of what constitutes spoilers, so even spoiler free reviews may ruin small bits of the game. Tread carefully when reading other people's opinions on the game. I'll do my best not to include anything specific here.
On to the game:
Undertale is a 8 to 9 hour 8-bit story-driven rpg where your decisions in the story affect how the entire game plays out. Each decision you make changes how the other characters respond to your presence. This mechanic makes combat more meaningful in a genre where most fights are treated only as a means to grow stronger.
|-The Battle System-|
The battle system in Undertale is most similar to the Earthbound series. All the fighting takes place in turn-based combat from the perspective of the player character.
There are two twists to the formula.
1.) Enemy attacks are a form of top-down arcade shooter. Your ability to survive depends on how well you can dodge their unique patterns.
2.) Arguably the most important aspect of the game: You can attempt to spare every enemy you encounter.
Killing the monsters is usually quicker and easier than sparing them. On top of that, sparing monsters does not award the player with experience. With this in mind, the player needs to decide whether or not it is worth the trouble to leave each hostile enemy they meet alive.
|-The Story-|
The biggest reason most people try Undertale. Someone recommends the game and, more than likely, it is the first thing they'll talk about when trying to convince you.
Bottom line?
It's good. Not great, but good. It has a couple interesting twists here and there, but for the most part it follows a predictable path. Now that isn't necessarily a bad thing, but don't go in expecting a new classic of storytelling. If I get specific on the why it'll tread into spoiler territory, so let's move on to what I believe is the strongest part of the game.
|-The Characters-|
Undertale has a boatload of funny and endearing characters. Even the random battle enemies have unique personalities and interactions. Outside of the various areas you visit, they help to fill in the world and make it believable. In many rpgs random npcs mostly just have throwaway lines that don't have any impact on you at all. In Undertale they almost always have another joke to tell, or something that adds a little more to the overall story. It's definitely something I wish more games would do.
That's without starting on the main cast. In order to avoid spoilers I will say that for as much care and effort that went into the random npcs, much more was put into the named characters you encounter. Every one feels like they are necessary to the story, and none of them feel like they were tacked on just for the sake of it. Some of their interactions, on the other hand...
|-The Writing-|
For the most part, Undertale is well written. I wouldn't say it's a pinnacle of writing, but it does its job. It is servicable throughout, and there are only one or two times where it takes you out of the experience. Usually, this happens when the game is attempting to convey sadness, desperation, or sentimentality. It goes from heartfelt to hokey real quick. Some of those moments are well done, however.
The jokes are Undertale's strength. There are so many so frequently that I wonder if they started out with the idea that they were going to make a game with a ton of puns and awkward humor, and then try to fill in a story around the jokes. Most are well done but, as to be expected with so many attempts, some fall flat.
|-The Music-|
The music is great. If the characters are the strongest part of the game, the music is a close second. Like the characters, each piece of music makes each different area, situation, and boss fight feel all the more unique. From the monsters to the places they accompany. The retro-style of the music goes hand-in-hand with the visual style to create a cohesive world.
|-Overall-|
I played Undertale having only heard that it was good, and I tried it with relatively neutral expectations. In the time since, I have seen many people laud it as the game of the year (or all time, even). With that in mind, is Undertale as good as many people claim it to be?
In my opinion: No.
Undertale is good. It is worth playing. It is of a quality I wish every indie game would be. But it's not perfect, and its flaws were apparent to me as I played through it.
For many people, Undertale is the first game that they've played of this quality. The first game that gave them meaningful impact for the decisions they made. For them, it is the game of the year, maybe even the best game they've ever come across. It is none of these things for me, but that is not something I can hold against them.
All in all, Undertale is a game I am glad I played, regardless of its shortcomings.

On to the game:
Undertale is a 8 to 9 hour 8-bit story-driven rpg where your decisions in the story affect how the entire game plays out. Each decision you make changes how the other characters respond to your presence. This mechanic makes combat more meaningful in a genre where most fights are treated only as a means to grow stronger.
|-The Battle System-|
The battle system in Undertale is most similar to the Earthbound series. All the fighting takes place in turn-based combat from the perspective of the player character.
There are two twists to the formula.
1.) Enemy attacks are a form of top-down arcade shooter. Your ability to survive depends on how well you can dodge their unique patterns.
2.) Arguably the most important aspect of the game: You can attempt to spare every enemy you encounter.
Killing the monsters is usually quicker and easier than sparing them. On top of that, sparing monsters does not award the player with experience. With this in mind, the player needs to decide whether or not it is worth the trouble to leave each hostile enemy they meet alive.
|-The Story-|
The biggest reason most people try Undertale. Someone recommends the game and, more than likely, it is the first thing they'll talk about when trying to convince you.
Bottom line?
It's good. Not great, but good. It has a couple interesting twists here and there, but for the most part it follows a predictable path. Now that isn't necessarily a bad thing, but don't go in expecting a new classic of storytelling. If I get specific on the why it'll tread into spoiler territory, so let's move on to what I believe is the strongest part of the game.
|-The Characters-|
Undertale has a boatload of funny and endearing characters. Even the random battle enemies have unique personalities and interactions. Outside of the various areas you visit, they help to fill in the world and make it believable. In many rpgs random npcs mostly just have throwaway lines that don't have any impact on you at all. In Undertale they almost always have another joke to tell, or something that adds a little more to the overall story. It's definitely something I wish more games would do.
That's without starting on the main cast. In order to avoid spoilers I will say that for as much care and effort that went into the random npcs, much more was put into the named characters you encounter. Every one feels like they are necessary to the story, and none of them feel like they were tacked on just for the sake of it. Some of their interactions, on the other hand...
|-The Writing-|
For the most part, Undertale is well written. I wouldn't say it's a pinnacle of writing, but it does its job. It is servicable throughout, and there are only one or two times where it takes you out of the experience. Usually, this happens when the game is attempting to convey sadness, desperation, or sentimentality. It goes from heartfelt to hokey real quick. Some of those moments are well done, however.
The jokes are Undertale's strength. There are so many so frequently that I wonder if they started out with the idea that they were going to make a game with a ton of puns and awkward humor, and then try to fill in a story around the jokes. Most are well done but, as to be expected with so many attempts, some fall flat.
|-The Music-|
The music is great. If the characters are the strongest part of the game, the music is a close second. Like the characters, each piece of music makes each different area, situation, and boss fight feel all the more unique. From the monsters to the places they accompany. The retro-style of the music goes hand-in-hand with the visual style to create a cohesive world.
|-Overall-|
I played Undertale having only heard that it was good, and I tried it with relatively neutral expectations. In the time since, I have seen many people laud it as the game of the year (or all time, even). With that in mind, is Undertale as good as many people claim it to be?
In my opinion: No.
Undertale is good. It is worth playing. It is of a quality I wish every indie game would be. But it's not perfect, and its flaws were apparent to me as I played through it.
For many people, Undertale is the first game that they've played of this quality. The first game that gave them meaningful impact for the decisions they made. For them, it is the game of the year, maybe even the best game they've ever come across. It is none of these things for me, but that is not something I can hold against them.
All in all, Undertale is a game I am glad I played, regardless of its shortcomings.

After devoting countless hours to this game (all over the course of one month mind you) it's hard to judge my experience with a straight yes or no.  A maybe is best.  A maybe with a lean to yes, but a lean to no; damn...that's still a maybe.  Well let me explain this in a little more detail...
Rust, like various other multiplayer PvP/PvE crafting games, suffers from some major game-breaking issues.  Some of them are hardwired into the game's design and some if it is just based on the player's own short-comings.
First off, this game requires committment.  You can try to do it alone - and i've developed some strategies for doing this successfully - but you're better off with a group, and even then...you gotta hope it's a large group.  With the servers being run 24/7 and any number of players activevly playing, Rust becomes a full-time job when you're having to manage, gather and constantly protect your base/belongings.  And even IF you have a large enough clan to have an 24/7 online presence, all it takes is a clan of close-to-equal number to tear everything down.  But such is Rust...
Secondly, hackers everywhere.  I don't need to elaborate any more.  The last time I played we had to deal with all sorts of hackers.  You have the ones that can nail headshots from miles away.  The ones that can no-clip and teleport into your base.  Fortunately if you're playing a well moderated server, you're only a tweet away from contacting a mod (with some delay if they aren't actively checking their Twitter account).  But such is Rust...
Lastly - and it's hard to go into exact detail without boring any potential reader of this review - is the work-in-progress nature of Rust.  There's some bugs here and there and a few of them can lead to more rage-quits if not properly recognized immediately.   This section of my review might even become outdated in previous Rust updates, so I dont feel any need to go into exact detail.  You'll come across things as you play.  Stuff like building-restriction boundaries having small "blank spots" where other players will manage to build and climb over your walls.  Lots of progress in my last playthrough was set-back due to crap like this.  But such is Rust...
But hey...here's one BIG positive thing to be aware of!
The community!  Sure every once in a while there can be some sh!theels who really wreck the experience, but I guess it's a matter of perspective.  If you're a small fish, you're gonna get stomped.  So adapt.  That's easier said than done.  My first week in Rust I got raided pretty hard by some people who knew the game better than me and had the resources to ruin all the work I did single-handedly. but once I was with a group of people who were doing pretty well, we were doing the stomping.  Let Rust take you over.  All is Rust and Rust is all.  Once you embrace the experience and find a way to coexist in the madness, it becomes a really unique experience.

If youve played B1 you know what to expect in B2. Obviously the main selling point is those bazillion guns, and they dont disappoint. The different zooms, mag sizes, reload speeds, elemental damages and other features give each weapon its own tactical feel. Theres also a pleasing variety of enemies to shoot. The story is vastly improved compared to B1, and includes a strong antagonist in Handsome Jack. I really grew to hate him, which is a tribute to the quality of the writing and voice acting. I also laughed several times at the wacky sense of humour throughout the game. Theres easily above 40 hours of content including side quests and I encountered no significant bugs. There are minor negative points. Vehicle combat still sucks but fortunately it can be avoided for most of the game. The checkpoint only save system doesn't fit the huge maps. And occasionally characters will talk during the shooting. But overall, B2 is an outstanding game, and a strong contender for my top 5 GOTY.

Before I start, I'll be honest; I never bought into the hype of this game. Even if almost every artist, reviewer and internet personality I know and care about was saying this was the BEST GAME EVAR (fortunatedly, I didn't got spoiled on anything), it never got to me as its sales pitch was ''It's just like Earthbound'', and of all the SNES-era masterpieces, Earthbound was the only one I never managed to like, no matter how many times I tried to.
So, between that and the fact it was made with GameMaker, I came into this game expecting yet another shoddy cash-grab using nostalgia as bait.
I've never been so glad of being wrong...
Putting the specifics away (to avoid spoilers), Undertale is less about the game itself and more about YOU, the player. So much that, as someone who studies Psychology, I dare to say this game is an excelent test of character about the attitude with take towards games. Or more specifically, to answer these questions:
-What are games to you?
-Are they something you use because you're bored or want to vent out frustration?
-Are you in for the joy of gameplay?
-For the pleasure of a good story?''
Whatever may be your answer, if you play the game as blind as possible, you'll probably find the answers to those questions.
So, with that said, play this game. And tell me, what did you learn at the end of your journey? Whatever path you took to arrive at it...

Before I start, I'll be honest; I never bought into the hype of this game. Even if almost every artist, reviewer and internet personality I know and care about was saying this was the BEST GAME EVAR (fortunatedly, I didn't got spoiled on anything), it never got to me as its sales pitch was ''It's just like Earthbound'', and of all the SNES-era masterpieces, Earthbound was the only one I never managed to like, no matter how many times I tried to.
So, between that and the fact it was made with GameMaker, I came into this game expecting yet another shoddy cash-grab using nostalgia as bait.
I've never been so glad of being wrong...
Putting the specifics away (to avoid spoilers), Undertale is less about the game itself and more about YOU, the player. So much that, as someone who studies Psychology, I dare to say this game is an excelent test of character about the attitude with take towards games. Or more specifically, to answer these questions:
-What are games to you?
-Are they something you use because you're bored or want to vent out frustration?
-Are you in for the joy of gameplay?
-For the pleasure of a good story?''
Whatever may be your answer, if you play the game as blind as possible, you'll probably find the answers to those questions.
So, with that said, play this game. And tell me, what did you learn at the end of your journey? Whatever path you took to arrive at it...

If youve played B1 you know what to expect in B2. Obviously the main selling point is those bazillion guns, and they dont disappoint. The different zooms, mag sizes, reload speeds, elemental damages and other features give each weapon its own tactical feel. Theres also a pleasing variety of enemies to shoot. The story is vastly improved compared to B1, and includes a strong antagonist in Handsome Jack. I really grew to hate him, which is a tribute to the quality of the writing and voice acting. I also laughed several times at the wacky sense of humour throughout the game. Theres easily above 40 hours of content including side quests and I encountered no significant bugs. There are minor negative points. Vehicle combat still sucks but fortunately it can be avoided for most of the game. The checkpoint only save system doesn't fit the huge maps. And occasionally characters will talk during the shooting. But overall, B2 is an outstanding game, and a strong contender for my top 5 GOTY.

After hearing about all of the hype and love of the game, I decided to buy it. I beat the game on the Genocide Route. (Going to try the Pacifist Route.) The narration of the story during some parts is great. Even the story in general is beautiful. The main characters you meet are rememberable.

I never thought it was going to be this good. My standards were extremely low after playing the game, FNaF. (Hate all you want. The game was alright, but it wasn't that great.)
Undertale is a Indie game, created by the man named Toby Fox. And boy did he do a great job on this game. After I heard that it was Kickstarter funded, that made it seem even better. I would love to see more, great titles by Toby. Great work, dude!
[About The Game]
The game starts off with a few photos with some text describing the prelude to some of it. Then, you continue on your adventure. During the tutorial, you're going to be given a choice when fighting enemies: Kill them, or Spare them. Killing them is a grind fest, where in every major area, you need to kill a specific amount of monsters until they're all dead. If you have feelings for video game characters, you'll feel definitely horrible after killing them. I suggest doing the Pacifist Route first, just in case you don't want the game to be changed after doing the Genocide Route, then the Pacifist.  On your journey, you'll buy food, fight/spare monsters, befriend people, love every last bit of Temmie Village, and solve easy, but fun puzzles.
[Pros and Cons]

Great Artwork
Beautiful Story
Rememberable Characters

[About The Game]
The game starts off with a few photos with some text describing the prelude to some of it. Then, you continue on your adventure. During the tutorial, you're going to be given a choice when fighting enemies: Kill them, or Spare them. Killing them is a grind fest, where in every major area, you need to kill a specific amount of monsters until they're all dead. If you have feelings for video game characters, you'll feel definitely horrible after killing them. I suggest doing the Pacifist Route first, just in case you don't want the game to be changed after doing the Genocide Route, then the Pacifist.  On your journey, you'll buy food, fight/spare monsters, befriend people, love every last bit of Temmie Village, and solve easy, but fun puzzles.

I dit not really care for the first Borderlands. I found it grindy, repetative and visually dull. Not even playing with friends saved the experience for me.
But then came Borderlands 2 and for some reason I bought it on day one, I loved it! Gone was the grindy feeling, gone was the repetative gameplay and gone was the boring enviornments. The humor is some of the best humor in any media ever, hollywood should take a look at the wonderful black humor displayed in this game.
Gameplay wise it's a blast. The various weapons (and there are ALOT of weapons) are satisfying to use and you get that great Diablo feel when you open a chest or kill something big and the loot just sprays everywhere. Missions are varied and so are the enviorments. Story is really good with Jack beeing one of the best villians in video game history.
Playing this with friends is almost a must, since the fun will multiply by the number of players joining in. When you are sitting in skype with three of your best friends, killing badasses is one of the most joyous experiences you can have over standard TCP/IP protocol.
Some of the DLC is good, some are not so good. It's really up to you and what you want to expand your game with.
The games only downside thou is that you have to play thru the game on normal mode before you can play with that character on "True Vault Hunter Mode". Which is when the game really starts to get interesting with better loot and harder enemies. It would be good if you upon character creation could just select "True Vault Hunter Mode" and start you new character with some basic gear to fit the level.
But overall, one of the best FPS/RPG games out there.

Capable of meeting all of the expectations of Borderlands veterans and welcoming newcomers without making them feel lost, Borderlands 2 is one of the best games out there. The game is very long (if you go for all of the sidequests, which is EXTREMELY recommended), but it manages to remain entertaing at every step of the way - quests don't feel repetitive, and thanks to a healthy dose of excellent humor, you'll be wanting to play it again. The game is considerably harder - enemies now scale to your level much more often than in the original game, leveling up is considerably harder and money drop has been DRASTICALLY reduced (prices were balanced, too). Newcomers will love it and veterans will have an excellent time. Worth every cent. DEFINITELY recommend.

DayZ is fun game to play with friends if you're able to get past the fact that it is optimized like a potato and there terrible glitches.

You explore and get geared up, getting enough supplies to last you a while, you're having fun!... until someone gets stuck in the wall or gets killed by invisible zombies. You are then left alone, dreading the run to meet up with your friend(s) once more to start the cycle again.
DayZ could be played without another friend to accompany you so you don't have to worry about wasting time trying to find each other, but in my personal opinion this game feels like it should be a co op experience to get the most enjoyment out of it.
TL;DR = Overall, the game is good and has potential to be great however the current state of it is pretty terrible and ruins a lot of the fun that could be had.
I would save the money until the game is optimized and mainly glitch free or preferably when (IF) it becomes a full-fledged game after what feels like very little progression has been made since the alpha release in late 2013.

tl:dr - It could be Garry's Mod 2.0 fun, but it ends up being CoD linear... Great game, but you have to struggle to find a "home".

Ok, I have been playing more rust lately and I must say... It is a lot better with friends. My first review was negative, because of the poor community and other stuff... But I have changed my mind. So, I guess this is my new and improved review.
PROS
-----------
-Fun to play with friends
-Many, MANY servers to chose from
-An Ok community on some servers
-Open world gameplay
-Many bugs, some are really funny
-Updated VERY frequently
CONS
----------
-Pumpjack can't be crafted anymore??
-9 times out of ten, the loot crates have useless junk in them
-Bad community on many servers
-Face clips through your weapon alot (9 times out of 10)
-Holo-Sight reticule keeps disappearing!!
-Many bugs, some are annoying.
-Updates are almost too frequent
So, in conclusion, RUST is and awesome game to play with friends, it is updated frequently, but it has many bugs and a poor community on some servers. I know it is still early access, so it really doesn't bug me all that much.
I recommend this game to people who have friends, or people who can make friends easily. Because in all honesty, this game is extremely boring when you are alone.
Well, that is my new review... I should probably get back to work now.

I haven't yet fully completed the Genocide Run, but I've played enough to make a decent review of the game. Now, I am totally glad I bought the game, but as all games, it has bad stuff. And as usual, I will start with the bad stuff of the game:
The biggest problem I've found so far, is one that has been slowing my playthrough since the start. And it's also something that I can't really understand at all: There's no way to change the controls.
Can I please ask
? The game uses the keys Z, X and C for interactions, and the arrow keys for movement. I literally can't think of a SINGLE GAME on my Steam account that uses those buttons. And I have nearly 200 games. In nearly all games, you would move using the classic wasd, but changing this is not only kind of dumb for a PC only game, but makes playing the game be really unconfortable. I've searched through the Internet for ways to change the controls, and I've found nothing, only if you plug a controller. I forced myself through the game, suffering these controls because I LOVED the story, but if you then decide to play it on a Genocide Run to see all of the stories in the game, you WILL end up tired of them, garanteed. Now, people say that playing with a controller is better... BUT I SHOULDN'T REQUIRE ONE TO PLAY THE GAME! Just think: You usually move in games with your left hand. This game forces you to move with your RIGHT hand, or cross your arms, which I tried and ends up being a pain. And for what I know, left-handed people have it even worse... And the creators haven't done anything about it.
The second problem I see with it, and last issue, is the gameplay. And this is related to the Genocide Run as well. The difficulty spikes are so pointy, they could take an eye out of your skull. Normal enemies are really simple, some bosses have a really GOOD balance of challenge and fun (like Papyrus, he seems to be the best example, as he changes the rules of the battle mid-way through... But it doesn't feel forced at all), and some hard battles like the two last ones on the Pacifist run were hard, challenging, original and still fun, but then you have the two on the Genocide Run. Yeah, there's only two real bosses on the Genocide Run, which is kind of dissapointing on it's own, but you will also have to face a difficulty spike way more crazy than the one before, as it's real boss appears nearly after an hour of killing enemies that really can't fight you at all, and it starts throwing attacks REALLY F#CKING FAST. I was able to beat it because it's movements were easy to master after a few tries... But then the other boss of the Genocide run has a ton of attacks that are randomized, and attacks even faster. To that point I decided to just take a break, and take my time to beat it, as sadly, both issues the game has so far go really good by hand, making enemies that require you to move really fast be more difficult than they already are.
There's a third problem with the game... But that one ain't the devs fault. It's the community of the game. Back when the game released, people would not SHUT THE F#CK UP about the game. What's the problem with that? This game is heavily story-driven, to the point that if you eat too many spoilers, you might as well just ignore buying it and go watch a playthrough on YouTube. And what did the community did? Just that. Spam stuff about the game everywhere. I know they were trying to give the game a good name, so more people go and play it; however that can back-fire really easy. If you haven't yet been spoiled a ton of crap of the game, you must live under a rock, or have no friends that have played it.
All of that being said, what do we have left? A really, really good game.
First of all, the story: It really gets you hooked for more. It's been really well written, and it shows that the creator actually knows what any gamer would do, as he though of nearly everything. And that's another thing...
The game really seems to be alive, to have a mind of it's own, to be self-aware of it. Everything seems to have a reaction, no matter how crazy it might be. It also helps that the forth-wall breaks a ton of times by some characters.
Talking about characters, the game has a ton of them, and let me tell you, you'll find it hard to hate them. Even the enemies have personalities, something you nearly ever see.
Combat is fun, if you stay away from Genocide runs. Feels rewarding to pull it off, and the boss fights are INSANELY EXCITING. It also has a item system which is okay, but suffers because of the controls at times. Save points are also forgiving, and there's usually at least one before those exiciting bosses.
The graphics are pretty. Now, if you hate old-school SNES graphics you might not like them... But I feel like everyone else will. The only thing that I feel awkward about is that the main character doesn't seem to have nearly the same detail as everything else.
The best part of the game, however, is the music. It's just perfect. Seriously. I'm not kidding. F#cking perfect. Well... Except in one part, when Toriel leaves you alone and you have to run for an entire area with a weird theme on the background. That's literally the only moment where I didn't like the soundtrack. And counting that it only takes 20 seconds of probably 8 hours for every run, it's not that bad.
Should you buy this game? Yes. Totally. However, I don't see nearly any sales for it. If you do wish to buy it, put it on your Wishlist, and wait. I mean, the only time I remember seeing it on a sale was on the Winter Sale, and it was only a 20% sale. If you can get it for bellow 5-6€, then it's a must buy. Otherwise wait, as I feel like 10€ might be too much.
And before I end, I must say: I am disgusted by the reviews of the game. I haven't seen nearly ANYONE comment the control issues on their reviews, instead some call it a 10/10, claiming that it's perfect. That's bullsh#t. If you can't make an honest review, please avoid doing it, as it creates problems like these. However, I would say that if the devs fix the controls, it's a solid 9/10, it's only bad part being the difficulty spikes. And maybe the over-used "Annoying Dog", that got old really fast.

tl:dr a really charming enjoyable game ,with loads of likeable and memorable characters, that turns the traditional turn based rpg genre on its head by giving you the option to spare the enemies you fight.
Long version:
Undertale is a turn based RPG with a twist. Where as normally you're expected to cut down every enemy you fight, this game gives you the option to spare them. Whether you do or not is up to you but your choices will have conseqences and the game takes note of everything you do. It takes note of when you die, when you turn the game off to re do something even when you start a new game previous decisions in youre last playthrough get referenced. It really is a game where consequences actually mean something. Add that to the great characters that inhabit the game and it makes for a truly memorable experience. Highly recommend giving this game a go.
Good points:
- i really enjoyed the characters you encounter through the game. The story is great and cango from wacky and goofy to  dark and sombre and it handles it all so well.
- the musical score is fantastic which given its a retro style game is quite an achievement
- the fact the game remembers and references your actions even on later playthroughs is impressive and adds a lot of weight to the decisions you make.
Bad points:
-the retro graphics might put some people off but i strongly advise to not let it put you off trying the game. Theres more to a game than just good graphics and this game is a good example of that.

(depending on how badly they wanna kill you that is. The game is only about 6 hours long, but since it keeps track of what you did, there is some replay value until you get all the endings. TL;DR version: If your sitting on the bench, give the game a try. Get to, or past, the 2nd boss. That way you'll have an idea of what the majority of the game will be like, and if you want to refund the game or not.

This game might be hard to like if you've been exposed to endless internet hype about it, so I'll focus on just one reason why it's worth your time.  Undertale has the best and freshest 'videogame humour' in anything I've seen for a very long time.
By that I don't mean it's just a bunch of gaming jokes in the script, but rather it's packed with little micro twists and surprises on gaming conventions that are genuinely funny.  If you're familiar with older RPGs and gaming in general you'll be in the right frame of mind to some genuinely good "jokes" delivered interactively - in the way that only a game can do it.  The game will definitely put a smile on your face just out of toying with your expectations as you try to finish it, and better than that the comedy varies and stays interesting throughout the length of the game.

I'm just gonna start by saying that I love this game very much. It has a fairly simple story but where it really shines is it's charecters. It is overflowing with interesting, relatable and funny charecters that through great writing and interesting visual design these charecters help to inject a large amount of heart into this world. I mean even the regular charecters that you encounter and fight are all unique and likeable. Undertale has a great mix of moments that range from being absolutely halrious and fun to creepy and ominous to heartfelt and sad. This is all thanks to again these great charecters and a truely spectacular soundtrack. There's a morality system that actualy makes you care. You could kill every charecter if you so wished, or you could spare them in a mechanic that could have so easily been a gimmick but instead is absolutely amazing. It breaks the fourth wall in ways that don't break immersion. Consiquences mean something, so if you do something bad, Undertale will remember. Even if you reset you game, Undertale will remember.  Most of the gameplay comes through either puzzles or bullet hell minigames. The puzzles are quite easy and are more used as either plot devices or comedic tools in some areas so if you highly dislike bullet hell then this might not be for you. If you dislike games that lean more to story then this might not be for you. I personaly think that the artstyle of the games retro graphics look beatiful, but if you really dislike pixle graphics, then this game may not be for you.
In closing Undertale is a game with a heartfelt, meaningful and funny story and charecters with unique game mechanics.

Where to start with this game.
We'll do music.  The music is has a lot of elements from early JRPG's like Earth Bound and Mother, but also pulls in a lot of modern trends.  The OST is amazing, creating vast sound scapes that add greatly to whatever play style you choose.  It's amazing that someone is able to cater each song to a specific character, and the song is also very fitting.  Most of the time, forced compositions like that fall short or over sell.
The story is just as good.  It's hard to find a game that has the ability to combine humor, action, morose, and tension in such a seamless way.  The humor isn't forced, the action is balanced, the tension is never to stressful, and the morose is balence byd the humor.  The story also isn't blatant.  Many games today push the story on you.  If you haven't figured out a puzzle within 10 seconds of walking into a room, the game immidately gives you hints. Instead of leaving plot devices that the player has to pick up on and piece together themselves, the game just gives them to you, hoping that the next high res skybox will make you forget it.
In a world of pushing graphics cards to the max and high res monitors, most woulud say Undertale was doomed.  Traditional pixel art? Why? But pixel art's simplicity is why it works so perfectly.  The simplicity of the art allows for the story to shine through.  The art (like the music) aguments the mood as the game progresses.  Each background pixel is place carefully and concisely.  Everything is there for a reason.
Overall, I can't say enough about Undertale.  With today's gaming market the way it is, with yearly half-arsed releases and sequels for the sake of money, it's always nice to see a well put together gem like this.  Buy it. Play it. Enjoy it.

Rust is... complicated. Writing a review is hard when I have mixed feelings about it, but I'll try. I'll start by saying I would reccomend it, but not if you are easily angered by dying a lot and having everyone try to kill you, regardless if you just spawned.
The gameplay:
Pros- It's a fun game, and has amazing concepts for building and all that. Having to build everything you own is a really really rewarding thing when you step back, look at your base, your gear, and you just say "yeah... yeah I did all this." It's like Minecraft int hat regard. It's just amazing when you make something and really like it too. Guns are crazy hard to use at times, but once you get used to it PVP and PVAI is really fun. Bows are great for starter weapons and they keep adding more great stuff. It's a good game in these regards.
Cons- Alpha, so expect a ton of glitches and bugs at times when they add new stuff. Sometimes stuff breaks, but Gary's pretty on top of getting it fixed. He's a solid developer. For sure. However, he has been making some mistakes in my opinion. These mistakes are that some of the things he's adding, and thing he is implimenting, make it easier to play when you have a group, but if you are solo you better get to be a good shot, and quick, because gathering materials and building as a solo player is not only difficult because of the amount of folks trying to kill you all at once, but also difficult because of the sheer amount of♥♥♥♥♥♥you have to collect to make a respectable, somewhat resilient to raids base. The amount needed is really only obtainable in two ways. You either have a huge group, say 4+ people, or you're only getting supplies by either killing everyone you see who's walking around for what they have on them or raiding someone elses base, or a groups base (while they are offline, and getting the stuff to build C4 and Rockets takes, you guessed it, a big group or killing folks wo are out and about). Pretty much, if you're solo, you have to kill. If you're a group, you can gather but it's easier to just kill everyone. This brings us to...
The Community:
Pros- Finding a group, when you find one, it's really fun. You can build gear and bases on a quick and crazy scale very quickly. Getting into a group, while hard when no one trusts one another, is well worth it. You can trade with people if you want to go try to find blueprints (which you need to build most gear and nice things like external walls and traps). However, this comes at the risk of that person deciding to just shoot you and taking what you have. With that in mind, trade with caution.
Cons- Oh dear God. Everyone's an♥♥♥♥♥hole. Everyone. If you aren't, you get rolled. If you are, you get rolled. If you are an♥♥♥♥♥hole in a group of♥♥♥♥♥holes, you're going to do alright if you guys are good shots and good at raiding. Other than that, expect to die and have people talking crap to you. A... Lot... Like... a whole hell of a lot. Honestly, other than League of Legends, this community is probably one of the most toxic.
In conclusion:
It's great fun when you are with a lot fo people, the game play is great when bugs are being kept up on, and when you are in servers owned by other players you aren't going to run into hacking a whole lot because admins are on it pretty well. The community has it's moments, but we're mostly♥♥♥♥♥holes. I'd give this game a solid 7/10. It's not a bad choice if you want a fun survival PVP game. It's worth the money, but you need to have a lot of time to dedicate, and a thick skin and low temper.

I'm just gonna start by saying that I love this game very much. It has a fairly simple story but where it really shines is it's charecters. In closing Undertale is a game with a heartfelt, meaningful and funny story and charecters with unique game mechanics.

Where to start with this game.
We'll do music.  The music is has a lot of elements from early JRPG's like Earth Bound and Mother, but also pulls in a lot of modern trends.  The OST is amazing, creating vast sound scapes that add greatly to whatever play style you choose.  It's amazing that someone is able to cater each song to a specific character, and the song is also very fitting.  Most of the time, forced compositions like that fall short or over sell.
The story is just as good.  It's hard to find a game that has the ability to combine humor, action, morose, and tension in such a seamless way.  The humor isn't forced, the action is balanced, the tension is never to stressful, and the morose is balence byd the humor.  The story also isn't blatant.  Many games today push the story on you.  If you haven't figured out a puzzle within 10 seconds of walking into a room, the game immidately gives you hints. Instead of leaving plot devices that the player has to pick up on and piece together themselves, the game just gives them to you, hoping that the next high res skybox will make you forget it.
In a world of pushing graphics cards to the max and high res monitors, most woulud say Undertale was doomed.  Traditional pixel art? Why? But pixel art's simplicity is why it works so perfectly.  The simplicity of the art allows for the story to shine through.  The art (like the music) aguments the mood as the game progresses.  Each background pixel is place carefully and concisely.  Everything is there for a reason.
Overall, I can't say enough about Undertale.  With today's gaming market the way it is, with yearly half-arsed releases and sequels for the sake of money, it's always nice to see a well put together gem like this.  Buy it. Play it. Enjoy it.

A friend and I grabbed the game and had never watched any tutorials or anything else. As noob as you can get.  It takes us a while, but we figure out sort of how the game works, how to build, etc.  We spend 4 hours or so building up a base that we thought was pretty sweet - turns out it wasn't.

We decide not to chase our bodies and just re-craft the basic weapons we had. We wouldn't have gotten back in time.
All of a sudden, we hear footsteps.  Then a door opens.  But wait, the door was locked.... OH GOD HE WENT AND TOOK OUR KEYS.  Two naked dudes shot dead on the spot, house ransacked and destroyed, 4-5 hours of gameplay completely gone.
It was as exhilarating as it was devastating. My heart was racing. Never had a gaming experience like that before. Solo play was fun, but playing with at least one friend was one of the better gaming experiences I've had recently - maybe ever.  This is a huge 'recommend' from me if you are even remotely interested in a survival/crafting game.  Fantastic.

And Hyperion's guns get accurate as you shoot them and lose accuracy after not being fired, making them less ideal for snipers than they were in Borderlands 1.
Maliwan makes some of the ONLY elemental guns in the game, with elemental enhancements becoming much rarer for all the other manufacturers. Torgue guns always fire explosive rounds which are great for crowd control but the low velocity makes single-target combat tedious.
Enough. Great game, buy it.

I dont even like "retro" RPG's but this game has consumed my life for a week and a half.
The addition of the bullet hell minigame in battles really keeps you on your toes and stops fights being tedious, every monster has its own attack pattern so you are always learning new ways to fight, at first i thought the "you dont have to kill anyone" would be a bit gimmiky but i was oh so wrong, this game manages to do everything without being heavy handed or cheesy (well except that skeleton's GODDANM PUNS) something that is very easy to do in a game like this.
The highlight of this game, however, is the story, this game has SO MUCH character in every single pixel of this game almost everything you can look at or interact with will tell you a little bit about the area around you or the game as a whole, ALL the monsters (even the random encounters) have a personality, reading this personality is in some ways a game mechanic because you can talk to the monsters and talking to them "correctly" will make them not want to fight you.
I GREATLY enjoyed this game the ENTIRE way and for just 10$ it was easily worthwhile.

Before we start, I just wanna say that if I could give this game a sideways thumb I would. So where to start... Well, first of all, character customization. There is none. The one you get when you start the game is tied to your steam account, and you can't change it. If you wanted to be black, but you got white, too bad. Can't change it. Got female, want to be male? Too bad. Can't change it. Next up, npcs/AI. Well, the only npcs or AI there is in this game are animals, and believe me they are worth talking about. There's a good variety in the animals, like horses, pigs, wolves, bears, and deer. (and they all drop pork, chicken, and bones) Think you're safe from bears because you're in a house? Think again. It'll just phase through your wall. Got this pig cornered, and about to hack it to pieces with your hatchet? Think again, it's suddenly on top of the rock with no effort. Don't get me wrong, it's a fun game. Like, a really fun game. The building system is amazing, and watching/participating in raids are fun, but there are a LOT of bugs. Oh, and I forgot to mention, don't play online. Before you can hit a tree with the rock you start with you'll have a bullet in your brain or a spear in your chest. So in conclusion, only play with friends, whether you play online or on your private server. ONLY. PLAY. WITH. FRIENDS.

Highly creative and inspiring! Undertale is game that progresses based off of the choises you make as the player. The first route you should do is Pacifist, in which you do not hurt a single thing. Each fight you encounter can be escaped in various ways, but you can beat the game without hurting anyone. This is very uncommon in an RPG. There is the Genocide route as well, in which you kill everyone and everything in the game. And then there's many different neutral routes and a ton of different endings you can trigger.
Obviously, you can do whatever you like, don't just take my word. But whatever routes you choose to do, I guarentee you will fall in love with the characters, from the main ones to the supporting ones. All the dialouge, no matter how small, adds something to the game. In fact, much of the dialouge is highly comedic!
Also, the game doesn't really have a fourth wall, an aspect I've always enjoyed in games. Whatever you do, the game will remember and sometimes it prompts dialouge and conversations that some players have not experienced because they haven't played the game exactly like you have.
I know there has been a LOT of hype about this game, but it is not undeserved. I apologize for the fans; they make it hard to want to play this game if you're unfamiliar with it. But if you are looking for a story rich game with multiple layers and angles you can get from it, then please. Play this game.

I got so everlovingly addicted to this game the moment I started it. I lost sleep and played for so long the only time I ever took a break was when I couldn't be a boss a few times and figured out it was 3 AM and I was tired. This game has everything you want:
Gameplay: 10/10
-From the puzzles to the creative battle system, you will NEVER be bored and every enemy is something unique. The ability to spare or kill any monster at your own decision quickly becomes something you actually have to think about, rather than just blow off as something to do to get to the ending.
Story: ∞/10
-The characters, the backstory, the story that you witness and progress through, everything about the story of this game is like it was chiseled from the gods themselves. Being the pacifist I was, I wanted to hug every single monster I saw, no matter whether they were hostile or not. EVERY SINGLE ACTION you take has a consequence somewhere in the story, and don't think that if you make a mistake and reload your save, that you're safe from consequences. It knows. You will laugh, you will cry, and you will cheer, and everything in between.
Music: ∞∞/10
-I know, I may be heavily biased with this review, but cut me some slack, especially here. Hundreds of scores of amazing music just makes this game. Any benign moment feels like a huge part of the story with the right background sounds, and god dammit if Toby Fox didn't do an amazing job here too. There are some scores in the soundtrack that I can't listen to now because I end up nearly crying, and I'm proud to say that.
So do I recommend this game?
You bet your [soul] I do.

Date:  1/29/16
Review Number: 4
Game: RUST
From (Creator Publisher): Facepunch Studios
Played On: Steambox with Steam Controller
Steam Price as of Review: $19.99
Total Time played: 60 Minutes (Had to drag myself away)
Review:
As someone who is a big fan of the crafting/survival games, and who has sunk many hours into the android version of Terraria, I am always excited to get into a new game like RUST, and the last time I tried was on my older laptop that managed around two frames a minute, so that was a bust.  When it came up on the randomizer,  I couldn’t wait to get started.  Now, as someone whose experience with first person survival was extended playthroughs of the Forest, I was prepared for difficulty, hardship, and frequent death.  I did get those things in abundance, though I was surprised at how many of them were really my fault.  In the hour I played I died four times.  Half of them without my rock, because I had accidentally thrown it away and lost it until I learned how the buttons were mapped on the steam controls.  One I was shot two minutes in because apparently  its fun to shoot a naked guy holding a rock and a torch, and the fourth time I was actually enjoying myself until I accidentally ran through a spike trap in the dark after burning out the aforementioned torch.  And I still had fun.  RUST is the sort of game that I usually pick up and play for like thirty hours, build up a lot of things, get shot a bunch, then get bored and move on from.  But what makes games like these so much fun is that when I come stumbling back, it’s like a whole new game is waiting for me, and I get sucked in again.
Game’s Fate:Kept, should stay for a while
Buy/No Buy: Honestly love this one.  Unless you’re explicitly choosing between this and The Forest, my recommendation is Buy Buy Buy.

Highly creative and inspiring! Undertale is game that progresses based off of the choises you make as the player. The first route you should do is Pacifist, in which you do not hurt a single thing. Each fight you encounter can be escaped in various ways, but you can beat the game without hurting anyone. This is very uncommon in an RPG. There is the Genocide route as well, in which you kill everyone and everything in the game. And then there's many different neutral routes and a ton of different endings you can trigger.
Obviously, you can do whatever you like, don't just take my word. But whatever routes you choose to do, I guarentee you will fall in love with the characters, from the main ones to the supporting ones. All the dialouge, no matter how small, adds something to the game. In fact, much of the dialouge is highly comedic!
Also, the game doesn't really have a fourth wall, an aspect I've always enjoyed in games. Whatever you do, the game will remember and sometimes it prompts dialouge and conversations that some players have not experienced because they haven't played the game exactly like you have.
I know there has been a LOT of hype about this game, but it is not undeserved. I apologize for the fans; they make it hard to want to play this game if you're unfamiliar with it. But if you are looking for a story rich game with multiple layers and angles you can get from it, then please. Play this game.

Highly creative and inspiring! Undertale is game that progresses based off of the choises you make as the player. The first route you should do is Pacifist, in which you do not hurt a single thing. Each fight you encounter can be escaped in various ways, but you can beat the game without hurting anyone. This is very uncommon in an RPG. There is the Genocide route as well, in which you kill everyone and everything in the game. And then there's many different neutral routes and a ton of different endings you can trigger.
Obviously, you can do whatever you like, don't just take my word. But whatever routes you choose to do, I guarentee you will fall in love with the characters, from the main ones to the supporting ones. All the dialouge, no matter how small, adds something to the game. In fact, much of the dialouge is highly comedic!
Also, the game doesn't really have a fourth wall, an aspect I've always enjoyed in games. Whatever you do, the game will remember and sometimes it prompts dialouge and conversations that some players have not experienced because they haven't played the game exactly like you have.
I know there has been a LOT of hype about this game, but it is not undeserved. I apologize for the fans; they make it hard to want to play this game if you're unfamiliar with it. But if you are looking for a story rich game with multiple layers and angles you can get from it, then please. Play this game.

Gameplay: 10/10
-From the puzzles to the creative battle system, you will NEVER be bored and every enemy is something unique. The ability to spare or kill any monster at your own decision quickly becomes something you actually have to think about, rather than just blow off as something to do to get to the ending.
Story: ∞/10
-The characters, the backstory, the story that you witness and progress through, everything about the story of this game is like it was chiseled from the gods themselves. Being the pacifist I was, I wanted to hug every single monster I saw, no matter whether they were hostile or not. EVERY SINGLE ACTION you take has a consequence somewhere in the story, and don't think that if you make a mistake and reload your save, that you're safe from consequences. It knows. You will laugh, you will cry, and you will cheer, and everything in between.
Music: ∞∞/10
-I know, I may be heavily biased with this review, but cut me some slack, especially here. Hundreds of scores of amazing music just makes this game. Any benign moment feels like a huge part of the story with the right background sounds, and god dammit if Toby Fox didn't do an amazing job here too. There are some scores in the soundtrack that I can't listen to now because I end up nearly crying, and I'm proud to say that.
So do I recommend this game?

An interesting twist on the original Borderlands plots; involving the destruction of a megacorporation. The graphics, even on minimum, are similiar to that of the first, with slight improvements, such as the implementation of Nvidia's PhysX. Being only 6 hours into the game, I can quite clearly see that this game will be an entertainment source for months to come.

Borderlands 2. The game that took 45 hours of my life at release, and I still haven't experienced everything. It's a gem, a true masterpiece. There's just so much content that it blows my mind. So many locations, so many interesting characters, a great story, great stylish graphics, and the best part? So much ♥♥♥♥ing loot that you just don't want to leave behind. There's so many weapon varieties, shield varieties, class mod varieties, that it just blows my balls off. Weapons can have slag, fire, shock, corrisive, freezing, and highly explosive abilities. Shields also have these, when your shield runs out it explodes and damages enemies nearby by covering them in something. The guns all have varying stats that go along with those properties, and they all look so unique and different.
It's honestly absurd. Just with the base game alone you'll have hundreds of hours of gameplay. The game of the year edition that comes with all the expansions and an extra 11 levels? Although I haven't tried them yet (just bought them as I'm writing this) will blow you even more away and make you sink even more hours into this game. This game has personality, this game has the loot, this game is like sex. It's worth every single penny.
