I bought this game thinking it was a survival game, but the survival mechanics are weak and may as well not be there, because I don't notice them at all when I play.
Sure, I gotta eat a pumpkin here and there to get health (until I reach full health anyway because after that it's basically pointless), but the hunger and thirst go down so slow and fill up so much from eating/drinking anything that it seems as though the actual survival isn't important to the gameplay at all.
The only things you will need to "survive" in this game are:
1.) The *WORST* community of gamers I have seen in any game in a long time. (including a lot of hackers)
2.) Occasional lag spikes that WILL get you killed by another player who will then take all your stuff you just worked for.
That's about it. The occasional bear or wolf may kill you, but there aren't many of those out there. I've seen only two bears and one wolf my entire 40 hours of playing.
* Regarding point #1, like really, if you are easily offended then DON'T play this game -- You will see racial slurs / bad language in general, crude drawings of d*cks all over the map, and the community kills on sight, or will say that they're friendly only to get close enough to kill you easier.
If you are going to play this game, here is what you should do:  Get a gun as fast as you can. Don't work for anything, because no one that frequents this game does any work for themselves considering they can just kill the people who are just starting out and steal the resources they collected... So you get a gun, and kill everyone you see that is harvesting items you will probably need (trees, rocks, cloth, leather, etc.) because that is the only way this game will be fun.
However, if you would rather be the one harvesting resources from trees and rocks, and don't want to turn into an enormous neckbeard-jackass, then DON'T play this game, because all of your work WILL get ruined by other people that found a gun before you and decided to kill you because it's easier to get loot that way.

I don't want to spoil this game for any one who hasn't played it, but in short; Undertale is a RPG that's willing to take everything you know about the genre, and challenge it to a godlike level, while still remaining a "Role-Playing Game". As you play, be wary of the term 'Role-Playing', as you may find that as time goes on your part in the game is more than just a mere 'role'.
I genuinely love this game, and hope it's appreciated for years at the very least, because there isn't a single RPG (out of 100's of classics I myself have played, like Chrono Trigger, FF7 etc.) that has handled emotion and character development as well as Undertale.
Funny,original and very well written. If like me you have grown up loving rpgs and feel the genre has become somewhat stale then you will find Undertale incredibly refreshing.

It takes a great deal for me to write a review about a game, as I generally don't feel it necessary to do it. However, Undertale, a game by Toby Fox, has proved to be an amazing game. From the story that has a great deal of lore, to the characters big and small, to all of those tear jerker moments (I'm not one to get to emotional for a game, but this one surely gets to me) The price for this game is fair, as it takes maybe around 6 hours to beat, but the replayability to this game is HUGE. The different runs you can do where you don't kill anyone or you kill everyone or a mix of the two, makes a LOT of different dialogue options, and lets you get tastes of more of the story, which still isn't 100% clear, but what you do get is an amazing game.
Also, thank you Toby Fox for making a game that has caused me to rage really hard on one boss (Those that see this and have played will probably get it).

I will admit, even after spoiling myself a bit and knowing what to expect in the game...
Tears were still shed.
Thank you Toby Fox.

Every bit as good as Borderlands 1 and even a little bit better. The dialogue is unnaturally hilarious, the plot is refreshingly engaging, and the gameplay is a marvel of balance and badassery.
The "random" gun system is still spectacular and unique, but new, manufacturer-specific gun modifications inspire more brand loyalty than Borderlands 1. For example, all Dahl guns use burst fire when aiming down the sights which makes them less desirable for players who enjoy full-auto machine guns or one-shot sniper rifles. And Hyperion's guns get accurate as you shoot them and lose accuracy after not being fired, making them less ideal for snipers than they were in Borderlands 1.
Maliwan makes some of the ONLY elemental guns in the game, with elemental enhancements becoming much rarer for all the other manufacturers. Torgue guns always fire explosive rounds which are great for crowd control but the low velocity makes single-target combat tedious.
Enough. Great game, buy it.

Heavily inspired by Earthbound, you play a kid who is trapped in the underground world where monsters live. Almost none of them are bad but they all seem to want something from you or are afraid of you so you get the choice to ACT things out peacfully like a puzzle or FIGHT with very basic combat. There's a special ending for pacifism and a gamebreaking ending for genocide. I recommend kill one person, spare another and just play as you like on the neutral route for your first run.
Characters are great in case you haven't seen the fans gushing over them, story gets real deep at times, combat is a lot more interesting. Offensivly it ranges from figuring out each enemy with actions and just bashing them over the head. The real kick is in the defense where you have to move your 'soul' around to avoid bullets. In most fights I didn't think it was too difficult but then again I've lost so many times to Ran from Perfect Cherry Blossom. Regardless Undyne will be the first real challenge in combat and in Genocide route certain enemies really mean business.
If you haven't been spoiled to what happens in this game I highly recommend playing it and locking yourself away until you've done a neutral route (it's okay, you can beat it in about 4 hours). I can understand the fans get annoying but for a few hours just ignore them, get this game, and never use Tumblr in the first place.

It is time to return to Pandora and face the madness of that planet once more.
After the events of the first game, where the original Vault Hunters learned that the mythical Vault they were looking for wasn't what it was rumored to be, they've gone into hiding.
And now, the Hyperion Corporation has arrived on the planet with its boss Handsome Jack with the intent to bring "peace and order" to it.
However, once more all is not as it seems.
Four new Vault Hunters are tricked while on the way onboard a train to Handsome Jack's HQ for a job to look for a new Vault, the train is a trap with soldiers and robots.
Just barely surviving the backstab, the Vault Hunters set out to find the original Vault Hunters and team up with them to kick Hyperion and Handsome Jack off the planet before he unleashes something terrifying on it.
Countless new weapons await you in the loot chests and you will also meet some familiar faces from the original, including weapon and ammo merchant Marcus and Dr Zed.

Solid game. Not particularly impressive as the fanbase appears to make it out to be.
The battles are definitely unique, but I think they can be fleshed out more. Killing enemies is just a cycle of attacking and dodging bullets, Kind of wished there were more ways to bring out offense i.e. Paper Mario. Of course sparing is the main mechanic. However, once you find the strategy for sparing an enemy, then battles just become monotonous from that point. Boss battles are hella cool because they have multiple attacks wheras regular enemies have as much as two. All boss battles are memorable in some way based on their attacks, the scenario, or the conversations.
Characters are memorable too from the loving mother Toriel and the silly Papyrus to the demonic Flowey. The humor got me to chuckle a few times. However, I don't think the humor isn't really for everyone, as the humor here is very much goofy or overdramatic. I know some people that aren't for that kind of thing. I for one am fine with it.
The art style definitely makes characters and environments stand out. Battles are in black and white, but that causes you to pay attention to enemies' physical design rather than color scheme. Environments are fine, nothing outstanding.
One thing I can say for sure, music is absolutely sick tho. Lots of styles represented here, a good chunk are chiptune. Glad to see breakcore in the game's "your best nightmare" song, as I think it fits the style of the  battle scenario it is in. I definitely get Earthbound vibes from the art style and music together.
Remember that sparing, killing, and overworld choices affect that outcome of the game. I think it takes several playthroughs of Undertale to truly appreciate Undertale's creativity. Seriously, this game has a lot of thought into the details of player consequences. Also, the game is pretty short. An experienced player can probably beat it in a day if you're determined (heh), but this game is about taking in the details through multiple playthroughs. This is more visual novel than video game IMO.
Overall, solid game for $10.00 imo, but don't expect so highly of the game like I did. I expected it to be the best game ever which kind of brought me to be more critical of the game's faults. The game's RPG mechanics get old real fast, but the characters, music, and story are great.

The story, dialogue, and characters of Undertale are charming, and the conflict resolution is a change from the ordinary, but that being said there are a lot of things wrong with this game:
1. "Retro art": Yes, we get it, it's retro, just like old games used to be. While it's interesting to see how much the game is able convey through a minimalist approach, the limitations of the visuals for the budget of the game seem to be "taking the easy way out". Don't want to put in long hours with amazing graphics? Use minimalist graphics and limit your potential! That's why I draw in MS Paint; so nobody realized I am a bad artist because I use a terrible medium as my excuse.
2. The sound: Again, retro, hooray. Some neat-o arrangements, but once again intentionally limited to "retro" style. You can't critique the peace as if it was a sweeping heart-wrenching orchestral piece if it sounds like the background song from a Final Fantasy area. The renditions people have done of the game music on YouTube is enough to show how much better it would have been with a less limited medium.
3. The characters: Considering that they were literally 2d, many of the "behaviors" of the characters were surprisingly deep... and then others seemed like obnoxious forced anime tropes. Alphys, Undyne, Mettaton, especially considering the depth of the story you find behind Alphys during the pacifist playthrough, she/it was surprisingly cardboard. "Look here is a nerdy tumblr user and her 'too-perfect' fish-lady ninja naruto lover." On one hand a person could say that all the characters were all just innocent and childish, "Let's date. This is a date? Date harder. How does one date? Spaghette." but then when they're also supposed to be portrayed as a crazy-intelligent scientist with a troubled past, there is a major continuity error. Is this character supposed to be clueless and adorable? Or world-weary and emotionally devastated?
4. The dialogue: For as much as this game got right, it got a whole lot horribly wrong. Memes? Really? You want to make a timeless game that breaks the paradigm of all the others in its genre... yet your source of humor is memes? Internet references? As a result the game is dated and will only become more obscure over time instead of classic.
4. The gameplay: The dialogue options and unique battle scenarios are interesting for the first time or to you see them, but it gets to a point where it just gets repetitive. Oh the seahorse showed up again? Let me spam "flex" until I can walk 20 more steps for the repeat of this Pokemon encounter.
5.

Ah Borderlands...you are my comfort drug. I am currently 34 and I have played games my entire life. With every "era" of gaming, there has been one game that I call my "rainy day" game. Its usually a game that I have logged hundreds of hours in but it never gets old. Borderlands 2 is currently that game and has been for some time now.
Borderlands does so many things right in so many ways:
GRAPHICS:
The graphical style may be a turn-off to some who just view screen shots or video but it works so well in this game, I could not image it being any different. It would only take away from the game if the styling was changed.
GAMEPLAY:
Borderlands is definitely a first-person-shooter at heart. It has all the familiar controls and mechanics of a fps but it is not your typical COD clone. It has an underlying RPG element at its core. As you complete quests and kill enemies, you gain experience. You can then spend this experience in one of three skill trees (much like Diablo 2). These trees drastically change the play style of your character in often hilarious ways. This feature adds extreme depth and replay-ability to Borderlands.
STORY/UNIVERSE:
Borderlands takes nothing for serious. The main antagonist, Handsome Jack, is one of the funniest characters I've ever encountered in a game. There are so many laugh-out-load moments scattered everywhere in the game. Some are tucked away in a quest line, some you just stumble across while exploring and others are in the main storyline. Borderlands captures humor perfectly which adds greatly to its replayibility and enjoyment.
MULTIPLAYER:
This category would be the only place that I would fault the game for. Granted, its still insanely fun to play multiplayer. After I beat the main story line, I started playing exclusively online with others. I just think that the network code could use a tad more work. There are some rare syncing and disconnect issues but they are not frequent enough to be much of an issue.
TLDR: This game is a masterpiece. Its Funny, Fun, and Repayable for hundreds of hours. It is an amazing value. Do not hesitate to purchase.

Here's the issues with DayZ (With all due respect to the developers). This game, as I understand it, has been in development for several years right now. I understand that this is an early access game, but this is getting silly. I'm giving this review in honest hope that the developers will see it and understand what is going wrong with this potetially AMAZING game.
Bohemia! Dammint, Bohemia, your vision for this game is wonderful, and it could be something great! but rather than focusing on key gameplay aspects, like making the hunger and thirst system more realistic (Because I'm pretty sure I'm not gonna go from having 4 cans of beans to starving to death within a few hours) you add more guns! Don't get me wrong, I love guns, and every time I find a new one I shiver in happiness a bit. But all these guns don't mean♥♥♥♥♥♥if your zombie AI is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and your gameplay is fundamentally broken in several aspects!
Okay. Let's go into the step-by-step.
For everything DayZ does right, it does another thing wrong, or something is broken. A lot of these broken things should be priorities for fixing.
First off, the hunger and thirst system. I love many ways in which this is handled. You will become thirstly from eating dry food, become sick from drinking tainted water, ect. The issue, as I mentioned, is that your hunger and thirst rates are ♥♥♥♥ING REDICULOUS. It's obvious that this is supposed to be a difficult game, but goddammit it's already hard enough without having to eat a five-course meal every hour or starve to death. The thirst, I tend to be a bit more understanding of that, as yeah, when you're running around like a maniac from zombies, that tends to get you pretty thirsty. But the hunger rate is just stupid. In a survival game, this should be a PRIORITY FIX.
Second, the gameplay itself.
This is not ♥♥♥♥ing Call of Duty, kiddos. There is no quick scope or twitch shooting. Ammunition is a precious commodity worth it's weight in gold, as it should be. Every shot is a precious thing. Unfortunately, zombies have a tendancy to run around like maniacal chickens with their heads cut off, speeding across your screen like a ten year old with ADHD who just spotted Thomas the Tank Engine in a store window. If you're not some kind of crack shot, you're gonna have a bad time with semi-auto weapons. I could touch on the PvP aspects of gameplay here, but I won't, because I feel like a game should be able to stand on it's own without multiplayer first.
I mentioned the zombies. Dear god, the zombies. When they're not standing around making your generic guy-with-a-cold noises, they're moving faster than a speeding bullet with no sense of direction. It's a refreshing change from the runners that just come straight at you at first, but then it just gets annoying and frustrating. You'll get a lot of cheap deaths from zombies, even if you're avoiding them like you should be, when they do things like smack you through walls or suddenly veer in a completely random direction. I've even seen zombies run AWAY from me, then come circling back. If there was a literal definition of a chicken running around with it's head cut off, it would be DayZ zombies.
The animations and graphics are also rather out-of-date. This is a game from a couple years ago, and it shows. There's a lot of stupidly low-res textures, expecially with buildings and the mysterious un-openable doors. Player models are stiff and look like they haven't been updated from ARMA 2 in the least. In short, the graphics and animation are TERRIBLE. TERR. IB. LE. They're not remotely up to bar with even other modern games in Alpha! Games that have been in development for much less time!
I'm sure a lot of you guys reading this are thinking "But Demon, you haven't even touched on the multiplayer! That's the thing that makes DayZ great!" Damn straight. Without the multiplayer, this game would be a trash heap. DayZ is in essence a platform for people to act out their post-apocolyptic dreams. You ever want to form a group and help other survivors? Or would you rather kill other survivors to prolong your own survival? This is the key part of DayZ, and, in my personal opinion, the reason so many play it. DayZ is an open world for you to explore and make friends and foes in.
But my beef is that a game should be more than that. DayZ doesn't need any NPC's or story mode, in my opinion, but what it does need is serious gameplay fixing, hardcore graphical updates, and more focus on gameplay rather than nice fluffy bits like extra guns. Bohemia, you're doing this backwards. Get the gameplay working first. Make everything ELSE go nice and smooth. THEN you can add in the cool fluffy bits like extra guns and custom ammo types and the like.
I could go into more detail about other aspects of the game, but I won't, because I feel like this is a long enough review as it stands. In conclusion, I rate DayZ as a 5/10. It's rather average. Without multiplayer taken into account, the score drops to a 3/10. I understand that this is an alpha game, but to have been and development this long and not have all this baisic♥♥♥♥♥♥finished is simply unnacceptable. This is less me saying "Don't buy this game" and more me saying "Devs, get your damn♥♥♥♥♥♥together."
Summary: Rated 5/10. Serious gameplay issues, horrid, out-of-date graphics and animations, wonderful concept, out-of-the-park multiplayer. Average game with multiplayer taken into account. Rated 3/10 without multiplayer in the equation. Baisic design issues and lack of concentrated effort on important gameplay aspects by the developers.

I didn't think that buying a game with more than 28,000 positive reviews and a few hundred negative reviews would be a risk, but this game didn't hold my attention. I was impressed by an early twist and thought that the game would continue to challenge my expectations, but for the most part, between some humorous encounters with some charming characters, there isn't much to this game.
The puzzles are a snorefest, far too easy to keep you coming back to the game. It seems that they basically exist purely as filler between encounters with the main characters. The combat (which is basically the same whether you choose to be merciful or not) involves dodging pixelated attacks using the arrow keys. This, also, is certain not to be the reason you would enjoy this game- it is extremely repetitive, especially after repeating the exact same sequence in a given boss fight 4 times in a row (after getting "GAME OVER") until you memorize it and advance. Even the story itself is pretty damn thin, at least as far as I can tell more than 5 hours into the game. Pretty much all the game has going for it is some geuinely funny characters that, at least in my opinion, aren't enough to make this game worth playing.
Lastly, I'll just add that I don't think that this is a case of me "not getting it." I feel like I had a pretty clear view of what the game was trying to be, but I just didn't find it as mindblowing as everyone else seems to consider it to be. I'm sure there were a few more interesting twists in the story ahead of where I left off, but it just didn't seem to be worth suffering through who knows how much more intolerable gameplay to get to them.
This is a game where you cry at the endings and just feel great playing it. Finally a game that doesn't rely on graphics or new tech to completely please a player. Just a perfect game.

Solid game. Not particularly impressive as the fanbase appears to make it out to be.
The battles are definitely unique, but I think they can be fleshed out more. Killing enemies is just a cycle of attacking and dodging bullets, Kind of wished there were more ways to bring out offense i.e. Paper Mario. Of course sparing is the main mechanic. However, once you find the strategy for sparing an enemy, then battles just become monotonous from that point. Boss battles are hella cool because they have multiple attacks wheras regular enemies have as much as two. All boss battles are memorable in some way based on their attacks, the scenario, or the conversations.
Characters are memorable too from the loving mother Toriel and the silly Papyrus to the demonic Flowey. The humor got me to chuckle a few times. However, I don't think the humor isn't really for everyone, as the humor here is very much goofy or overdramatic. I know some people that aren't for that kind of thing. I for one am fine with it.
The art style definitely makes characters and environments stand out. Battles are in black and white, but that causes you to pay attention to enemies' physical design rather than color scheme. Environments are fine, nothing outstanding.
One thing I can say for sure, music is absolutely sick tho. Lots of styles represented here, a good chunk are chiptune. Glad to see breakcore in the game's "your best nightmare" song, as I think it fits the style of the  battle scenario it is in. I definitely get Earthbound vibes from the art style and music together.
Remember that sparing, killing, and overworld choices affect that outcome of the game. I think it takes several playthroughs of Undertale to truly appreciate Undertale's creativity. Seriously, this game has a lot of thought into the details of player consequences. Also, the game is pretty short. An experienced player can probably beat it in a day if you're determined (heh), but this game is about taking in the details through multiple playthroughs. This is more visual novel than video game IMO.
Overall, solid game for $10.00 imo, but don't expect so highly of the game like I did. I expected it to be the best game ever which kind of brought me to be more critical of the game's faults. The game's RPG mechanics get old real fast, but the characters, music, and story are great.

Dayz is one of my most favorite games, I began with the mod and happily play StandAlone at least once a day.
+ You play the game how you want to - People seem to complain the most about bandits and how they are "game breaking" but thats just how they play, yes a majority are bandits (I try not to be in most situations) but there are friendly players out there, if you want a mostly "Freindly only gameplay" then join a server that disallows bandits or really play expiermental! (BUT WHAT IS EXPIERMENTAL) Dayz Exp is the next patch before it is released onto the stable servers, (to do this right click dayz select properties then click betas and should be on the drop down bar) with exp you do get to enjoy the new things but whats more important is that the Devs are relying on the community to help find these game breaking bugs and to find even minor bugs like images not showing up or animations breaking! and you haven't quiet enjoyed the game until you befriend some one, who quickly turns on you when you both manage to find and kill a cow, then you manage to best him in hand to hand combat and eat him alive....
+ The majority of guns, when I look at other games (these I do not own) for example H1Z1 there are a total of 10 weapons (4 of these are just crossbow and 3 bow and arrows) there are 38 Weapons (more to come!) but what I really love about this is the fact that you can acutally customize your weapons. Your walking around in the tree line waiting for a target to kill or rob when a shot rings out and you see sparks off your scope, you run instinctively and hide, then you realize that your scope has been damaged NO WORRIES! you have a back up wore PU Scope in your back pack. (and being able to camo your guns is a nice touch)
+ The devs DO update - the devs for this game once a week put out dev notes of what they are doing and plan to do in the future, people are complaining about the speed of these updates that they want more and more updates, but the devs once a month let out a big update adding new items, new AI for zombies, and zombies (finally), one must understand dayz is on a more complicated engine then those of rust, or H1Z1.
+ Now you actually have to survive - This is for the more recent updates, and this is probably my favorite thing, I played the 0.57 exp and loved it because I was forced to survive. I wasn't give a Can of beans and a soda with a way to open my beans in my first house! no the first thing I found was a extra shirt which I promptly tore into rags, then I spent 10 to 15 minuets gather apples for my adventure inland. When I had gotten all ready I headed out looting along the way finding next to nothing but keeping my alive by picking every apple tree I saw, I then found rope quickly went into the woods for sticks came back with a rabbit trap! Set up the trap caught a rabbit (ended up cooking and eating later) contiuned travling north! this is when I met who i thought was a friend we introduced and we were both hungry didn't have much food or water but we traveled together. Suddenly we spot a cow in the field we both sneak about and promptly beat it to death, then I started cleaning and gathering meat when my friend started stabbing me in the back... so I started running pulled out my pitchfork, turned around and started swinging. I later enjoyed a feast of Cow and Human. but with crafting becoming more important and farming now becoming very important to survive it really feels like a "zombie survival" (for a while I didn't encounter zombies which frustrated me because zombies add flavor to the game, but once I encountered a horde I had to run for my life I nearly died from starvation because there were so many following me once one with give up another would make a noise and it would follow it ;-;)
Prison Island + and - I have mixed feeling about prison island as loot seems to be sporadic there, every server i've been on whether hive or public always has clothing and items there, and most of the times a lot of it, and I don't like that becuase I could just swim over there and get a large enough inventory to not have problems for a long time, and with the possible weapon spawns like AK's and such it makes people really just get weapons and head back up the coast to new spawn areas. On the other hand when it comes to combat, the prison island is almost how I wish combat was in the larger cities like cherno or electro, it's very narrow and fast paced one mistake and you end up dead. You might be traped in a hall way with no way out, the only thing to do is hope that they get unpatient before you do and come into your ambush.
But for those of you complaining about game breaking glitches be sure to post them to the dayz feedback tracker!
) I want an improved game to play and for others to enjoy as well!

Overall, I think of it as a survival PVP game but not something fast paced like Call of Duty but a game where evertime you die, the next life will always be different. It is also the only game ive ever played that gives me an adrenaline rush as im in a firefight.

Grab your friends and jump back to the viscious planet of Pandora again! This time we'll be fighting a new horde of monsters, bandits, robots, midgets, and an all new evil big boss: Handsome Jack, who wish to terminate every single person who tries to stop him - and of course, including YOU! (and your friends, but yeaah who cares?)
Bazillion guns just got bazillion-dier and badassness just got badass-endier!
...okay, I made that last one up.

This game provides an excellent combination of humour, entertainment, and shiny, shiny things to collect and then use to do violence upon the somewhat twisted world of Pandora. Gearbox have clearly upped the ante and this game is a clear improvement over the original Borderlands. I've enjoyed my time here and the DLC has been worth the extra money in my opinion.
Graphically, it shares the same 'cell-shading' style as its predecessor. The benefit of this is that you'll be able to run this game well on a less powerful machine. Don't get me wrong, it looks superb on a top of the line rig, but I also play this game on an Alienware M11x R3 with a GT 540M card, and it's still very playable at 720p and medium settings.
Overall, I've spent 300+ hours on this game and I think it has given me real value for money. Like all games, this is best enjoyed with friends!

I normally don't write reviews about games, but this game is the exception.
Undertale's story is pretty simple; you are a human who falls down into the world of monsters, a race banished into the underground by humans long ago. The beginning of the game already starts off strong. Everything you thought you knew about RPGs or even gaming will be challenged on an emotional, rational and hilarity level. This game goes outside the box in many ways, sometimes even literally!
I have cried, laughed, and almost sh*t my pants with this game. The characters are lovable, the story is engaging, and each play through will be completely different. And I don't mean different in the sense that you find new things through each play through (which you will), but on a whole different level that I have never seen a game do before!
I highly recommend avid RPG players to pick this game up! And even if you are a casual gamer I recommend this game just because of how much fun it is.
Don't let the graphics fool you, this game is the most engaging and exciting game you will have the pleasure to play in your entire life and it will change the way you view the possibilities of gaming.
I give this game a 10/10, and not a lot of games I have played have ever reached such a number on my personal list,
Buy this game. Now.

Undertale is a really good game, and you should probably play it. That's it. To say any more about the game would probably ruin it for you.
It seems to me undertale is becoming one of those games people don't shut up about. Like Minecraft, or god forbid, FNaF. And it's kind of a bittersweet thing. With a huge fanbase comes huge expectations for a game. Everybody and their mother is singing the praises of this game, and while I love this game to death, and it deserves recognition, the popularity is in a way doing the game a disservice. Not to sound like some kind of hipster, of course, but with all the voices of the internet calling the game the second coming of Jesus Christ, it's easy to come into the game with inflated expectations. And when you come into a game expecting the best thing ever, you'll undoubtedly be let down every time.
My advice is to just play the game, and listen to no one. And avoid the fanbase like the damn plague. It's a good rule of thumb to do so with most things, but here it's especially important. To come into this game expecting something that will change gaming and make you have a religious experience and give you a free pot of golden hookers is going to result in you being very disappointed. Try and enjoy the game for what it is, and for the experience
have with it, not for what other people tell you.

I'm recommending the game, simply because it's a pretty unique game. Not only in how it presents itself, but also because it's got some clever writing.
However, the developer should be castigated for denying people the right to explore the content as they see fit. Specifically, resetting the game back to stock should be either a documented option, or a process. I take a dim view of any dev that delibrately throws roadblocks down in front of users who wish to explore all of the content they paid money to experience. This developer has violated that by creating a save system that punches the user. This is never cool to do, even when you're trying to present a concept.
Despite this, it's a fun game with a fun and vibrant cast of characters. The developer should be commended for this.
Do I think it's worthy of all the hype: I do not. It's not *that* special. It is way overhyped for what it is. While it has some unique qualities and some interesting presentation....it's way way overhyped.
You gotta play it to understand it. And don't let either the rabid fans OR the haters potentially ruin your experience!

Is Undertale the best JRPG ever? No.
Is Undertale the best PC game ever? No.
Is Undertale the best Indie game ever? No.
Is Undertale the best game of 2015? No.
But ultimately, is Undertale a good game? Absolutely yes.
If you had not purchased Undertale yet, it's likely that you have already heard of it. Undertale has gotten quite a lot of attention throughout 2015 and will continue to do so for a while. You might even call it 'overrated', though that will still remain a subjective term. Yes, Undertale's fanbase is well known for it's constant blabbering about this point, and I can see why people get annoyed by it. I often avoid games myself that get overhyped, because my expectations become very high. But like literally every fanbase in the world, there is a light of hope. Do not let the fanbase, haters of the fanbase and haters of the haters of the fanbase influence your decision.
Undertale is a game that plays with your emotions and succeeds. I am known as a man who does not feel emotions that much, especially not when it comes to any form of fictional media. But I really liked to play through the neutral and true pacifist run, and making friends, only to make me feel like an extremely bad person when going through the genocide route. The game makes you feel like a bad person, because you are. The entire atmosphere changes, and boss battles become way harder to let you know you're making the wrong decision. It even gives you the chance to abort the route. Now that is good game design and a good example of a game playing with your feelings. Every decision you make matters, and you can feel it. I don't consider the characters to be that good, but it's the writing and overall humour of the game that make you care about them and the future of all monsters.
The gameplay is unique because unlike most JRPGs, it's more of a bullethell shooter with variations, like platforming. It's a unique form of gameplay, and because Undertale is a pretty short game (one route should take 5 hours max, can be lower depending on your skill and experience with JRPGs), the gameplay doesn't get boring very quick. For example, if this gameplay mechanic was in a 40 hour long JRPG, chances are high you're getting bored of it towards the end. It also helps that literally every enemy in their game have their own attacks, making you think how to avoid them. But probably Undertale's most unique asset is sparing enemies. The main goal of the game is to not kill any monsters and instead befriend them, and you can do that by showing mercy. You might have to do some actions before being able to (like, complimenting them), but as a reward you still get money.
Overall, Undertale is a game with a bit too much hype going on for it, but it's definitely a recommendation. Try not to let anyone influence you, and see if this game is something for you. You might just find a gem on your hands here. Or not.

For new players, join a server with 0 people on it and experiment with the game first before you go in on a full server (as I said, you will die many, many, many times with other players around).
Pros:
- Great survivor gameplay.  Bandages for bleeding problems, thirst, hunger, energy, etc.
- Finding a group of friendly players can be hours of the most fun gameplay I have participated in.
- Graphics are "ok" (more in cons though)
Cons:
- Game is horribly not optimized yet.  People with Titan(s) still have trouble on highest settings when they walk into town.  Keep graphics set low if you don't have a super machine!
- Community is somewhat "evil".  They will kill you many times.
In all, I would definitely recommend getting this game in alpha while the price is lower than when/if it goes full release.

This review has been mostly spoiler free because it's almost cardinal sin to spoil this game.
Hell, even in the game files there is a playable music file that says in different text to speech profiles that you shoudln't share the plot with anybody (also looking through the game files can technically be considered part of the experience but I won't go into that).
This is one of the reasons I despise playthroughs of this game because people can just watch the story unfold FOR FREE ("wow tell me what is new, lets players have been spoiling stories since their conception" Yea but Toby Fox deserves every single dime for the story he wrote plus indie developers don't make nearly as much money as big publishers do unless you're talking about Markus Perrson).
Actually i'm going to condradict myself and say that this game has one big flaw, the story outshines the gameplay.
And that's not to say the gameplay is bad at all in fact its one of the more original RPG fighting mechanics i've seen in a while, Your enemy throws a bullet hell attack at you and instead of just staring at a text screen (It's super effective!) your character (represented by a heart) would dodge creative bullet hell attacks that are thrown at you and some attacks have a clever way of dispatching them and require some thinking on the player's part. I love bullet hell games because it keeps you on edge and it punishes you for not being prepared to take massive amounts of damage, each and every bullet hell segement in this game requires quick reaction time and no carelessness is tolerated from the player to dodge it.
The mercy mechanic (technically this isn't a spoiler because the game openly proclaims you don't have to kill ANYTHING) Is something I loved using becasue it split up the button mashing gameplay of generic RPGs and instead had you observe what a character did when you executed an action, then after doing a combination of these actions you could simply resolve the conflict you had by not hurting anyhing and you would work out combinations of speech and gyrating of hips to dispatch each enemy (although there are some segments where you have to damage things until a certain point and then you can spare them, or you just have to wait out a boss and dodge all of the bosses' attacks until the fight ended and that would be mercying a boss)
Some people don't like this game because "It doesn't have skill trees, it tries way too hard to be dark" A: skill trees? SKILL TREES??? Can you take off your Mother 3 tinted glasses of for one damn second and look who developed this?? THIS is an indie title with a VERY small development team and Mother 3 was developed by HAL Laboratory and Brownie Brown BOTH co-develop for Nintendo, an industry GIANT, if you hold up the game to unrealistic expectations then you are expecting too much from a small development team and a ten dollar game (or £ 6.99 if you live elsewhere). B: Where in Sam hill did you get the impression that this game was dark, it's not and it doesn't try to be. I assume you get that from a genocide playthrough of the game in which case it is just you that thinks it is trying to be dark, the characters in the game just think you are a horrible person.
But besides the combat which is pretty stellar, the story is top notch, if you don't have a good sense of humour, cannot be immersed in the plot and feel for the characters in the game, treat your character as an extension of yourself and reflect on the choices you made in the game then... you won't like it.
Sadly some critics (with tighter sphincters than an 8-follow-through knot) cannot experience what most do experience in this game because they simply do not allow themselves' to get immersed and relax and actually have fun with the game and take the critiqueing glasses off for a second "Well that would be the games fault for not adapting to my tight bumhole and giving me a emotional experience" Yes, but if you buy into the game's plot you will have the time of your life, and if you don't, you'll just be part of the minority.
This game on my first playthrough was not the ending I wanted, I killed things I immensely regret killing, I didn't pick up items I wanted to because I completely missed them.
The second playthrough was the ending I wanted, not killing anything and everyone being happy in the end because I feel remorse for killing fictional characters, aren't I mentally sound?
And the last playthrough was killing everything and I was a bit dissapointed, not because the game never lets you become the bad guy, far from it, but there was little difference between pacifist playthroughs and genocide playthroughs, one might make the game harder for you and one may make the game a breeze for you.
In conclusion, this game is no doubt a masterpiece, Toby Fox put a lot of effort into this game and it really shows.
TL;DR Section
The gameplay is great.
The story is fantastic (but is probably too good for the game)
The soundtrack that accompanies most of the game is fantastic and I recommend that you buy that along with the game but probably don't listen to it until you've completed it once
Overall 9.5/10

This is one of the reasons I despise playthroughs of this game because people can just watch the story unfold FOR FREE ("wow tell me what is new, lets players have been spoiling stories since their conception" Yea but Toby Fox deserves every single dime for the story he wrote plus indie developers don't make nearly as much money as big publishers do unless you're talking about Markus Perrson).
Actually i'm going to condradict myself and say that this game has one big flaw, the story outshines the gameplay.
And that's not to say the gameplay is bad at all in fact its one of the more original RPG fighting mechanics i've seen in a while, Your enemy throws a bullet hell attack at you and instead of just staring at a text screen (It's super effective!) your character (represented by a heart) would dodge creative bullet hell attacks that are thrown at you and some attacks have a clever way of dispatching them and require some thinking on the player's part. I love bullet hell games because it keeps you on edge and it punishes you for not being prepared to take massive amounts of damage, each and every bullet hell segement in this game requires quick reaction time and no carelessness is tolerated from the player to dodge it.
The mercy mechanic (technically this isn't a spoiler because the game openly proclaims you don't have to kill ANYTHING) Is something I loved using becasue it split up the button mashing gameplay of generic RPGs and instead had you observe what a character did when you executed an action, then after doing a combination of these actions you could simply resolve the conflict you had by not hurting anyhing and you would work out combinations of speech and gyrating of hips to dispatch each enemy (although there are some segments where you have to damage things until a certain point and then you can spare them, or you just have to wait out a boss and dodge all of the bosses' attacks until the fight ended and that would be mercying a boss)
Some people don't like this game because "It doesn't have skill trees, it tries way too hard to be dark" A: skill trees? SKILL TREES??? Can you take off your Mother 3 tinted glasses of for one damn second and look who developed this?? THIS is an indie title with a VERY small development team and Mother 3 was developed by HAL Laboratory and Brownie Brown BOTH co-develop for Nintendo, an industry GIANT, if you hold up the game to unrealistic expectations then you are expecting too much from a small development team and a ten dollar game (or £ 6.99 if you live elsewhere). B: Where in Sam hill did you get the impression that this game was dark, it's not and it doesn't try to be. I assume you get that from a genocide playthrough of the game in which case it is just you that thinks it is trying to be dark, the characters in the game just think you are a horrible person.
But besides the combat which is pretty stellar, the story is top notch, if you don't have a good sense of humour, cannot be immersed in the plot and feel for the characters in the game, treat your character as an extension of yourself and reflect on the choices you made in the game then... you won't like it.
Sadly some critics (with tighter sphincters than an 8-follow-through knot) cannot experience what most do experience in this game because they simply do not allow themselves' to get immersed and relax and actually have fun with the game and take the critiqueing glasses off for a second "Well that would be the games fault for not adapting to my tight bumhole and giving me a emotional experience" Yes, but if you buy into the game's plot you will have the time of your life, and if you don't, you'll just be part of the minority.
This game on my first playthrough was not the ending I wanted, I killed things I immensely regret killing, I didn't pick up items I wanted to because I completely missed them.
The second playthrough was the ending I wanted, not killing anything and everyone being happy in the end because I feel remorse for killing fictional characters, aren't I mentally sound?
And the last playthrough was killing everything and I was a bit dissapointed, not because the game never lets you become the bad guy, far from it, but there was little difference between pacifist playthroughs and genocide playthroughs, one might make the game harder for you and one may make the game a breeze for you.
In conclusion, this game is no doubt a masterpiece, Toby Fox put a lot of effort into this game and it really shows.

Surviving amongst the other players can easily be the hardest part of the game as most players will shoot you in the head without thinking twice.  If they do think twice, it will be to degrade you, then kill you.  My best advice, don't get attached to ANYTHING in the game.  You will die, and you will lose whatever it is.  For new players, join a server with 0 people on it and experiment with the game first before you go in on a full server (as I said, you will die many, many, many times with other players around).
Pros:
- Great survivor gameplay.  Bandages for bleeding problems, thirst, hunger, energy, etc.
- Finding a group of friendly players can be hours of the most fun gameplay I have participated in.
- Graphics are "ok" (more in cons though)
Cons:
- Game is horribly not optimized yet.  People with Titan(s) still have trouble on highest settings when they walk into town.  Keep graphics set low if you don't have a super machine!
- Community is somewhat "evil".  They will kill you many times.
In all, I would definitely recommend getting this game in alpha while the price is lower than when/if it goes full release.

The survival genre on PC is one of the most exciting fields when it comes to gameplay innovation imo. The most important survival game in the last couple of years is probably the online innovator Rust. I had to stop playing Rust, because it was a massive time sink and the psychological stress level was too high, but I can't deny that the idea behind the game is brilliant and innovative.
The paranoia when you try to hide your base from other people, the fear when you are discovered, and the attachment you start to feel to your protective walls are some of the strongest emotions I have ever experienced in a game. The lack of a protected despawn state or a protected inventory made the game so intense ... I can really understand all those Russian kids who seem to spend their youth griefing people in Rust and Ark. Other genres can't compete with the emotional attachment and the thrill level that online survival can deliver.

I vote "Yes" on this game as it stands in ALPHA.  If this were advertised as a finished game I would easily vote "NO!".
This game is great for killing a few hours if you're in the mood for a survival game with no point (story, background, etc.)  You simply have to survive amidst the zombies (which honestly are annoying and a little over powered in my opinion), elements, and other survivors.  Surviving amongst the other players can easily be the hardest part of the game as most players will shoot you in the head without thinking twice.  If they do think twice, it will be to degrade you, then kill you.  My best advice, don't get attached to ANYTHING in the game.  You will die, and you will lose whatever it is.  For new players, join a server with 0 people on it and experiment with the game first before you go in on a full server (as I said, you will die many, many, many times with other players around).
Pros:
- Great survivor gameplay.  Bandages for bleeding problems, thirst, hunger, energy, etc.
- Finding a group of friendly players can be hours of the most fun gameplay I have participated in.
- Graphics are "ok" (more in cons though)
Cons:
- Game is horribly not optimized yet.  People with Titan(s) still have trouble on highest settings when they walk into town.  Keep graphics set low if you don't have a super machine!
- Community is somewhat "evil".  They will kill you many times.
In all, I would definitely recommend getting this game in alpha while the price is lower than when/if it goes full release.

Heres the thing, if you've put endless hours into the Day Z mod then your perception on this game might be a tad sour. It's understandable to feel that way. While this game is heading in a good direction, there are some core features that are present in the mod and are absent with in the Day Z SA. There is still some good to be said about this game.
What Day Z really has going for it is the fact that it is easily one of the more featured, polished survival simulation games out there. The team at Bohemia has been working on this game for quite some time now and the early access has come far since it was first released. Chernarus (I think that's miss spelled) is a huge map, probably the largest out of any the survival games out right now. It can sometime take an hour or more to travel from on end to the other and thats if you don't have to make too many stops. learning all the mechanics in the game can be daunting at first, but take the time to learn the ropes and you start to see the depth. Starting farms, creating camps, being a knowledgeable medic and a myraid of other features really make you feel like you are surviving. But for me Day Z really shines with its intense PvP. Day Z is a game of patience with a bit of thinking on your feet. This is one of those games where you can truley be a sniper, range finders and binoculars are a must, and knowing the lay of the land with raise your chances of survival exponetially. The stories that you'll have after playing for a while will be memorable for sure.
Most of the negative things to say about this game are father minor, but still affect the game as a whole. It was built using a buggy engine to begin with, so the bugs are there. Zomibes can be difficult to deal with when they all of the sudden show up in the house through a wall. Falling from 8 stories of a building because you were on the patio and somehow slide through the rails has happend more time than I wish to remember. And since this is a permadeth game dying really, REALLY sucks. Especially if you've spent an hour finding your friends and they are far from any spawn point.
There have been issues with hackers but honestly I've really not had an issue with that.
The ugly of this game really affects Day Z vets as opposed to some who is just coming into the game with the stand alone. LLike I mentioned earlier, if you have been playing Day Z since mod there are some core features missing, mainly vehicles and to some extent base building. While base building wasn't in the vanillia mod, many other versions provided that feature, and this was before SA was available. They have started to make progress with vehicles, but its been such a long time to get to this point that many have given up on SA. Especially with other games in the genre now offering these types of mechanics, it's almost as if SA will have to start playing catch up.
I do feel its taken Bohemia way too long to get to this point, and even then the game is still not where it should be. With other solid games coming out (most notably H1Z1) I worry that Day Z will be left behind before its real potential shines.
If your new to Day Z and just getting into the genre then you can't do much better than Day Z. If your a vet, well then you find a few holes that are hard to fill.

If you don't know already, Undertale is a popular game and honestly, I believe that it deserves the recogition it has. This is a game where you should definitely go in blind with no expectation of what's going to happen. This isn't just one of those games that you just play once and forget, it's an experience.
But reviews are supposed to be informative, right? So anyways...
Undertale is a pretty popular game that has been shown in Youtube videos and appeared in social media, but I digress. The game is a nice mix between turn-based JRPGs and bullet hell games. There are multiple ways to play this game, and your choices actually matter in this game, and because of this, the game has some good replay value to it.
The gameplay itself is pretty simple to understand. You traverse an overworld (or underworld, I should say) with different areas, each having a different theme. Along the way, you'll meet a bunch of different characters and encounter a bunch of different enemies, as well as obtaining new items by finding them or buying them and there are also a bunch of puzzles to solves (which aren't that hard unless you're bad at solving puzzles).
The combat system isn't just choosing moves and staring at animations, which is always nice. To fight, you have to line up your attack to deal the most amount of damage you can do possible or try acting in different ways to make the enemy not want to absolutely destroy you. In between your turns, there are bullet hell sections that vary from enemy to enemy, and the game occassionally throws in twists so that the bullet dodging system won't get stale.
This game also has it's own charm. The graphics have a nice retro look to it, the music is well made and memorable, the game's dialogue is filled with humor that made me chuckle (though humor is subjective), and all the characters are actually unique and likable. Not only that, Undertale pokes fun at RPG tropes that you would usually find in other games, and the game tends to break the fourth wall from time to time.
If you like secrets, then you won't be disappointed. There are a bunch of secret areas you can discover, secret enemies you can fight, conversations to have with NPCs, and more...
Personally, I don't have many complaints about this game. The game isn't buggy, it runs just fine, and it just plays well. In my opinion, this game is worth $10, and most of the work done here is made by one man, so take that into consideration. If I convinced you to get this, then have a good time. Besides, I'm not the only guy to say good things about this game.

TL;DR AT THE BOTTOM. (BUT HEY, READ AT LEAST THE FIRST PARAGRAPH. ESPECIALLY IF YOU'RE SOMEONE LIKE ME.)
P.S. No spoilers in this review (duh) I did put in little references, but they have no relation with the plot whatsoever.
Just finished playing through the pacifist route. Wait, before I go there, let me preface this with something very important.
If you're someone like me who tends to check the reviews of a game before buying it, TAKE MY WORD FOR THIS ONE. Undertale is, and will always be a game that I will remember fondly. Shoot, I might as well play it through a couple of times in my next years or so. Best 10 dollars I've ever spent on a video game, hands down.
Do I recommend this game?
HELL YEAH, I DO! (tl;dr for the paragraph above :P
Sure, the graphics (kinda..?) turned me off for this game, but as I saw more and more YouTubers play through this game, they began to grow on me. For example, the protagonist, whose name I will NOT be providing :3   , and his 'I don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥ just let me spare/kill you' face that he wears for (pretty much) the ENTIRE game, began as a slight nuisance. However, as my experience with this game proceeded, the little -.- look the protagonist wears started to become funnier and funnier. You'll see why if you play through the game. Same philosophy goes for the terrain, enemies, and basically everything else. (NOT INCLUDING (most) BOSSES!!) Sure, it starts off kinda basic, but you'll see that changes QUICKLY. You'll find yourself impressed with how well pixelated graphics go with this game, I kid you not.
Mechanics. Oh lord, I could write an essay that would get me college credit here. Pokemon, you're probably thinking. The words 'grind city' ring in your head like a bunch of lousy chimes. Warframe, anyone??? :3 Anyways, Undertale is definitely NOT a grind game, which makes it even better. Battles are unlike anything I've experienced in a turn-based game before. In addition, wild encounters are so rare, I've actually been happy to run in to an enemy. Also, if you've spent at least 5 minutes researching this game, you'd know that you can actually DODGE damage, as opposed to just sitting there and watching your HP whittle away to 0 (but it refused :3   . Even if you do get close to dying, you can just heal up and keep truckin'. So, before I get in to boss battles, random encounters and the damage system is definitely a plus. No grind = two thumbs up. OK, now on to boss battles. A ton of fun. Sure, you might rage out if you're that type of guy (I don't mind, I just like to hear the music again :P     ). However, boss battles, while they do provide some type of challenge, really aren't all that hard. Take it from me. There's this boss battle that everyone's been freaking out about, but I did it in my first try. No joke. I surprised even myself. I'm not that stereotypical Asian gamer that can one shot everything and walk away with full HP. But that's besides the point. Long story short, boss battles are fun and adrenaline-filled. Mechanics: definitely a plus.
Audio. EVERYONE'S been talking about the audio of this game. I swear, I found myself listening to YouTube videos of songs from the Undertale soundtrack WEEKS before I got this game. Even when you're walking by yourself in the wilderness, the background music makes this wander MUCH less boring. Hell, it probably makes it better, if I say so myself. And don't even get me started on battle music. Yeah, when you run into an enemy, the music is there, and it's kinda cool, but wait until you get to some of these boss fights. I can't tell you how many times I've bounced in my chair to the beat of the boss fight music that plays. (I recommend Bonetrousle, Spider Dance, Metal Crusher, and Death by Glamour.) Audio is definitely a plus. If you have headphones, WEAR THEM. (trust me)
So, to conclude, I definitely recommend this game to anyone that might be reading this review. Toby Fox's Undertale is definitely a quality game that deserves the respect it's been getting. From little jokes and awkward/funny situations to adrenaline-filled boss battles with bangin' soundtracks, from making enemies that actually become friends, and vice versa(..?) to pondering the inspiration behind the creation of OHMYGODWHATISTHATTHINGONMYSCREEN ( comma / , anyone?). Regardless, like I've said before, this is a very good game. Top notch. Hope you'll appreciate it as much as I did/will.
Anyways, I'm off to marinate in my feels for a little before thinking if Genocide is a good idea. Good luck, and remember:
Snowmen taste good.

About a week later, Undertale was EVERYWHERE, to the point where I was sick of it. It seemed like I couldn't get on the internet without seeing some character within five minutes. I tired of it. I was ready to never touch Undertale before I had even put it on my computer. I thought it was FNaF all over again. An overhyped game that wasn't worth the reception it was getting.
If you are thinking the same while reading this review, do not make the same mistake. Buy this game.
Between a branching, choice based storyline, a colorful cast of fun and memorable characters, fun controls (that I got to remap onto an SNES controller) and a good storyline, this game has a lot to offer. I found myself enjoying a whole story and cast of characters a lot more with Undertale than I have in a long time in a video game. Maybe a little too long.
Do yourself a favor and buy this.

By the end of the game you don't know what to expect, because this isn't a standard rpg like it seems at first. It understands that the player is, in fact, a player, and uses that fact so well by changing the rules and and doing things that only a video game could possibly do. I can't really say much more without spoiling it, but once you get past the boring combat and get further into the game, you start to appreciate it more and more.
tl;dr Play the game once all the way through to understand why there's so much hype about it. It's more about how the game uses the fact that its a game to its advantage, rather than just following the same old boring jrpg rules that most retro games do these days.

Let me just start off by saying that although I may not recommend this game in it's current state, it may improve in the future (albeit the FAR future, from what's happened so far in terms of development) and become something actually worth purchasing. The devs would have to be the first problem in mind , considering their lead dev left the studio a year in to development and essentially ran off with the money to make his own studio, leaving Bohemia to deal with the rest. I really can't blame Bohemia for this ♥♥♥♥ up, this is their first go at making a zombie game. If anyone is really to blame for the state it's currently in, it'd probably be Dean, since he left the very project he created to go make indie games or something of the like. And this is AFTER the huge success that was DayZ Mod, he realized the market for it, and pursued it with Standalone. I don't know what went on at Everest (To those who don't know, Dean climbed Mt. Everest and shortly after declared he was leaving the project) , but he must've fallen off a cliff to think that leaving the project after he set such lofty goals for it is OK. Not only that, but some of the other DayZ mods devs that stuck around with Hall left afterwards, probably after realizing this game would never be made.
These lofty goals that were set can actually be viewed on their own website
, and one can see that the things mentioned for Q1 (soon to be the end of Q2) AREN'T EVEN DONE YET. The only things actually done are the 'Basic Vehicles' (or vehicle, rather), Loot Distribution (so entire towns won't be completely void of all loot, just mostly), Horticulture (At least that's done) and Zombie AI (Which is still, at best, whether or not Zombie Usain Bolt will zigzag or straight up pursue you until the end of days). Sure, this is a 'light' roadmap, and is generally a baseline, not exact. But if they can't even complete these light goals they've made for themselves, what will become of the bigger things they've offered from when this game was first thought up (Underground bases, anyone?) ? i am let down time and time again after seeing DayZ update in steam, then seeing that it is yet another dissapointing update. And considering that it takes well over a month to push updates that actually do anything, the hopes for completing anything in Q2 are slim. Half-Life 3 could very well be released before this does, honestly.
I won't say anything about the community, it isn't really the game's fault, as it is essentially up to the player entirely. And to those who think that I haven't played nearly enought to develop such an opinion, well, it's your opinion and you're entitled to it, and I won't argue that. But know that I've played the Mod for some 180 hours, and can certainly determine that in comparison, this game is still severely lacking. "But they're making a new engine and it needs time" sure, it takes time, but they've had somewhere around 2 years to work on it and aren't even close to finishing it. You'd think that within that time frame a respectable company like Bohemia could handle such a feat, right? No, since the devs that had the vision for this game abandoned it too, leaving Bohemia to clean up and do their best.
Like I said, I could never recommend this game in it's current state, nor agree with it's 35$ price tag, but there is potential in it. Like the mod, it could even grow successful and end up not complete♥♥♥♥♥♥like it is now.
Edit: A year Later...
Under the pretense of massive engine imporovements and additional content, I decided to try the .60 update. Within moments, I'm incapable of joining any server, and after several relaunches and even a reinstall, nothing. After a full year, I'd at least somewhat expect the same problems that plagued Arma's sever browser to be rid of. At least now I don't have to worry until the next update.
I REALLY REALLLLY want this game to do well, as a fan of Bohemia and the original Mod, but yet again I am left dissappointed. I can tell in the changelog itself all these amazing and new additions to the aging Mil-sim's engine. A new renderer, UI update, a Central Loot Economy, all sounds excellent and a massive improvement upon what I experienced a year ago, but, in the end, even these massive improvements have yet to fix one of the fundamental flaws of the Arma Engine.

This is a very good game with a very good story.  Enter Undertale with an open mind and without any preconceptions about it, and you'll discover how many preconceptions you have about games in general.
Please don't let the hype sway you.  Go in without expecting much.  You might be surprised.  Play it now.  It's short.
What, you're still reading this?  Fine, but don't let my hype inflate your expectations too much.
Undertale's crowning achievement, something that it does better than any other game I've experienced, is that it has complete and total integration of player intention, gameplay, and story.  You may have heard the phrase "ludonarrative dissonance", where the actions you take in a game can conflict with the narrative without affecting it.  Undertale does not have this.  Frankly, the ways that Undertale avoids it (it even accounts for player ignorance!) are inventive and serve to make the story more interesting and engaging.
If you want to experience an engaging narrative that only a video game could provide, this is your game.  I'm not talking about games like Mass Effect or the Witcher series, which are all fantastic games and stories but could be told equivalently well as books or in a TV series.  Undertale could not be told as anything but a video game.
The only real criticism (minus a few gripes like Alphys's texts) I have of Undertale is that other games have made us so jaded and given us so many preconceptions of how games work it is possible to play Undertale once, put it down, and never experience the real meat of the narrative.  But if that does happen to you, maybe Undertale isn't the game for you.

To borrow from Fallout: New Vegas, this game is "not for the faint of heart or the serious of temperament". Those who've played Borderlands will know what to expect. For those who haven't, this game is not your typical shooter. Think of it as a cross between any of your generic action-shooter and a high-on-drugs version of Quake. You're either going to be fast to adapt to the crazy situations you'll be in or fast to fall to the psychos.

It's silly, it's frenetic, it's "OH MY GOD GET OVER HERE AND REZ ME GODDAMNIT RIGHT NOW"
It's best with friends, but fun on it's own -- which is vital for any game.
It's a bit crass.
It's ultimately 'just another shooter', but the great visuals and fun characters make it well worth your time.
It's got a lot of DLC + additional content, say what you will about it's cost, but it's well done and fun content to play.
It's got lovely replay value with new-game-plus modes and plenty of different classes to try.
Ultimately, Strong accept on merits. Go buy it.

I like this game. A lot.
There is a huge amount of hype for this game. Usually when that is the case it's not very good, but for me this game exceeded all expectations. It's of course best played knowing as little as possible.
The game subverts every expectation you might have of it, and the amount of things you can do in this little rpg to trigger an event is astounding. The soundtrack is lovely, the game is absolutely oozing with creativity and style. This is exactly what I want in a game. The first ever steam review I did about 5 years ago called Dustforce my "wet dream game." While I've evolved past the crude expression, this is probably what I would want in a game.
Aside from being genuinely fun and original the game has an excellent story with several layers of helpings. The game might not have a huge team working behind it to crank excellent visuals, but the story is crafted to a pristine shine. Every character, minor or NPC has some sort of resolution, which I love. The amount of depth and foreshadowing in the story really pays off, I enjoyed my second playthrough much more than my first.
As for the gameplay, it is quite good. The dodging mechanics can be genuinely fun and challenging. With the presentation the way it is with wholly unique enemies and environments, the usual turn based rpg elements engaged rather than bored me. It's only because of the unique writing, excellent music, incredible cast of characters, and meta fiction nature that the gameplay is able to shine. It never gets boring because the creator doesn't allow it to get boring, every enemy has a new way to fight, and the bullet patterns change all the time. The sections of the game that focus on puzzle elements, while technically "easy" are quite fun, and welcome breaks to the narrative.
IF you like games like Jazzpunk, then you'll LOVE this. It's the best single player game I've played in many years. Well worth the money. I didn't even mention the amount of secrets, some of which are still being figured out. Play Undertale, with or without the hype (preferably without, and an open mind) and see if you like it.

Undertale is an interesting game.
The graphics are old school and the game overall gives a very old school SNES Earthbound type of feel. It's kind of a fun, even wacky games at times, with much deeper plot lines and arching themes.
The game has a rather interesting combat system that blends kind of an old school JRPG type (think earlier Final Fantasy) of feeling while blending in ways to keep the player involved. It is very creative and challenging.
I feel like some parts of the game just hope you can learn on your feet as you go. I'm still not sure how to not fight everyone, despite based on the ending I got, it must be possible. I'm not sure when inter-dimensional boxes showed up. I wasn't sure at the start how to equip weapons and armor and just had to figure it out.
The game is well wrote, and the pacing is a good mix of dialog, events, and puzzles. None of the puzzles are too difficult, the hardest probably took about 5 min to solve, and most are solvable very quickly.
The game will toy with your emotions. You will laugh, you will be stressed, you will think, you will answer trivia questions, and you will grapple with your choices, maybe. Or maybe you'll do what I did and just kill everyone and then the game just ♥♥♥♥s with you on the ending.
Overall a play through only took ~5hours.  If you have enough determination, you can easily finish it.
Overall game is good, even has some replay value, but feels like it lacks some polish.
I think it's worth the price of admission, but don't expect to be crazy blown away.  3/5

I'll admit it- I googled, a lot, while playing undertale. There were several areas that I didn't want to spend anymore time on if the solution just wasn't going to happen. Note to new players- no combination of mushrooms will open the door. Just sayin'. ;)
I was intrigued and enjoyed the simple puzzle solving, but it wasn't until I made a decision, reloaded my game, made a different decision, and was called out on it from the next character I saw, that I realized I was dealing with something truly special. Undertale takes the time to develop a world that is a genuine delight to discover. Once I realized a True Pacifist path was possible, fights became all about getting to know the enemies. Seeing the differences in the game, however subtle (note the patrons in Grillsby, as an example) between the different routes was just plain fun. The world changes around you based on your choices, giving you some amount of control in the ending. Being rewarded for going all the way back to the beginning, and exploring all the out of the way places in the end was also a pleasure. It's like a fun thank you from the developers, and makes in enjoyable to keep exploring the same places over again.
The detail, the story, the general gameplay- all A+. Playing off a save power was brilliant, and allowing the choice to be made, over and over, with truly different outcomes makes this not only a game that is well worth the initial hours invested, but will be fantastic on replays to see what other tidbits are waiting.

Today i returned to DayZ after a 1½ year break. The experience back then was somewhat endurable but still painful and i convinced myself that it will only get better in the future... how wrong and naive i was.
In the year 2012 when DayZ mod came out, while it was clunky and very bad in many ways,  it managed to be fresh and very memorable, so all its flaws could be easily forgiven, after all - it was a MOD created by a single man.
DayZ standalone on the other hand is the complete opposite of the mod.  Developed and produced by a bigger company with more people and resources than the original mod.
I literally saw 0 progress after 1½ years of "development", unless you count pink Deringers, hockey sticks and bunch of other useless crap as progress. Instead of going forward like you would expect from an early access game, it has been in the same buggy and broken state all this time, perhaps you could even say that the game has gone backwards.
I could add your typical pros/cons- list but why bother? There are so many bad things about this game that the non-existing pros could not tip the scale.
Overall i feel very disappointed because DayZ seriously had alot of potential but i just cant see it to be possible for DayZ to be complete and functioning. I have no doubts that the developers just took the early access money and ran for the hills, abandoning the game.
I paid full price for the game when it came out and honestly, i dont really regret that. For me DayZ mod gave me hundreds of hours of fun and new friends, so i consider the standalone money to be a payment for Dean Hall, not for anyone else.
