Undertale is an RPG with just the right amount of charm to make it stand out amongst other RPGs, it feels like it has a lot of inspiration from the Earthbound series, which isn't a bad thing.
I originally bought undertale thinking It might end up being just another RPG that would get put on my backlog because I couldn't be bothered to finish it, but no as soon as I started my twelve hour play through, Determined to go full pacifist, simply because it was different from the usual mash attack for every battle and heal when low seemed oddly charming.  Almost immediately I found myself getting pulled in with its quirky humor and lovable characters.
I found myself getting lost into the story and wanting to know more about all of the characters in this world, it was an amazing trip from start to end and I can't recommend this game enough to anyone looking for a RPG to play, but is sick of the typical grind.
This game bursts from the seams with character and the music is absolutely fantastic all the way through the game is sending a really powerful message and as much as I want to play ever last detail, after getting the true ending...I literally cannot bring myself to go back through the game and do a genocide play through...It would hurt to kill all the characters that grew on me.
So if you find yourself looking at undertale and wondering if its worth the buy, I would say hands down yes, this game is something else, its been years since a single player game has drawn me in and made me play it from start to end in one full sitting.
* Edit *  I have now gone through a Genocide route and I gotta say, both routes are throughly enjoyable, each reveals different sides of the story.  A nice way to get replay value out of your game.

While my this specific account would say otherwise, I've been playing this game for almost 2 years now on and off. Heres how I've felt about it:
Rust started off as a real basic survival game with zombies and stiff & ugly animations. I understood that it was a super early access at this point, and I still had fun for what it was. Every time I keep checking back after several months away, the game looks even more beautiful and complex than the last time I played it. Its cheap, and you'll probably have a lot of fun once you start to strive off the land. You also get to look at a game thats attempted to be a different from other survival games. They aren't quite there yet, but more and more its getting there. The only knock though is that once you start to really make it in the game, it sort of gets boring and loses its replay value. You're fully stocked on materials, got all the weapons, have a dope house, tons of food & water. Its cool to get to this point, but once you're there the game loses its fun after awhile. Even after server wipes or getting your house blown up into while you're offline you're basically just set to start the process all over again, which is where I stop playing for awhile. It's a lot of grinding to get to that point (which they've said they want to fix). I'm curious to see how they step away from this problem of basically getting super-rich in the game and just running out of♥♥♥♥♥♥to do afterwards.
TL;DR, I enjoy myself everytime I fire up this game again. It's also fun to see where this game goes during its development. It's just once after 2 years I keep running into the problem getting super "rich" and not having anything to do afterwards.

Undertale is an RPG with just the right amount of charm to make it stand out amongst other RPGs, it feels like it has a lot of inspiration from the Earthbound series, which isn't a bad thing.
I originally bought undertale thinking It might end up being just another RPG that would get put on my backlog because I couldn't be bothered to finish it, but no as soon as I started my twelve hour play through, Determined to go full pacifist, simply because it was different from the usual mash attack for every battle and heal when low seemed oddly charming.  Almost immediately I found myself getting pulled in with its quirky humor and lovable characters.
I found myself getting lost into the story and wanting to know more about all of the characters in this world, it was an amazing trip from start to end and I can't recommend this game enough to anyone looking for a RPG to play, but is sick of the typical grind.
This game bursts from the seams with character and the music is absolutely fantastic all the way through the game is sending a really powerful message and as much as I want to play ever last detail, after getting the true ending...I literally cannot bring myself to go back through the game and do a genocide play through...It would hurt to kill all the characters that grew on me.
So if you find yourself looking at undertale and wondering if its worth the buy, I would say hands down yes, this game is something else, its been years since a single player game has drawn me in and made me play it from start to end in one full sitting.
* Edit *  I have now gone through a Genocide route and I gotta say, both routes are throughly enjoyable, each reveals different sides of the story.  A nice way to get replay value out of your game.

This amazing pancake  recipe:
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I don't think this game is worth buying. I admit, the story can be interesting and the humor is hilarious, but I'd recommend you to simply check the game Youtube. The gameplay has the interesting feature that you can "spare" enemies - Interesting idea, but horrible execution. To spare an enemy, you have to fulfill requirements, that can either be randomly pressing the options listed in the "act"-menu or tasks that no regular player would come up with. For example, you can spare the first boss, if you randomly press the "spare"-button a few times. Like, seriously? The game teaches you you have to use the "act"-menu, which is just simply not true. So you decide to kill the enemies - In which you have a classical turn-based RPG that gets boring after 10 minutes of playing. Also, you run in danger to enter the so called "genocide"-route...A route where every boss is one-hit beside of two, which are just hilariously strong and take several days of pattern memorization to beat. Yeah. That's the gameplay from my point of view.

For THAT price tag, I met two of the greatest (and funniest) characters in gaming. You know who they are. Sans and Papyrus. When I tried to play Genocide (but then f*cked up at the third boss), I legit nearly teared up when I had to kill Papyrus. I was HEARTBROKEN. And Sans... he talks.. in COMIC SANS. As Papyrus talks in, well, Papyrus. Nonetheless, this is the most funny (and interesting) game of last year; if you haven't give it a shot, DO IT. I rate Papyrus/Spaghetti.

This game is just great. Although it looks graphically simple, it's the attention to detail in the storytelling and the soundtrack that really makes the game stand out. Each boss fight is unique and fun, and the fact that "you dont have to destroy anyone" makes the game incredibly choice driven.
The fighting aspect of the game is fairly standard. You gain EXP and LV, and you can find different weapons around that each have unique ways of timing your hits. If, however, you decide to spare a monster, the game becomes more like a puzzle, trying to figure out exactly what each monster wants from you.
Both ways of ending a battle involve short, simple "bullet-hell" like sections wherein you have to dodge the attacks of the opponents. If you encounter more than one monster at a time, their attacks combine. This makes each battle feel somewhat unique.

Undertale is a rather refreshing experience in terms of RPG games. There's a lot of mechanics from your usual RPGs that have been reworked to make this game something special. Now, in my opinion it isn't necessarily as great as the internet puts it out to be but it is pretty damn close and more than worth the asking price. The combat system plays out in a way that is typical for games in the genre, but what makes Undertale's combat so unique is that aside from killing whatever crosses your path you can also talk it out or divert the combatants attention. The combat alone can drastically affect how your game changes, primarily depending on whether or not you decide to befriend everyone or simply burn the whole damn world to pieces.
Building off of that, the game takes a very unique direction in terms of its player consequence. What makes Undertale unique is that, along with the way certain characters break the fourth wall, they may also (not directly) remember things you have done in previous playthroughs or reloads. Let's say you killed a certain character and then reloaded your save for whatever reason. That character may or may not act differently the second time around. This mechanic alone made me want to play through the game multiple times to see what kinds of endings I could achieve and what general mischief could be caused. The fate of the world the game takes place in is entirely in your hands.
Let's break it down:
Positives:
Interesting characters
Amazing/hilarious dialogue
Great soundtrack (and I mean GREAT!)
Refreshing take on RPG combat
Consequences to player actions
Unique boss battles
Deep backstory
Negatives:
Some parts may seem a bit slow (depends on the person)
Certain enemy encounters can be infuriating
My personal rating for Undertale is 9/10. Though it isn't perfect, it is on the right track.

Now, before you continue reading, just know that I have played for at least 500 hours on the ArmA 2 mod, so my review isn't one that came from someone who played a few hours and decided it was bad.
Let's take a look at DayZ.
DayZ is a zombie-bandit survival game which originally came to be a mod for ArmA 2. In this, you're a survivor meant to scavenge and defend yourself against the nasties of the Russian environment.
The pros and cons of this game will be listed below, but beware, the cons outnumber the pros:
-Great to play with some friends, especially on RP servers.
-Incredibly detailed world, real-time survival which is pretty fun.
-Crafting and exploring a big terrain.
-Challenging in all the right ways.

-Still in Early-Access since December 2013.
-VERY buggy. Don't expect to jump in without error.
-Even a brilliant system can still be laggy with this. Hello 40fps in Cherno.
-Russians and other people who can't speak English playing on English servers therefore ruining the game for others...
-HACKERS HACKERS HACKERS
-Running up stairs breaks your legs
-Spawning under a building if you log out in one and having to kill yourself...(sometimes)
-Wringing clothes and keeping them dry does NOT work. Trust me.
-Not even a zombie game anymore. The 20 hours I've played on the standalone, I've seen 3 zombies. Yes, 3. No more.
-Griefers... yeah, you can't trust anyone. The community is bad now.
Now, I'm not saying it's a BAD game per se. The mod is freaking brilliant. Easily the best survival game I've played. The standalone is really good too, but of course, it's still in Alpha and will be for at least another year at this rate...
If you see it on sale or for cheap, grab it. If not, just find a cheap copy of ArmA 2 (easy to find, I got the complete thing for $5 on disc) and download the DayZ MOD.
6/10

WARNING: THIS REVIEW CONTAINS SOME MINOR SPOILERS
It's difficult to write a review for a game like this, since there are so many ways it can be played and viewed. Should a player go for a neutral run, they may end up feeling disatisfied with the ending they get. If they go for a genocide run, they will most likely get annoyed at the game for the difficulty spikes for certain boss fights. And if they go for the True Pacifist run, they'll end up seeing the perfect ending, but will be less motivated to play it again, because of the events at the end.
Either way, this game is one of the most unique, funny, and genuinely amazing games I've played in a long time, and I feel like there's gonna be a long period of time where I won't be able to forget it.

Aside from the heart warming story (if you want it to be that is), hilarious characters and brilliant RPG style, this game has one of the best soundtracks I have heard from a game :D All in all I absolutely loved it! And yes this game did fill me with determination...

Personal Tip : Use your own Name when you choose a name for your character. I think you will find it a worthwhile decision.  I personally found the game even more rewarding, because the characters I met used my name. This decision especially bore meaningful fruit during the end game.
Undertale is one of those rare, shooting stars of an experience that, if you stick with it, and are well disposed to its genre, unique personality, and cultural sensibilities, will have an experience that will leave a permanent change chiseled onto your heart.
I haven't reached the ending yet, but the path I took in the game has led to such a powerful positive deonuement , so moving, so honest, so touching of the deep feelings I believe are fundamental to everyone, that I found myself openly crying with gratitude.
Toby Fox is abundantly aware that his core themes are constantly explored in Anime; he isn't shy about making regular references to the great story telling medium that is Anime and the motifs consistently explored in the most popular of them.
Themes like :
1. Staying true to your beliefs
2. Never giving up, no matter how bleak things look
3. The power of friendship (which almost always manifests itself as a physical power to save one's friends)
4. Accepting people for who they are, no matter how weird they see themselves as being, no matter if they think they're losers
5. An often off the wall, truly wacky sense of humor (which the game has in spades, hoes, and shovels!)
6. When you believe in yourself, and have earned the belief of others, you can save the world
7. When others need you, you tap into a power that you never knew you had
Some people might see the game as "derivative" and "unoriginal" since, again, its themes are readily found in most popular Anime, but I would say that the game is done with so much love and belief in the themes of Anime, that those themes are given a new and unique life in the world of Undertale. The game is not simply imitating these timeless themes, it is weaving them into a special shape that touches people in another way...a good way...a lasting way.
Need I say it, but Toby Fox is the quintessential model of the Renaissance Man. At 23, he has accomplished something revolutionary in the gaming genre.
1. Programming : The game is bug free as far as I can tell during my 15 hours. Admittedly, the game does not have the complexity of a Triple A title, but for 1 guy to create a game with the many moving parts Undertale has, and for the game to run so smoothly is a feat, so I think.
2. Combat / Dynamic Evasion System : The "Combat" mechanic in the game is wholly unique in my experience with RPG's. Combining "Bullet-Hell" gameplay with "Turn-Based" combat was a stroke of genius! It really works! And the Bullet-Hell scenarios are unique and surprising for each "enemy" you encounter. I would even venture to say that the way each "enemy" attacks you is a Story-Telling device unto itself, actually, I think I will say that they are absolutely part of the Story-Telling mechanics of the game. Fighters will tell you that one learns a great deal about a person through engaging them in combat. Toby Fox has created a "combat"...y'know... let's call it an "engagement" system that is Fun! and adds to the Story-Telling a great, great deal.
Now, taken individually, all these elements could be considered laudatory, but hardly revolutionary; however, when all these elements are combined into one game, by one person!...well, that is a revelation!
But, it is the path of non-violence and choosing instead to understand others, which makes this game truly revolutionary.
The music in the game is just stellar. I purchased the soundtrack. If you liked the game, you will definitely like the soundtrack. ;)
When I listen to "Hopes and Dreams" and "SAVE The World!" I feel a tremendous desire to do all those things : be filled with Hope! fulfill my Dreams and help fulfill the Dreams of others! and ultimately save the World!
I can feel that moment those songs play in the game and the faith of the friends you have made in the game flowing through yourself. It's moving stuff. It's eternal stuff.
And the main theme of the game, the referentially titled "Undertale" is such a beautiful song. So whimsical, and just lovely. A story about a young boy or girl who falls into a hole and enters another world where they experience a powerful adventure, and are given the choice to choose how they will meet life : as an aggressor or embracer... A thoughtful piece of music. It stays with you.
- Note : I will keep working on this review when I have some more free time. If you've read until now : thanks a lot! It really is a special, special game. : ) -

Do I recommend this game....? Hmm... Let me think... Only a million, billion, trillion, quadrillion, quintillion...obbedy-gillion times! I'm not even done the game yet and I'm nearly 15 hours in! This game...this game...it's a watershed moment in gaming, in popular culture...even...dare I be so portentous...human evolution.
I don't have the words to describe my thoughts on this game to the width and breadth I would be satisfied with at the moment, but, suffice it to say...I think that whatever happens in the rest of my life...I will always be able to find a little space inside myself that is : Filled With " DETERMINATION ! Undertale is a rather refreshing experience in terms of RPG games. There's a lot of mechanics from your usual RPGs that have been reworked to make this game something special. Now, in my opinion it isn't necessarily as great as the internet puts it out to be but it is pretty damn close and more than worth the asking price. The combat system plays out in a way that is typical for games in the genre, but what makes Undertale's combat so unique is that aside from killing whatever crosses your path you can also talk it out or divert the combatants attention. The combat alone can drastically affect how your game changes, primarily depending on whether or not you decide to befriend everyone or simply burn the whole damn world to pieces.
Building off of that, the game takes a very unique direction in terms of its player consequence. What makes Undertale unique is that, along with the way certain characters break the fourth wall, they may also (not directly) remember things you have done in previous playthroughs or reloads. Let's say you killed a certain character and then reloaded your save for whatever reason. That character may or may not act differently the second time around. This mechanic alone made me want to play through the game multiple times to see what kinds of endings I could achieve and what general mischief could be caused. The fate of the world the game takes place in is entirely in your hands.
Let's break it down:
Positives:
Interesting characters
Amazing/hilarious dialogue
Great soundtrack (and I mean GREAT!)
Refreshing take on RPG combat
Consequences to player actions
Unique boss battles
Deep backstory
Negatives:
Some parts may seem a bit slow (depends on the person)
Certain enemy encounters can be infuriating
My personal rating for Undertale is 9/10. Though it isn't perfect, it is on the right track.

The game was going through a rough patch for quite some time, but it appears as though it's starting to return to what I played for so many hours before.  Given the size of the development team, they could be hashing out more updates, but they are too busy going to every gaming con there is.  I wish that it was someone else developing it, but other than that, it is definitely an experience.

You either like it or you don't, but you could say that about pretty much anything. So I'm going to explain why:
If you play games to see your character grow and develop with new equipment and skills. Then you might get frustrated with this game, because you can spend 10 hours gathering decent equipment only to get picked off by a sniper from 300 metres away. In most other games, dying will set you back anywhere from 5 seconds to half an hour which is more of a nuisance than anything. But in Dayz, death means the end. Everything you've worked for will be lost and picked up by some guy who shot you.
This makes Dayz one of the most tense games I've ever played, you could die at any moment from any direction with no warning. It forces you to be alert at all times whilst also having to focus on getting food, water, fighting disease and of course.... Zombies.
I can understand how that description may turn you away from the game, and that's fine. You're opinion is no less vaild than mine or anyone else's. But if that makes the game sound appealing to you... then I'd strongly recommend you buy it or at least look into the game further.
I have to also add that the game is in early access alpha, so the game is still very buggy and you will not likely get a solid 60fps framerate no matter how good your PC specs are. Research the state of the game currently and know that you are buying an unfinished game and understand the implications of that. Features will be missing, bugs will happen (and might kill your character) and your character will almost certainly be a victim to hacking at some point. If you can look past that (Like I, and many others do) then you could have lots of fun with dayz.

DayZ is in Alpha. It is a given that there are flaws and you will encounter these flaws. Undoubtedly, you are going to get frustrated and quit the game after you die from falling down a few steps of stairs.
I bought this game believing that it is a good investment for the future. A game I can enjoy later as it progresses and I enjoy it now. I'll go ahead and state my thoughts at this point. Top tens that I can think of off the top of my head.
Pros of Alpha DayZ Standalone:
1) The spawn points are almost always on the shoreline near a big city (if you run enough).
2) The basics of the game are pretty straight forward and rather easy to use.
3) Environments are pretty for a game that costs $30.
4) Realistic bullet drop.
5) The Zombie AI is in the developing stage, and presents a legitimate threat if you are not prepared.
6) Fear. This game gets your heart pumping in certain zombie encounters. Don't want to die from a horde of zombies that you alerted by speaking in-game? Run like ♥♥♥♥. Don't try punching your way out of a crowd or you're going to become food for the infected.
7) Status bars. Not drinking enough? Sick? Are you starving to death? They game will tell you through first person by monologue.
8) Medicine and transferable diseases!
9) "I'm freezing." Build a damn fire, and fast.
10) Emotes! You can make your character do different actions with their arms as well as sit, lay down and roll around in the grass.
Cons of Alpha DayZ Standalone:
1) There is no tutorials to understand how the game works.
2) If you have friends, don't plan on finding them right away.
3) Text abilities are limited.
4) It is rather easy to lose your way using the in-game map fragments. If you don't want to find theses fragments, I suggest using
for the map.
5) The UI can be confusing for new players at first.
6) Zombies can bug through house walls.
7) Public servers crash or restart at random points. (They usually warn you before restarts.)
8) Finding food right off the bat can be difficult and starving to death can come quickly if you are constantly running around.
9) Weapons? Good luck finding the matching ammo.
10) Trucks! It is easy to desync from the server if your ping is high. If your ping is high, you're going to glitch all over the place when driving a truck and you may cause the death of yourself, or your friends.
As said before, the game is in Alpha and if you plan on buying it, it's more of an investment for the future of your entertainment, not instant all-fun right now. Help the developers out by submitting bug reports!

There is very little I can say about this game without spoiling it, This game is so rich with story that if i mention that name of the main character i will have ruined the entire game for you. I will have to try to talk about the game itself instead of the story.
as you'd expect there are several endings in the game which sucks because you have to play the game several times to see all of the content. Anyways:
the neutral route
This is most likely what you will get the first time playing assuming you haven't looked up the ending like you should.
It has a good story and it is obvious that the gameplay was balanced around this route and the good ending route. Other than that there is not much you can say about this route as there are so many ways to play it that i can't be completely accurate in describing what you will experience
"The good route"
I don't think I am spoiling anything by saying there is a good ending, but I will say that, if you beat the neutral ending, the good ending will be very easy. In fact, if you go this route the game gives stuff to you and it's almost impossible to lose. It works because of how you get this route and it keeps an appropriate tone. There is a satisfying ending to this as well
"The bad route"
The bad route has a constant negative tone in the entire thing which is definetely a bit wierd because there are plenty of elements from the good ending that still show up despite that. also the difficulty curve is awful in this mode. At first it starts okay than it curves down until one of the boss fights where it spikes up very high. After that, the gameplay gets easier than it was at the start of the game until you meet the final boss which has the highest spike in difficulty I have ever seen. I guess it's kind of appropriate considering the story of the bad route but I'd feel that it is way too steep for difficulty that only spikes higher during the fight.
Overall:
You could complete the game in 3-8 hours depending on how good you are at games like these and with a great soundtrack, likable characters, and enjoyable (but by no means perfect) gameplay. It is definetely worth playing.

I remember when I saw the hype train of Undertale following it's release. All these images in my newsfeeds which seemed amusing, but not enough to pursue in depth. It seemed like the sort of 2nd degree point of internet culture that I'd never bother to search for. In the early days, I saw enough of a variety of positive reviews that it seemed to strike me as a decent game, but one which I still didn't have the time or interest for.
And then the hype had the inevitable retaliation, just as all bandwagons do. Associated with the crap of tumblr, a game which was promoted for hype rather than being better than other games on any really objective measures. I grew suspicious of it, and eventually grew to ignore it because I leant towards the opinion of disliking overrated games. The hype kept with me though; I had friends play the soundtrack to me when we met up, and I saw cynical Youtubers like Yahtzee Crowshaw or Facebook pages like NYJWFP singing it's praise. And so I relented and bought the game.
I was just amazed. After the first boss I faced, I realised that either it was an exceptional game, or I just haven't played enough others. Since then I've seen reviews praising other games like Fly Me To the Moon and Lisa, and I think I'll have to get around to playing them for a more comprehensive opinion, but honestly? I don't think that takes away from just how great this game is. That something as simple as this in art and music style kept me up at night...that was what struck me the most about it. I left the game for a while after I made a mistake, but then eventually came back and binged the rest of my first playthrough overnight weeks after. I'm writing this now because I need to vent about the game; like an incredibly touching film, it has affected me such that I need to reflect upon the endings that I've seen, and what I'll take from it into life. Pretentious statement, eh?
To the cynics or the apathetic, consider that popular culture isn't always a terrible thing just for being popular. Yes, there will always be crowds of people who don't enjoy whatever aspect of the game, and yet I think that's a moot point. You are reading reviews if you see this, and then you need to have played the game to be able to understand the opinions, one way or the other.
Whether you think I'm shilling it or not, I think everyone should play this. It costs less than a movie ticket, and it'll change your perspective.

I rarely write reviews, especially negative reviews, but given the amount of positive reviews and hype surrounding this game, I feel compelled to throw my two cents in.  Are the glowing reviews and hype a massive joke to unsuspecting gamers?  Is this game the proverbial snipe hunt?  Because this game is terrible.  The graphics and music, meant to hearken back to days of yore (I can call them that, I gamed during those days!) are not charming at all but completely throw-away.  Gameplay is terrible (for me, the character constantly and inexplicably would jerk back to the left side of the screen) with tired mechanics that were retired ages ago.  The enemy interaction is unique, I'll give it that, but the bullet-hell "combat" gets old VERY fast (again, I had the issue of the heart jerking back to the left side of the screen, just as I did walking around with the character, which made dodging impossible.)  If there's a story here, I didn't encounter it in the almost hour I played this thing, and it is undeserving of any more of my time.  Out of my 60+ Steam games, this is my first ever refund request.  Do yourself a favor, don't fall for the hype!
